q001.stem:
A data engineer is working with two tables. Each of these tables is displayed below in its entirety.

sales

customer_id  spend   units
a1           28.94   7
a3           874.12  23
a4           8.99    1

favorite_stores

customer_id  store_id
a1           s1
a2           s1
a4           s2

The data engineer runs the following query to join these tables together:

SELECT sales.customer_id, sales.spend, favorite_stores.store_id
FROM sales
LEFT JOIN favorite_stores
ON sales.customer_id = favorite_stores.customer_id;

Which of the following will be returned by the above query?
options:
customer_id      spend     store_id
a1         28.94    s1
a4         8.99    s2

customer_id    spend store_id
a1           28.94    s1
a2           NULL      s1
a4          8.99    s2

customer_id     spend       store_id
a1          28.94     s1
a3          874.12 NULL
a4          8.99     s2

customer_id     spend   store_id
a1            28.94   s1
a2            NULL     s1
a3            874.12 NULL
a4            8.99   s2

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    customer_id     spend       store_id
a1          28.94     s1
a3          874.12 NULL
a4          8.99     s2

Why it is correct: a LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table (sales). a1 and a4 match; a3 has no match in favorite_stores, so its store_id is NULL. Row a2 exists only in the right table and is not returned.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: that is an INNER JOIN result: it would drop a3, which must appear with NULL.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it includes a2 (only in the right table) and omits a3 (from the left); that is not a LEFT JOIN from sales.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: that is a FULL OUTER JOIN: it adds a2, which is not in sales.

q002.stem: Which of the following benefits is provided by the array functions from Spark SQL?
options: An ability to work with data in a variety of types at once
An ability to work with data within certain partitions and windows
An ability to work with time-related data in specified intervals
An ability to work with complex, nested data ingested from JSON files

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: An ability to work with complex, nested data ingested from JSON files

Why it is correct: array functions (explode, filter, transform, array_contains…) let you manipulate nested structures, typical of JSON, without flattening them first.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — An ability to work with data in a variety of types at once — Why it is incorrect: an array holds elements of one type; it is not for mixing types.
  • Option B — An ability to work with data within certain partitions and windows — Why it is incorrect: that describes window functions (OVER (PARTITION BY …)), not array functions.
  • Option C — An ability to work with time-related data in specified intervals — Why it is incorrect: working with time intervals is the job of date/time functions and time windows.

q003.stem: Which of the following is hosted completely in the control plane of the classic Databricks architecture?
options: Worker node
JDBC data source
Databricks web application
Databricks Filesystem
Driver node

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Databricks web application

Why it is correct: in the classic architecture the web application, management services and metadata live in the Databricks control plane. Clusters (driver and workers) and data live in the customer cloud account (data plane).

  • Official documentation: Databricks architecture (control and data planes) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Worker node — Why it is incorrect: workers run in the customer cloud account (data plane).
  • Option B — JDBC data source — Why it is incorrect: it is an external customer data source; it does not belong to the control plane.
  • Option D — Databricks Filesystem — Why it is incorrect: DBFS is backed by storage in the customer account (data plane).
  • Option E — Driver node — Why it is incorrect: the driver also runs in the data plane, in the customer account.

q004.stem: Which of the following benefits of using the Databricks Lakehouse Platform is provided by Delta Lake?
options: The ability to manipulate the same data using a variety of languages
The ability to collaborate in real time on a single notebook
The ability to set up alerts for query failures
The ability to support batch and streaming workloads
The ability to distribute complex data operations

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: The ability to support batch and streaming workloads

Why it is correct: Delta Lake is a transactional (ACID) storage layer that serves batch and streaming reads and writes on the same table.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The ability to manipulate the same data using a variety of languages — Why it is incorrect: multi-language support (SQL, Python, Scala, R) comes from notebooks/Spark, not from Delta Lake.
  • Option B — The ability to collaborate in real time on a single notebook — Why it is incorrect: real-time collaboration is a workspace notebook feature.
  • Option C — The ability to set up alerts for query failures — Why it is incorrect: alerts are provided by Databricks SQL / Jobs, not by Delta Lake.
  • Option E — The ability to distribute complex data operations — Why it is incorrect: distributing compute is done by Apache Spark.

q005.stem: Which of the following describes the storage organization of a Delta table?
options: Delta tables are stored in a single file that contains data, history, metadata, and other attributes.
Delta tables store their data in a single file and all metadata in a collection of files in a separate location.
Delta tables are stored in a collection of files that contain data, history, metadata, and other attributes.
Delta tables are stored in a collection of files that contain only the data stored within the table.
Delta tables are stored in a single file that contains only the data stored within the table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Delta tables are stored in a collection of files that contain data, history, metadata, and other attributes.

Why it is correct: a Delta table is a directory of Parquet data files plus the _delta_log transaction log (JSON and checkpoints) holding metadata and history. Together they form a collection of files.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Delta tables are stored in a single file that contains data, history, metadata, and other attributes. — Why it is incorrect: it is not a single file.
  • Option B — Delta tables store their data in a single file and all metadata in a collection of files in a separate location. — Why it is incorrect: data is not in a single file nor is metadata kept elsewhere: both live in the table directory.
  • Option D — Delta tables are stored in a collection of files that contain only the data stored within the table. — Why it is incorrect: besides data, the _delta_log stores metadata and history.
  • Option E — Delta tables are stored in a single file that contains only the data stored within the table. — Why it is incorrect: it is neither a single file nor data-only.

q006.stem: Which of the following code blocks will remove the rows where the value in column age is greater than 25 from the existing Delta table my_table and save the updated table?
options: SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE age > 25;
UPDATE my_table WHERE age > 25;
DELETE FROM my_table WHERE age > 25;
UPDATE my_table WHERE age <= 25;
DELETE FROM my_table WHERE age <= 25;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: DELETE FROM my_table WHERE age > 25;

Why it is correct: DELETE FROM … WHERE age > 25 removes exactly the rows meeting the condition and commits the change to the Delta table.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE age > 25; — Why it is incorrect: SELECT only reads; it does not modify the table.
  • Option B — UPDATE my_table WHERE age > 25; — Why it is incorrect: UPDATE needs SET and changes values; it does not delete rows.
  • Option D — UPDATE my_table WHERE age <= 25; — Why it is incorrect: UPDATE without SET is invalid and deletes nothing.
  • Option E — DELETE FROM my_table WHERE age <= 25; — Why it is incorrect: it would delete rows with age ≤ 25, the opposite ones.

q007.stem: Which tool is used by Auto Loader to process data incrementally?
options: Checkpointing
Spark Structured Streaming
Databricks SQL
Unity Catalog

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Spark Structured Streaming

Why it is correct: Auto Loader (cloudFiles) is a Structured Streaming source: it discovers new files and processes the increment with the Spark streaming engine.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Checkpointing — Why it is incorrect: a checkpoint only records progress; it is not the engine processing data.
  • Option C — Databricks SQL — Why it is incorrect: Databricks SQL is the SQL query service, not the Auto Loader engine.
  • Option D — Unity Catalog — Why it is incorrect: Unity Catalog handles governance and permissions; it does not process files.

q008.stem: Which of the following commands will return the number of null values in the member_id column?
options: SELECT count(member_id) FROM my_table;
SELECT count(member_id) - count_null(member_id) FROM my_table;
SELECT count_if(member_id IS NULL) FROM my_table;
SELECT null(member_id) FROM my_table;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: SELECT count_if(member_id IS NULL) FROM my_table;

Why it is correct: count_if(member_id IS NULL) counts the rows where the condition is true, i.e. the nulls.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SELECT count(member_id) FROM my_table; — Why it is incorrect: count(col) counts NON-null values.
  • Option B — SELECT count(member_id) - count_null(member_id) FROM my_table; — Why it is incorrect: count_null does not exist in Spark SQL.
  • Option D — SELECT null(member_id) FROM my_table; — Why it is incorrect: null() is not a valid aggregate for this.

q009.stem: Which of the following data lakehouse features results in improved data quality over a traditional data lake?
options: A data lakehouse provides storage solutions for structured and unstructured data.
A data lakehouse supports ACID-compliant transactions.
A data lakehouse allows the use of SQL queries to examine data.
A data lakehouse stores data in open formats.
A data lakehouse enables machine learning and artificial Intelligence workloads.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A data lakehouse supports ACID-compliant transactions.

Why it is correct: ACID transactions (Delta Lake) prevent partial writes, isolate concurrent reads and writes and guarantee consistency, which a plain file-based data lake does not provide.

  • Official documentation: What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks | Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A data lakehouse provides storage solutions for structured and unstructured data. — Why it is incorrect: that is a flexibility benefit, not a quality one.
  • Option C — A data lakehouse allows the use of SQL queries to examine data. — Why it is incorrect: using SQL does not improve data quality.
  • Option D — A data lakehouse stores data in open formats. — Why it is incorrect: open formats avoid vendor lock-in; they do not improve quality.
  • Option E — A data lakehouse enables machine learning and artificial Intelligence workloads. — Why it is incorrect: it enables use cases, not quality.

q010.stem:
A data engineer wants to create a relational object by pulling data from two tables. The relational object does not need to be used by other data engineers in other sessions. In order to save on storage costs, the data engineer wants to avoid copying and storing physical data.

Which of the following relational objects should the data engineer create?
options: Spark SQL Table
View
Delta Table
Temporary view

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Temporary view

Why it is correct: a temporary view stores no data (only the query) and lives only in the session, exactly what is asked.

⚠️ Heads-up: option B (a regular view) also avoids copying data; the question favors the temporary view because it is only needed in the current session. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Views - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Spark SQL Table — Why it is incorrect: a table physically stores data.
  • Option B — View — Why it is incorrect: a regular view also avoids copying data, but it is stored in the catalog and visible to other sessions; since sharing is not needed, the temporary view is the best fit.
  • Option C — Delta Table — Why it is incorrect: a Delta table physically stores data.

q011.stem: A Unity Catalog table owner has left the company and no longer has access. The table is not in the workspace's default workspace catalog. No remaining team member owns the table's parent schema/catalog or has the MANAGE privilege on the table. Who among the following can transfer ownership of the table to the new lead data engineer using Catalog Explorer?
options: Databricks account representative
Nobody: ownership cannot be transferred
Unity Catalog metastore administrator
The new lead data engineer, solely because of their role
The former owner, despite having no account access

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Unity Catalog metastore administrator

Why it is correct: a metastore admin can manage and transfer ownership of any object in the metastore. The other routes (schema/catalog owner, MANAGE) are excluded by the scenario.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks account representative — Why it is incorrect: Databricks does not manage customers' data permissions.
  • Option B — Nobody: ownership cannot be transferred — Why it is incorrect: ownership can be transferred.
  • Option D — The new lead data engineer, solely because of their role — Why it is incorrect: being the engineering lead does not by itself grant privileges on the object.
  • Option E — The former owner, despite having no account access — Why it is incorrect: without account access they cannot act.

q012.stem:
A data analyst has created a Delta table sales that is used by the entire data analysis team. They want help from the data engineering team to implement a series of tests to ensure the data is clean. However, the data engineering team uses Python for its tests rather than SQL.

Which of the following commands could the data engineering team use to access sales in PySpark?
options: SELECT * FROM sales
There is no way to share data between PySpark and SQL.
spark.sql("sales")
spark.delta.table("sales")
spark.table("sales")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: spark.table("sales")

Why it is correct: spark.table("sales") loads the registered table as a PySpark DataFrame.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SELECT * FROM sales — Why it is incorrect: that is SQL, not PySpark code.
  • Option B — There is no way to share data between PySpark and SQL. — Why it is incorrect: false: metastore tables are accessible from both SQL and PySpark.
  • Option C — spark.sql("sales") — Why it is incorrect: spark.sql expects a full SQL statement, not just a table name.
  • Option D — spark.delta.table("sales") — Why it is incorrect: spark.delta.table does not exist (the API is DeltaTable.forName).

q013.stem: In a Unity Catalog-enabled Databricks workspace, the schema main.customer360 has a managed storage location. Which SQL statement shows extended schema metadata, including its location?
options: DESCRIBE LOCATION main.customer360;
DROP SCHEMA main.customer360;
DESCRIBE SCHEMA EXTENDED main.customer360;
ALTER SCHEMA main.customer360 SET DBPROPERTIES ('location' = '/user');
USE SCHEMA main.customer360;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: DESCRIBE SCHEMA EXTENDED main.customer360;

Why it is correct: DESCRIBE SCHEMA EXTENDED returns the schema name, comment, location, owner and properties.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DESCRIBE LOCATION main.customer360; — Why it is incorrect: DESCRIBE LOCATION is not a valid schema statement.
  • Option B — DROP SCHEMA main.customer360; — Why it is incorrect: DROP SCHEMA deletes the schema.
  • Option D — ALTER SCHEMA main.customer360 SET DBPROPERTIES ('location' = '/user'); — Why it is incorrect: ALTER SCHEMA … SET DBPROPERTIES changes properties; it does not display them.
  • Option E — USE SCHEMA main.customer360; — Why it is incorrect: USE SCHEMA only switches the active schema.

q014.stem:
A data engineer wants to create a new table containing the names of customers that live in France. They have written the following command:

CREATE TABLE customersInFrance
  _____
AS
SELECT id, firstName, lastName
FROM customerLocations
WHERE country = 'FRANCE';

A senior data engineer mentions that it is organization policy to include a table property indicating that the new table includes personally identifiable information (PII). Which of the following lines of code fills in the above blank to successfully complete the task?
options: There is no way to indicate whether a table contains PII.
"COMMENT PII"
TBLPROPERTIES PII
COMMENT "Contains PII"
PII

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: COMMENT "Contains PII"

Why it is correct: COMMENT "Contains PII" adds a table comment in CREATE TABLE … AS; it is the syntactically valid way to document that it contains PII.

⚠️ Heads-up: the SQL in the question has a stray comma after lastName; that is a flaw in the original and does not change the answer. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks | Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — There is no way to indicate whether a table contains PII. — Why it is incorrect: it can: with COMMENT or TBLPROPERTIES.
  • Option B — "COMMENT PII" — Why it is incorrect: "COMMENT PII" in quotes is a string literal, not the COMMENT clause.
  • Option C — TBLPROPERTIES PII — Why it is incorrect: TBLPROPERTIES requires parenthesized key=value pairs; TBLPROPERTIES PII is invalid.
  • Option E — PII — Why it is incorrect: a bare PII is not a SQL clause.

q015.stem: What is stored in the Databricks customer's cloud account?
options: Databricks web application
Cluster management metadata
Notebooks
Data

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Data

Why it is correct: customer data stays in its own cloud account (data plane). The web app, metadata and notebooks live in the Databricks control plane.

  • Official documentation: Databricks architecture (control and data planes) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks web application — Why it is incorrect: the web app lives in the control plane.
  • Option B — Cluster management metadata — Why it is incorrect: cluster management metadata is in the control plane.
  • Option C — Notebooks — Why it is incorrect: notebooks are stored in the control plane (encrypted), not in the customer account.

q016.stem: Which of the following commands can be used to write data into a Delta table while avoiding the writing of duplicate records?
options: DROP
IGNORE
MERGE
APPEND
INSERT

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: MERGE

Why it is correct: MERGE INTO compares source and target with a condition and only inserts (or updates) rows that do not exist, avoiding duplicates.

  • Official documentation: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DROP — Why it is incorrect: DROP deletes objects; it does not write data.
  • Option B — IGNORE — Why it is incorrect: IGNORE is not a write command in Delta.
  • Option D — APPEND — Why it is incorrect: APPEND adds rows without checking duplicates.
  • Option E — INSERT — Why it is incorrect: INSERT adds rows without checking duplicates.

links.t: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE

q017.stem:
A data engineer is designing a data pipeline. The source system generates files in a shared directory that is also used by other processes. As a result the files should be kept as is and will accumulate in the directory. The data engineer needs to identify which files are new since the previous run in the pipeline, and set up the pipeline to only ingest those new files with each run.

Which of the following tools can the data engineer use to solve this problem?
options: Unity Catalog
Delta Lake
Databricks SQL
Auto Loader

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Auto Loader

Why it is correct: Auto Loader tracks which files it already processed (in the checkpoint) and ingests only new ones on each run, without moving or deleting the originals.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Unity Catalog — Why it is incorrect: it is data governance; it does not detect new files.
  • Option B — Delta Lake — Why it is incorrect: it is the table format; it does not discover new source files.
  • Option C — Databricks SQL — Why it is incorrect: it is the SQL query service; it does not handle incremental file ingestion.

q018.stem:
A data analyst has a series of queries in a SQL program. The data analyst wants this program to run every day. They only want the final query in the program to run on Sundays. They ask for help from the data engineering team to complete this task.

Which of the following approaches could be used by the data engineering team to complete this task?
options: They could submit a feature request with Databricks to add this functionality.

They could wrap the queries using PySpark and use Python's control flow system to determine when to run
the final
   query.
They could only run the entire program on Sundays.

They could automatically restrict access to the source table in the final query so that it is only accessible on
Sundays.
They could redesign the data model to separate the data used in the final query into a new table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    They could wrap the queries using PySpark and use Python's control flow system to determine when to run
the final
   query.

Why it is correct: using spark.sql(…) inside a Python if lets you run the final query only on a given weekday.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They could submit a feature request with Databricks to add this functionality. — Why it is incorrect: not needed: it is already doable with code.
  • Option C — They could only run the entire program on Sundays. — Why it is incorrect: it fails: the other queries must run daily.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: restricting permissions is not a scheduling mechanism and would break the query.
  • Option E — They could redesign the data model to separate the data used in the final query into a new table. — Why it is incorrect: redesigning the model does not control when the query runs.

q019.stem:
A data engineer runs a statement every day to copy the previous day's sales into the table transactions. Each day's sales are in their own file in the location "/transactions/raw".

Today, the data engineer runs the following command to complete this task:

COPY INTO transactions
FROM "/transactions/raw"
FILEFORMAT = PARQUET;

After running the command today, the data engineer notices that the number of records in table transactions has not changed. Which of the following describes why the statement might not have copied any new records into the table?
options: The format of the files to be copied were not included with the FORMAT_OPTIONS keyword.
The names of the files to be copied were not included with the FILES keyword.
The previous day's file has already been copied into the table.
The PARQUET file format does not support COPY INTO.
The COPY INTO statement requires the table to be refreshed to view the copied rows.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The previous day's file has already been copied into the table.

Why it is correct: COPY INTO is idempotent: it remembers already loaded files and skips them. If yesterday's file was already copied, no rows are added.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The format of the files to be copied were not included with the FORMAT_OPTIONS keyword. — Why it is incorrect: the format is already given by FILEFORMAT; FORMAT_OPTIONS is optional.
  • Option B — The names of the files to be copied were not included with the FILES keyword. — Why it is incorrect: FILES is optional; without it all new files are loaded.
  • Option D — The PARQUET file format does not support COPY INTO. — Why it is incorrect: Parquet is supported by COPY INTO.
  • Option E — The COPY INTO statement requires the table to be refreshed to view the copied rows. — Why it is incorrect: no refresh is needed to see the rows.

q020.stem: In which of the following scenarios should a data engineer use the MERGE INTO command instead of the INSERT INTO command?
options: When the location of the data needs to be changed
When the target table is an external table
When the source is not a Delta table
When the target table cannot contain duplicate records

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: When the target table cannot contain duplicate records

Why it is correct: MERGE INTO performs a keyed upsert and avoids duplicates; INSERT INTO only appends rows.

  • Official documentation: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — When the location of the data needs to be changed — Why it is incorrect: changing the location has nothing to do with MERGE.
  • Option B — When the target table is an external table — Why it is incorrect: both commands work with external tables.
  • Option C — When the source is not a Delta table — Why it is incorrect: both commands accept sources of any format.

links.t: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE

q021.stem: A notebook needs to read a supported transactional source through JDBC before writing to a Unity Catalog table. Which Spark DataFrame reader format is correct?
options: spark.read.format('jdbc').option('url', jdbc_url).option('dbtable', 'customer360').load()
spark.read.format('autoloader').option('url', jdbc_url).load()
spark.read.format('sqlite-stream').load(jdbc_url)
spark.read.format('unity-catalog-jdbc').load(jdbc_url)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: spark.read.format('jdbc').option('url', jdbc_url).option('dbtable', 'customer360').load()

Why it is correct: spark.read.format("jdbc") with url and dbtable is the standard Spark JDBC reader.

  • Official documentation: Query databases using JDBC - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — spark.read.format('autoloader').option('url', jdbc_url).load() — Why it is incorrect: autoloader is not a Spark format (it is cloudFiles) and does not read JDBC.
  • Option C — spark.read.format('sqlite-stream').load(jdbc_url) — Why it is incorrect: sqlite-stream does not exist.
  • Option D — spark.read.format('unity-catalog-jdbc').load(jdbc_url) — Why it is incorrect: unity-catalog-jdbc does not exist.

q022.stem:
A data engineer needs access to a table new_table, but they do not have the correct permissions. They can ask the table owner for permission, but they do not know who the table owner is.

Which of the following approaches can be used to identify the owner of new_table?
options: Review the Permissions tab in the table's page in Data Explorer
There is no way to identify the owner of the table
Review the Owner field in the table's page in Data Explorer
Review the Owner field in the table's page in the cloud storage solution

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Review the Owner field in the table's page in Data Explorer

Why it is correct: the table page in Data/Catalog Explorer shows the Owner field.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Review the Permissions tab in the table's page in Data Explorer — Why it is incorrect: the Permissions tab lists granted privileges; it does not identify the owner.
  • Option B — There is no way to identify the owner of the table — Why it is incorrect: it can be identified.
  • Option D — Review the Owner field in the table's page in the cloud storage solution — Why it is incorrect: cloud storage does not know the logical ownership of the catalog table.

q023.stem:
A data engineer is attempting to drop a Spark SQL table my_table. The data engineer wants to delete all table metadata and data.

They run the following command:

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS my_table

While the object no longer appears when they run SHOW TABLES, the data files still exist. Which of the following describes why the data files still exist and the metadata files were deleted?
options: The table's data was larger than 10 GB
The table's data was smaller than 10 GB
The table was external
The table did not have a location
The table was managed

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The table was external

Why it is correct: dropping an external table only removes its metastore definition; the files stay in place. A managed table loses its data too.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The table's data was larger than 10 GB — Why it is incorrect: size is irrelevant.
  • Option B — The table's data was smaller than 10 GB — Why it is incorrect: size is irrelevant.
  • Option D — The table did not have a location — Why it is incorrect: every table has a location.
  • Option E — The table was managed — Why it is incorrect: a managed table would be deleted along with its data.

q024.stem:
A data engineer wants to create a data entity from a couple of tables. The data entity must be used by other data engineers in other sessions. It also must be saved to a physical location.

Which of the following data entities should the data engineer create?
options: Database
Function
View
Temporary view
Table

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Table

Why it is correct: a table persists physical data and is visible from other sessions.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Database — Why it is incorrect: a database is a container, not an entity holding data.
  • Option B — Function — Why it is incorrect: a function stores no data.
  • Option C — View — Why it is incorrect: a view does not store data physically.
  • Option D — Temporary view — Why it is incorrect: it exists only in the session and stores no data.

q025.stem:
A data engineer is maintaining a data pipeline. Upon data ingestion, the data engineer notices that the source data is starting to have a lower level of quality. The data engineer would like to automate the process of monitoring the quality level.

Which of the following tools can the data engineer use to solve this problem?
options: Unity Catalog
Data Explorer
Delta Lake
Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables), mediante expectations
Auto Loader

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables), mediante expectations

Why it is correct: Lakeflow expectations let you define data-quality rules and automatically record compliance metrics on every run.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Unity Catalog — Why it is incorrect: governance and permissions; it does not monitor data quality.
  • Option B — Data Explorer — Why it is incorrect: it only browses the catalog.
  • Option C — Delta Lake — Why it is incorrect: it provides ACID and basic constraints, not automated quality monitoring.
  • Option E — Auto Loader — Why it is incorrect: it ingests files; it does not monitor quality.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q026.stem:
A data engineer has a Job that has a complex run schedule, and they want to transfer that schedule to other Jobs.

Rather than manually selecting each value in the scheduling form in Databricks, which of the following tools can the data engineer use to represent and submit the schedule programmatically?
options: pyspark.sql.types.DateType
datetime
pyspark.sql.types.TimestampType
Cron syntax

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Cron syntax

Why it is correct: a Job schedule is expressed as a cron (Quartz) expression, which can be copied and submitted via API or configuration.

  • Official documentation: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — pyspark.sql.types.DateType — Why it is incorrect: DateType is a date data type, not a scheduling format.
  • Option B — datetime — Why it is incorrect: datetime handles dates in Python; it does not describe recurring Job schedules.
  • Option C — pyspark.sql.types.TimestampType — Why it is incorrect: TimestampType is a data type, not a scheduler.

links.t: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers

q027.stem:
A data analyst has developed a query that runs against Delta table. They want help from the data engineering team to implement a series of tests to ensure the data returned by the query is clean. However, the data engineering team uses Python for its tests rather than SQL.

Which of the following operations could the data engineering team use to run the query and operate with the results in PySpark?
options: SELECT * FROM sales
spark.delta.table
spark.sql
spark.table

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: spark.sql

Why it is correct: spark.sql("…") runs a SQL query and returns a DataFrame to work with in PySpark.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SELECT * FROM sales — Why it is incorrect: it is plain SQL, not a PySpark operation.
  • Option B — spark.delta.table — Why it is incorrect: spark.delta.table does not exist.
  • Option D — spark.table — Why it is incorrect: spark.table loads a table by name; it does not run an arbitrary query.

q028.stem:
A data organization leader is upset about the data analysis team's reports being different from the data engineering team's reports. The leader believes the siloed nature of their organization's data engineering and data analysis architectures is to blame.

Which of the following describes how a data lakehouse could alleviate this issue?
options: Both teams would respond more quickly to ad-hoc requests
Both teams would use the same source of truth for their work
Both teams would reorganize to report to the same department
Both teams would be able to collaborate on projects in real-time

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Both teams would use the same source of truth for their work

Why it is correct: the lakehouse unifies data on a single platform, so engineering and analytics query the same source of truth.

  • Official documentation: What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Both teams would respond more quickly to ad-hoc requests — Why it is incorrect: it may happen, but it does not resolve discrepancies between reports.
  • Option C — Both teams would reorganize to report to the same department — Why it is incorrect: that is an organizational change, not an architecture feature.
  • Option D — Both teams would be able to collaborate on projects in real-time — Why it is incorrect: real-time collaboration does not fix differing source data.

q029.stem: Which Structured Streaming query is performing a hop from a Silver table to a Gold table?
options:
(spark.readStream.load(rawSalesLocation)
  .writeStream
  .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
  .outputMode("append")
  .table("newSales")
)

(spark.table("sales")
   .withColumn("avgPrice", col("sales") / col("units"))
   .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
   .outputMode("append")
   .table("newSales")
)

(spark.table("sales")
   .filter(col("units") > 0)
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("append")
    .table("newSales")
)

(spark.readStream.table("sales")
    .groupBy("store")
    .agg(sum("sales"))
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("complete")
    .table("newSales")
)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    (spark.readStream.table("sales")
    .groupBy("store")
    .agg(sum("sales"))
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("complete")
    .table("newSales")
)

Why it is correct: the Silver → Gold hop reads the Silver table as a stream (readStream.table) and computes a business aggregate (groupBy().agg()), which requires outputMode("complete").

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it reads raw data (rawSalesLocation) and writes it: that is Raw → Bronze.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it adds a derived column with a batch read (spark.table) and no aggregate: a cleaning/enrichment step (Bronze → Silver).
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it only filters rows with a batch read: Silver-style refinement, not a Gold aggregate.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q030.stem:
A data engineer has configured a Structured Streaming job to read from a table, manipulate the data, and then perform a streaming write into a new table. The code block used by the data engineer is below:

(spark.table("sales")
   .withColumn("avg_price", col("sales") / col("units"))
   .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
   .outputMode("complete")
   ._____
   .table("new_sales")
)

If the data engineer only wants the query to execute a micro-batch to process data every 5 seconds, which of the following lines of code should the data engineer use to fill in the blank?
options: trigger("5 seconds")
trigger()
trigger(once="5 seconds")
trigger(processingTime="5 seconds")
trigger(continuous="5 seconds")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: trigger(processingTime="5 seconds")

Why it is correct: trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") starts a micro-batch every 5 seconds.

  • Official documentation: Structured Streaming trigger intervals - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — trigger("5 seconds") — Why it is incorrect: trigger("5 seconds") is not a valid signature.
  • Option B — trigger() — Why it is incorrect: trigger() without arguments defines no interval.
  • Option C — trigger(once="5 seconds") — Why it is incorrect: once is a one-shot trigger and takes no interval.
  • Option E — trigger(continuous="5 seconds") — Why it is incorrect: continuous enables continuous mode (low latency), not micro-batches.

q031.stem:
A dataset has been defined using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) and includes an expectations clause:

CONSTRAINT valid_timestamp EXPECT (timestamp > '2020-01-01') ON VIOLATION DROP ROW

What is the expected behavior when a batch of data containing data that violates these constraints is processed?
options: Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and loaded into a quarantine table.

Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and flagged as invalid in a field added to
the
   target dataset.

Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event
log.
Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event log.
Records that violate the expectation cause the job to fail.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event
log.

Why it is correct: with ON VIOLATION DROP ROW invalid rows are dropped from the target and the metrics are recorded in the pipeline event log.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and loaded into a quarantine table. — Why it is incorrect: no quarantine table is created automatically.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: with DROP ROW they are not added; they are dropped.
  • Option D — Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event log. — Why it is incorrect: they are dropped, not added.
  • Option E — Records that violate the expectation cause the job to fail. — Why it is incorrect: failing the update is ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q032.stem: In Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, when should CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE be used instead of CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW?
options: Only when the next pipeline step is a static table.
When new records must be processed incrementally using streaming semantics.
It is redundant because all declarative datasets behave as ordinary views.
Only for complex full-batch aggregations over all historical records.
Only when the source table never changes.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: When new records must be processed incrementally using streaming semantics.

Why it is correct: a streaming table incrementally processes only new data (append semantics). A materialized view maintains the result of a full query.

  • Official documentation: Streaming tables - Databricks | Materialized views - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Only when the next pipeline step is a static table. — Why it is incorrect: the type of the next step does not decide the choice.
  • Option C — It is redundant because all declarative datasets behave as ordinary views. — Why it is incorrect: they are not redundant: they have different semantics.
  • Option D — Only for complex full-batch aggregations over all historical records. — Why it is incorrect: full-history aggregations fit materialized views better.
  • Option E — Only when the source table never changes. — Why it is incorrect: a static source is not what streaming tables are for; they suit growing sources.

q033.stem: A Lakeflow pipeline contains the following SQL: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE loyal_customers AS SELECT customer_id FROM STREAM(customers) WHERE loyalty_level = 'high'; Why is STREAM(customers) used?
options: The STREAM function is not needed and will cause an error.
The data in the customers table has been updated since its last run.
To read customers with streaming semantics and process new records incrementally.
The customers table is a reference to a Structured Streaming query on a PySpark DataFrame.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: To read customers with streaming semantics and process new records incrementally.

Why it is correct: STREAM() declares a streaming read of the source, so only new records are processed on each update.

  • Official documentation: Streaming tables - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The STREAM function is not needed and will cause an error. — Why it is incorrect: it is needed for an incremental read in a streaming table.
  • Option B — The data in the customers table has been updated since its last run. — Why it is incorrect: it is not an update flag.
  • Option D — The customers table is a reference to a Structured Streaming query on a PySpark DataFrame. — Why it is incorrect: customers need not be a streaming DataFrame; STREAM() is what enables the incremental read.

q034.stem: Working with Databricks Git folders (formerly Repos), which Git operation is typically performed in the external Git provider rather than as the main workspace action?
options: Commit
Pull
Merge
Clone

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Merge

Why it is correct: branch merge is typically done in the Git provider (for example when approving a pull request). Git folders cover commit, pull, push, clone and branch switching.

⚠️ Heads-up: Databricks Git folders do support merging branches; the question refers to the usual practice of doing it in the Git provider. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Commit — Why it is incorrect: commit is done from the workspace Git folder.
  • Option B — Pull — Why it is incorrect: pull is done from the workspace.
  • Option D — Clone — Why it is incorrect: clone is how you create the Git folder in the workspace.

q035.stem:
A data engineer has three tables in a Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) pipeline. They have configured the pipeline to drop invalid records at each table. They notice that some data is being dropped due to quality concerns at some point in the DLT pipeline. They would like to determine at which table in their pipeline the data is being dropped.

Which of the following approaches can the data engineer take to identify the table that is dropping the records?
options: They can set up separate expectations for each table when developing their DLT pipeline.
They cannot determine which table is dropping the records.
They can set up DLT to notify them via email when records are dropped.
They can navigate to the DLT pipeline page, click on each table, and view the data quality statistics.
They can navigate to the DLT pipeline page, click on the “Error” button, and review the present errors.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: They can navigate to the DLT pipeline page, click on each table, and view the data quality statistics.

Why it is correct: the pipeline page shows, for each table, data-quality statistics (records passing/failing expectations).

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can set up separate expectations for each table when developing their DLT pipeline. — Why it is incorrect: the expectations already exist on each table; what is missing is reading their metrics.
  • Option B — They cannot determine which table is dropping the records. — Why it is incorrect: it can be determined.
  • Option C — They can set up DLT to notify them via email when records are dropped. — Why it is incorrect: DLT does not send alerts per dropped record with that setting.
  • Option E — They can navigate to the DLT pipeline page, click on the “Error” button, and review the present errors. — Why it is incorrect: dropping rows is not a pipeline error.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q036.stem:
A data engineer has a single-task Job that runs each morning before they begin working. After identifying an upstream data issue, they need to set up another task to run a new notebook prior to the original task.

Which of the following approaches can the data engineer use to set up the new task?
options: They can clone the existing task in the existing Job and update it to run the new notebook.
They can create a new task in the existing Job and then add it as a dependency of the original task.

They can create a new task in the existing Job and then add the original task as a dependency of the new
task.
They can create a new job from scratch and add both tasks to run concurrently.
They can clone the existing task to a new Job and then edit it to run the new notebook.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: They can create a new task in the existing Job and then add it as a dependency of the original task.

Why it is correct: the new task must finish first: create it in the same Job and set it as a dependency (Depends on) of the original task.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can clone the existing task in the existing Job and update it to run the new notebook. — Why it is incorrect: cloning and replacing adds no prior step; it replaces the task.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it reverses the order: the new task would run after the original.
  • Option D — They can create a new job from scratch and add both tasks to run concurrently. — Why it is incorrect: running them concurrently does not guarantee order.
  • Option E — They can clone the existing task to a new Job and then edit it to run the new notebook. — Why it is incorrect: it creates another Job; it is not chained to the original task.

q037.stem:
A data engineering team has two tables. The first table march_transactions is a collection of all retail transactions in the month of March. The second table april_transactions is a collection of all retail transactions in the month of April. There are no duplicate records between the tables.

Which of the following commands should be run to create a new table all_transactions that contains all records from march_transactions and april_transactions without duplicate records?
options:
CREATE TABLE all_transactions AS SELECT * FROM march_transactions INNER JOIN SELECT * FROM
april_transactions;

CREATE TABLE all_transactions AS SELECT * FROM march_transactions UNION SELECT * FROM
april_transactions;

CREATE TABLE all_transactions AS SELECT * FROM march_transactions OUTER JOIN SELECT * FROM
april_transactions;

CREATE TABLE all_transactions AS SELECT * FROM march_transactions INTERSECT SELECT * from
april_transactions;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    CREATE TABLE all_transactions AS SELECT * FROM march_transactions UNION SELECT * FROM
april_transactions;

Why it is correct: UNION combines both query results and removes duplicates.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: INNER JOIN combines columns and keeps only matching rows; the syntax is also invalid.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: OUTER JOIN does not stack rows and the syntax is invalid.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: INTERSECT returns only common rows, of which there are none.

q038.stem:
A data engineer wants to schedule their Databricks SQL dashboard to refresh once per day, but they only want the associated SQL warehouse to be running when it is necessary.

Which of the following approaches can the data engineer use to minimize the total running time of the SQL warehouse used in the refresh schedule of their dashboard?
options: They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint matches each of the queries' SQL endpoints.
They can set up the dashboard's SQL endpoint to be serverless.
They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL warehouse.
They can reduce the cluster size of the SQL endpoint.
They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint is not one of the included query's SQL endpoint.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL warehouse.

Why it is correct: Auto Stop shuts the warehouse down after a period of inactivity, so it only runs during the scheduled refresh.

⚠️ Heads-up: option B (serverless) also reduces costs and startup time, but the official key is C (Auto Stop). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: SQL warehouses - Databricks | AI/BI dashboards - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint matches each of the queries' SQL endpoints. — Why it is incorrect: matching endpoints does not shorten running time.
  • Option B — They can set up the dashboard's SQL endpoint to be serverless. — Why it is incorrect: serverless starts quickly, but shutting the warehouse down after the refresh is what Auto Stop does.
  • Option D — They can reduce the cluster size of the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: a smaller size changes performance/cost, not when it shuts down.
  • Option E — They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint is not one of the included query's SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: it does not affect running time.

q039.stem: In which of the following scenarios should a data engineer select a Task in the Depends On field of a new Databricks Job Task?
options: When another task needs to be replaced by the new task
When another task needs to successfully complete before the new task begins
When another task has the same dependency libraries as the new task
When another task needs to use as little compute resources as possible

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: When another task needs to successfully complete before the new task begins

Why it is correct: Depends on defines execution order: the task does not start until the task it depends on has completed successfully.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — When another task needs to be replaced by the new task — Why it is incorrect: the field does not replace tasks.
  • Option C — When another task has the same dependency libraries as the new task — Why it is incorrect: libraries are configured separately.
  • Option D — When another task needs to use as little compute resources as possible — Why it is incorrect: it has nothing to do with compute resources.

q040.stem: Which of the following best describes a valid code source when configuring a Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline?
options: A mandatory key-value Spark configuration with no source code.
SQL or Python pipeline definitions supplied through supported source files or notebooks.
A manually selected DBFS root data directory is mandatory.
A Hive database target is mandatory even when using Unity Catalog.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: SQL or Python pipeline definitions supplied through supported source files or notebooks.

Why it is correct: a pipeline is defined with SQL or Python code in supported notebooks or source files.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A mandatory key-value Spark configuration with no source code. — Why it is incorrect: a pipeline needs code; a configuration alone does not define it.
  • Option C — A manually selected DBFS root data directory is mandatory. — Why it is incorrect: no manual DBFS directory is needed.
  • Option D — A Hive database target is mandatory even when using Unity Catalog. — Why it is incorrect: with Unity Catalog the target is catalog.schema, not Hive.

q041.stem:
A data engineer has a Job with multiple tasks that runs nightly. Each of the tasks runs slowly because the clusters take a long time to start.

Which of the following actions can the data engineer perform to improve the start up time for the clusters used for the Job?
options: They can use endpoints available in Databricks SQL
They can use jobs clusters instead of all-purpose clusters
They can configure the clusters to be single-node
They can use clusters that are from a cluster pool
They can configure the clusters to autoscale for larger data sizes

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: They can use clusters that are from a cluster pool

Why it is correct: a pool keeps pre-provisioned instances ready to assign, reducing cluster start-up time.

  • Official documentation: Pool configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can use endpoints available in Databricks SQL — Why it is incorrect: SQL endpoints are for queries, not for Job tasks.
  • Option B — They can use jobs clusters instead of all-purpose clusters — Why it is incorrect: job clusters cut cost, not start-up time.
  • Option C — They can configure the clusters to be single-node — Why it is incorrect: single-node does not speed up provisioning.
  • Option E — They can configure the clusters to autoscale for larger data sizes — Why it is incorrect: autoscaling affects performance on large data, not start-up.

q042.stem: A team must work with the objects of Unity Catalog schema main.customers. Which SQL GRANT statement best matches ALL PRIVILEGES on this schema (not schema ownership)?
options: GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE customers TO team;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE team TO customers;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.customers TO team;
GRANT OWNERSHIP ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team;

Why it is correct: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team grants all privileges applicable to the schema.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE customers TO team; — Why it is incorrect: USAGE ON DATABASE customers is not the right object and only grants usage.
  • Option B — GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE team TO customers; — Why it is incorrect: it swaps recipient and object (team as the database).
  • Option C — GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.customers TO team; — Why it is incorrect: it only grants SELECT on a table, not all privileges.
  • Option D — GRANT OWNERSHIP ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team; — Why it is incorrect: OWNERSHIP transfers ownership, not ALL PRIVILEGES.

q043.stem: An engineering group team already has USE CATALOG on main. Which grant lets members use schema main.customers in Unity Catalog?
options: GRANT VIEW ON CATALOG customers TO team;
GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE customers TO team;
GRANT USE CATALOG ON SCHEMA team TO customers;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE team TO customers;
GRANT USE SCHEMA ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: GRANT USE SCHEMA ON SCHEMA main.customers TO team;

Why it is correct: USE SCHEMA on the schema, together with USE CATALOG on the catalog, lets users access objects in the schema.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — GRANT VIEW ON CATALOG customers TO team; — Why it is incorrect: VIEW is not a valid catalog privilege here.
  • Option B — GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE customers TO team; — Why it is incorrect: CREATE ON DATABASE lets you create objects, not use the schema.
  • Option C — GRANT USE CATALOG ON SCHEMA team TO customers; — Why it is incorrect: USE CATALOG is not granted on a schema and the syntax swaps the names.
  • Option D — GRANT SELECT ON TABLE team TO customers; — Why it is incorrect: SELECT ON TABLE team treats the team as a table.

q044.stem: A data engineer is running code in a Databricks Repo that is cloned from a central Git repository. A colleague of the data engineer informs them that changes have been made and synced to the central Git repository. The data engineer now needs to sync their Databricks Repo to get the changes from the central Git repository. Which of the following Git operations does the data engineer need to run to accomplish this task?
options: Merge
Push
Pull
Commit
Clone

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Pull

Why it is correct: Pull brings remote changes into the local repo.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Merge — Why it is incorrect: it combines branches; it does not by itself fetch remote changes.
  • Option B — Push — Why it is incorrect: it sends local changes to the remote.
  • Option D — Commit — Why it is incorrect: it records local changes.
  • Option E — Clone — Why it is incorrect: it creates a new copy; it is already cloned.

q045.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of the Databricks Lakehouse Platform embracing open source technologies?
options: Cloud-specific integrations
Simplified governance
Ability to scale storage
Ability to scale workloads
Avoiding vendor lock-in

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Avoiding vendor lock-in

Why it is correct: open formats and projects (Delta, Spark, MLflow…) mean you are not tied to a single vendor.

  • Official documentation: What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Cloud-specific integrations — Why it is incorrect: openness does not imply cloud-specific integrations.
  • Option B — Simplified governance — Why it is incorrect: governance comes from Unity Catalog.
  • Option C — Ability to scale storage — Why it is incorrect: storage scaling comes from cloud storage.
  • Option D — Ability to scale workloads — Why it is incorrect: workload scaling comes from distributed compute.

q046.stem:
A data engineer only wants to execute the final block of a Python program if the Python variable day_of_week is equal to 1 and the Python variable review_period is True.

Which of the following control flow statements should the data engineer use to begin this conditionally executed code block?
options: if day_of_week = 1 and review_period:
if day_of_week = 1 and review_period == "True":
if day_of_week = 1 & review_period = "True":
if day_of_week == 1 and review_period:

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: if day_of_week == 1 and review_period:

Why it is correct: comparison uses == and a boolean is evaluated directly: if day_of_week == 1 and review_period:.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — if day_of_week = 1 and review_period: — Why it is incorrect: = is assignment, not comparison.
  • Option B — if day_of_week = 1 and review_period == "True": — Why it is incorrect: = 1 is assignment and "True" is a string, not a boolean.
  • Option C — if day_of_week = 1 & review_period = "True": — Why it is incorrect: = and & are not the right operators.

q047.stem: Which of the following describes a scenario in which a data engineer will want to use a single-node cluster?
options: When they are working interactively with a small amount of data
When they are running automated reports to be refreshed as quickly as possible
When they are working with SQL within Databricks SQL
When they are concerned about the ability to automatically scale with larger data
When they are manually running reports with a large amount of data

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: When they are working interactively with a small amount of data

Why it is correct: a single-node cluster (driver only) is enough and cheap for interactive work with small data.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — When they are running automated reports to be refreshed as quickly as possible — Why it is incorrect: speed calls for distributed resources.
  • Option C — When they are working with SQL within Databricks SQL — Why it is incorrect: Databricks SQL uses SQL warehouses.
  • Option D — When they are concerned about the ability to automatically scale with larger data — Why it is incorrect: single-node does not autoscale.
  • Option E — When they are manually running reports with a large amount of data — Why it is incorrect: large data calls for a multi-node cluster.

q048.stem: Which of the following describes the relationship between Bronze tables and raw data?
options: Bronze tables contain less data than raw data files.
Bronze tables contain more truthful data than raw data.
Bronze tables contain raw data with a schema applied.
Bronze tables contain a less refined view of data than raw data.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Bronze tables contain raw data with a schema applied.

Why it is correct: Bronze keeps data as it arrives, with a schema applied and ingestion metadata.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Bronze tables contain less data than raw data files. — Why it is incorrect: Bronze preserves all source content.
  • Option B — Bronze tables contain more truthful data than raw data. — Why it is incorrect: truthfulness does not change in Bronze; cleaning arrives in Silver.
  • Option D — Bronze tables contain a less refined view of data than raw data. — Why it is incorrect: it is not less refined than raw: it already has a schema.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q049.stem: A data engineer has realized that the data files associated with a Delta table are incredibly small. They want to compact the small files to form larger files to improve performance. Which of the following keywords can be used to compact the small files?
options: REDUCE
OPTIMIZE
COMPACTION
REPARTITION
VACUUM

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: OPTIMIZE

Why it is correct: OPTIMIZE compacts small files into larger ones.

  • Official documentation: Optimize data file layout (OPTIMIZE) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — REDUCE — Why it is incorrect: REDUCE is not a Delta command.
  • Option C — COMPACTION — Why it is incorrect: COMPACTION is not a Delta SQL command.
  • Option D — REPARTITION — Why it is incorrect: REPARTITION is a DataFrame operation; it does not compact the table.
  • Option E — VACUUM — Why it is incorrect: VACUUM removes obsolete files; it does not compact.

q050.stem:
A data engineer has realized that they made a mistake when making a daily update to a table. They need to use Delta time travel to restore the table to a version that is 3 days old. However, when the data engineer attempts to time travel to the older version, they are unable to restore the data because the data files have been deleted.

Which of the following explains why the data files are no longer present?
options: The VACUUM command was run on the table
The TIME TRAVEL command was run on the table
The DELETE HISTORY command was run on the table
The OPTIMIZE command was run on the table

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: The VACUUM command was run on the table

Why it is correct: VACUUM deletes files of old versions beyond the retention period, so time travel to them is no longer possible.

  • Official documentation: Remove unused data files with VACUUM - Databricks | Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — The TIME TRAVEL command was run on the table — Why it is incorrect: TIME TRAVEL is not a command that deletes files.
  • Option C — The DELETE HISTORY command was run on the table — Why it is incorrect: DELETE HISTORY does not exist.
  • Option D — The OPTIMIZE command was run on the table — Why it is incorrect: OPTIMIZE compacts files but keeps the old ones until VACUUM.

links.t: Remove unused data files with VACUUM
Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q051.stem:
A data engineer needs to apply custom logic to string column city in table stores for a specific use case. In order to apply this custom logic at scale, the data engineer wants to create a SQL user-defined function (UDF).

Which of the following code blocks creates this SQL UDF?
options:
CREATE FUNCTION combine_nyc(city STRING)
RETURNS STRING
RETURN CASE
  WHEN city = "brooklyn" THEN "new york"
  ELSE city
END;

CREATE UDF combine_nyc(city STRING)
RETURNS STRING
CASE
   WHEN city = "brooklyn" THEN "new york"
   ELSE city
END;

CREATE FUNCTION combine_nyc(city STRING)
RETURN CASE
   WHEN city = "brooklyn" THEN "new york"
   ELSE city
END;

CREATE UDF combine_nyc(city STRING)
RETURNS STRING
RETURN CASE
  WHEN city = "brooklyn" THEN "new york"
  ELSE city
END;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    CREATE FUNCTION combine_nyc(city STRING)
RETURNS STRING
RETURN CASE
  WHEN city = "brooklyn" THEN "new york"
  ELSE city
END;

Why it is correct: a SQL UDF is created with CREATE FUNCTION name(params) RETURNS type RETURN expression.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: CREATE UDF does not exist and RETURN is missing.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: the RETURNS STRING clause is missing.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it uses CREATE UDF, which does not exist in SQL.

q052.stem: Which of the following can be used to simplify and unify siloed data architectures that are specialized for specific use cases?
options: None of these
Data lake
Data warehouse
All of these
Data lakehouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Data lakehouse

Why it is correct: the lakehouse combines the best of the data lake and the data warehouse in one platform, removing silos.

  • Official documentation: What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — None of these — Why it is incorrect: the lakehouse does achieve it.
  • Option B — Data lake — Why it is incorrect: a data lake alone is one of the silos.
  • Option C — Data warehouse — Why it is incorrect: a data warehouse alone is another silo.
  • Option D — All of these — Why it is incorrect: only the lakehouse unifies.

q053.stem:
An engineering manager uses a Databricks SQL query to monitor ingestion latency for each data source. The manager checks the results of the query every day, but they are manually rerunning the query each day and waiting for the results.

Which of the following approaches can the manager use to ensure the results of the query are updated each day?
options: They can schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the SQL endpoint's page in Databricks SQL.
They can schedule the query to refresh every 12 hours from the SQL endpoint's page in Databricks SQL.
They can schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the query's page in Databricks SQL.
They can schedule the query to run every 12 hours from the Jobs UI.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: They can schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the query's page in Databricks SQL.

Why it is correct: the refresh schedule is set on the query's own page, with a 1-day frequency.

  • Official documentation: Databricks SQL - Databricks | Automating jobs with schedules and triggers - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the SQL endpoint's page in Databricks SQL. — Why it is incorrect: the schedule is not defined on the endpoint page.
  • Option B — They can schedule the query to refresh every 12 hours from the SQL endpoint's page in Databricks SQL. — Why it is incorrect: it is neither set there nor is 12 h the requested frequency.
  • Option D — They can schedule the query to run every 12 hours from the Jobs UI. — Why it is incorrect: 12 h is not the requested frequency; scheduling the query is enough.

links.t: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers

q054.stem:
A data engineer has a Python notebook in Databricks, but they need to use SQL to accomplish a specific task within a cell. They still want all of the other cells to use Python without making any changes to those cells.

Which of the following describes how the data engineer can use SQL within a cell of their Python notebook?
options: It is not possible to use SQL in a Python notebook
They can attach the cell to a SQL endpoint rather than a Databricks cluster
They can simply write SQL syntax in the cell
They can add %sql to the first line of the cell
They can change the default language of the notebook to SQL

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: They can add %sql to the first line of the cell

Why it is correct: magic commands (%sql) switch the language of a single cell.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — It is not possible to use SQL in a Python notebook — Why it is incorrect: it is possible with magic commands.
  • Option B — They can attach the cell to a SQL endpoint rather than a Databricks cluster — Why it is incorrect: cells are not attached individually to an endpoint.
  • Option C — They can simply write SQL syntax in the cell — Why it is incorrect: without %sql the cell is interpreted as Python.
  • Option E — They can change the default language of the notebook to SQL — Why it is incorrect: it would change the language of the whole notebook.

q055.stem: Which of the following SQL keywords can be used to convert a table from a long format to a wide format?
options: TRANSFORM
PIVOT
SUM
CONVERT
WHERE

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: PIVOT

Why it is correct: PIVOT turns row values into columns (long → wide).

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — TRANSFORM — Why it is incorrect: TRANSFORM applies scripts/functions; it does not pivot.
  • Option C — SUM — Why it is incorrect: SUM is an aggregate.
  • Option D — CONVERT — Why it is incorrect: CONVERT does not pivot.
  • Option E — WHERE — Why it is incorrect: WHERE filters rows.

q056.stem: Which of the following describes a benefit of creating an external table from Parquet rather than CSV when using a CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement?
options: Parquet files can be partitioned
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statements cannot be used on files
Parquet files have a well-defined schema
Parquet files have the ability to be optimized
Parquet files will become Delta tables

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Parquet files have a well-defined schema

Why it is correct: Parquet stores the schema (column types) with the data; CSV is untyped text.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Parquet files can be partitioned — Why it is incorrect: partitioning is also possible with CSV.
  • Option B — CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statements cannot be used on files — Why it is incorrect: CTAS can be used with files.
  • Option D — Parquet files have the ability to be optimized — Why it is incorrect: OPTIMIZE is a Delta feature, not plain Parquet.
  • Option E — Parquet files will become Delta tables — Why it is incorrect: they do not become Delta on their own.

q057.stem:
The Delta transaction log for the 'students' table is shown using the 'DESCRIBE HISTORY students' command. A Data Engineer needs to query the table as it existed before the UPDATE operation listed in the log.

version  timestamp                 operation
8        2024-04-22T14:33:31.000    OPTIMIZE
7        2024-04-22T14:33:16.000    MERGE
6        2024-04-22T14:33:06.000    DELETE
5        2024-04-22T14:32:58.000    UPDATE
4        2024-04-22T14:32:47.000    WRITE
3        2024-04-22T14:32:44.000    WRITE
2        2024-04-22T14:32:23.000    WRITE
1        2024-04-22T14:32:20.000    WRITE
0        2024-04-22T14:31:49.000    CREATE TABLE

Which command should the Data Engineer use to achieve this? (Choose two.)
options: SELECT * FROM students@v4
SELECT * FROM students TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-04-22T14:32:47.000+00:00'
SELECT * FROM students FROM HISTORY VERSION AS OF 3
SELECT * FROM students VERSION AS OF 5
SELECT * FROM students TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-04-22T14:32:58.000+00:00'

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: SELECT * FROM students@v4
  • Option B: SELECT * FROM students TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-04-22T14:32:47.000+00:00'

Why it is correct: the UPDATE is version 5, so you must read version 4 (the one just before): students@v4 or TIMESTAMP AS OF with version 4's timestamp (14:32:47).

  • Official documentation: Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option C — SELECT * FROM students FROM HISTORY VERSION AS OF 3 — Why it is incorrect: FROM HISTORY VERSION AS OF is not valid syntax.
  • Option D — SELECT * FROM students VERSION AS OF 5 — Why it is incorrect: VERSION AS OF 5 already includes the UPDATE.
  • Option E — SELECT * FROM students TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-04-22T14:32:58.000+00:00' — Why it is incorrect: 14:32:58 is the UPDATE itself (version 5).

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q058.stem:
A data engineer needs to access the view created by the sales team, using a shared cluster. The data engineer has been provided usage permissions on the catalog and schema. In order to access the view created by sales team.

What are the minimum permissions the data engineer would require in addition?
options: Needs SELECT permission on the VIEW and the underlying TABLE.
Needs SELECT permission only on the VIEW
Needs ALL PRIVILEGES on the VIEW
Needs ALL PRIVILEGES at the SCHEMA level

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Needs SELECT permission only on the VIEW

Why it is correct: in Unity Catalog SELECT on the view is enough; the view owner already has access to the underlying table.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Needs SELECT permission on the VIEW and the underlying TABLE. — Why it is incorrect: access to the base table is not needed.
  • Option C — Needs ALL PRIVILEGES on the VIEW — Why it is incorrect: that is more than the minimum.
  • Option D — Needs ALL PRIVILEGES at the SCHEMA level — Why it is incorrect: that is far more than the minimum.

q059.stem:
A data engineer needs to apply custom logic to identify employees with more than 5 years of experience in array column employees in table stores. The custom logic should create a new column exp_employees that is an array of all of the employees with more than 5 years of experience for each row. In order to apply this custom logic at scale, the data engineer wants to use the FILTER higher-order function.

Which of the following code blocks successfully completes this task?
options:
SELECT
  store_id,
  employees,
  FILTER (employees, i -> i.years_exp > 5) AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

SELECT
  store_id,
  employees,
  FILTER (exp_employees, years_exp > 5) AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

SELECT
   store_id,
   employees,
  FILTER (employees, years_exp > 5) AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

SELECT
  store_id,
  employees,
  CASE WHEN employees.years_exp > 5 THEN employees
     ELSE NULL
  END AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

SELECT
  store_id,
  employees,
  FILTER (exp_employees, i -> i.years_exp > 5) AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    SELECT
  store_id,
