  employees,
  FILTER (employees, i -> i.years_exp > 5) AS exp_employees
FROM stores;

Why it is correct: FILTER(employees, i -> i.years_exp > 5) applies a lambda over the existing employees array and returns matching elements.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: FILTER over exp_employees (not yet existing) and without a lambda.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: the lambda (i -> …) is missing.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: CASE does not filter elements inside an array.
  • Option E — … — Why it is incorrect: it uses exp_employees, which does not exist yet.

q060.stem: A Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline processes employee travel reimbursements. The field location must be provided. The pipeline must fail the affected update if any record has NULL in location. Which expectation is correct?
options: CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NULL)
CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE
CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW
CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION FAIL

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE

Why it is correct: EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE checks a value exists and stops the update otherwise.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NULL) — Why it is incorrect: IS NULL inverts the condition and defines no action.
  • Option C — CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW — Why it is incorrect: DROP ROW drops rows; it does not fail the update.
  • Option D — CONSTRAINT valid_location EXPECT (location IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION FAIL — Why it is incorrect: ON VIOLATION FAIL is not valid syntax; it is FAIL UPDATE.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q061.stem:
Identify a scenario to use an external table.

A Data Engineer needs to create a parquet bronze table and wants to ensure that it gets stored in a specific path in an external location.

Which table can be created in this scenario?
options: An external table where the location is pointing to specific path in external location.
An external table where the schema has managed location pointing to specific path in external location.
A managed table where the catalog has managed location pointing to specific path in external location.
A managed table where the location is pointing to specific path in external location.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: An external table where the location is pointing to specific path in external location.

Why it is correct: an external table is created with LOCATION pointing to the specific path wanted.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — An external table where the schema has managed location pointing to specific path in external location. — Why it is incorrect: a schema's managed location applies to managed tables, not to the path of an external table.
  • Option C — A managed table where the catalog has managed location pointing to specific path in external location. — Why it is incorrect: for a managed table the path is decided by Unity Catalog, not the engineer.
  • Option D — A managed table where the location is pointing to specific path in external location. — Why it is incorrect: a managed table does not accept its own LOCATION.

q062.stem:
Data engineer and data analysts are working together on a data pipeline. The data engineer is working on the raw, bronze, and silver layers of the pipeline using Python, and the data analyst is working on the gold layer of the pipeline using SQL. The raw source of the pipeline is a streaming input. They now want to migrate their pipeline to use Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables).

Which of the following changes will need to be made to the pipeline when migrating to Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables)?
options: The pipeline can have different notebook sources in SQL & Python
The pipeline will need to be written entirely in SQL
The pipeline will need to use a batch source in place of a streaming source
The pipeline will need to be written entirely in Python

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: The pipeline can have different notebook sources in SQL & Python

Why it is correct: a declarative pipeline supports several SQL and Python source files/notebooks at once and streaming sources. Nothing needs to be changed necessarily.

⚠️ Heads-up: the wording is unclear: A is the only option that does not impose a false restriction, but none describes a strictly mandatory "change". Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — The pipeline will need to be written entirely in SQL — Why it is incorrect: using only SQL is not required.
  • Option C — The pipeline will need to use a batch source in place of a streaming source — Why it is incorrect: streaming sources are supported.
  • Option D — The pipeline will need to be written entirely in Python — Why it is incorrect: using only Python is not required.

q063.stem:
A data engineer that is new to using Python needs to create a Python function to add two integers together and return the sum?

Which of the following code blocks can the data engineer use to complete this task?
options:
function add_integers(x, y):
return x + y

function add_integers(x, y):
x+y

def add_integers(x, y):
print(x + y)

def add_integers(x, y):
return x + y

def add_integers(x, y):
x+y

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    def add_integers(x, y):
return x + y

Why it is correct: a Python function is declared with def and returns the result with return.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: function is not a Python keyword.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: function does not exist and returns nothing.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it only prints; it does not return the sum.
  • Option E — … — Why it is incorrect: it computes but does not return.

q064.stem:
A data engineer has configured a Structured Streaming job to read from a table, manipulate the data, and then perform a streaming write into a new table.

The code block used by the data engineer is below:

(spark.readStream
   .table("sales")
   .withColumn("avg_price", col("sales") / col("units"))
   .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
   .outputMode("complete")
   .[blank]
   .table("new_sales")
)

The data engineer only wants the query to process all of the available data in as many batches as required.

Which line of code should the data engineer use to fill in the blank?
options: trigger(availableNow=True)
trigger(processingTime="once")
trigger(continuous="once")
trigger(once=True)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: trigger(availableNow=True)

Why it is correct: trigger(availableNow=True) processes all available data in multiple micro-batches and then stops.

  • Official documentation: Structured Streaming trigger intervals - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — trigger(processingTime="once") — Why it is incorrect: processingTime expects an interval, not "once".
  • Option C — trigger(continuous="once") — Why it is incorrect: continuous="once" is not valid.
  • Option D — trigger(once=True) — Why it is incorrect: once=True processes everything in a single batch (deprecated).

q065.stem:
In a healthcare provider organization using Delta Lake to store electronic health records (EHRs), a data analyst needs to analyze a snapshot of the patient_records table from two weeks ago before some recent data corrections were applied.

What approach should the Data Engineer take to allow the analyst to query that specific prior version?
options:
Truncate the table to remove all data, then reload the data from two weeks ago into the truncated table for the
analyst to query.

Identify the version number corresponding to two weeks ago from the Delta transaction log, share that version
    number with the analyst to query using VERSION AS OF syntax, or export that version to a new Delta table
for the
    analyst to query.

Restore the table to the version from two weeks ago using the RESTORE command, and have the analyst
query the
   restored table.

Use the VACUUM command to remove all versions of the table older than two weeks, then the analyst can
query the
   remaining version.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Identify the version number corresponding to two weeks ago from the Delta transaction log, share that version
    number with the analyst to query using VERSION AS OF syntax, or export that version to a new Delta table
for the
    analyst to query.

Why it is correct: time travel reads the old version without touching the production table.

  • Official documentation: Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it would destroy production data.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: RESTORE changes the table's current state for everyone.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: VACUUM removes old versions; it would do the opposite.

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q066.stem:
A data engineer has developed a data pipeline to ingest data from a JSON source using Auto Loader, but the engineer has not provided any type inference or schema hints in their pipeline. Upon reviewing the data, the data engineer has noticed that all of the columns in the target table are of the string type despite some of the fields only including float or boolean values.

Which of the following describes why Auto Loader inferred all of the columns to be of the string type?
options: There was a type mismatch between the specific schema and the inferred schema
JSON data is a text-based format
Auto Loader only works with string data
All of the fields had at least one null value
Auto Loader cannot infer the schema of ingested data

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: JSON data is a text-based format

Why it is correct: by default Auto Loader infers JSON/CSV columns as string because they are text formats; to infer types enable cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes or use schema hints.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — There was a type mismatch between the specific schema and the inferred schema — Why it is incorrect: no schema had been defined.
  • Option C — Auto Loader only works with string data — Why it is incorrect: it works with many types.
  • Option D — All of the fields had at least one null value — Why it is incorrect: nulls do not force string.
  • Option E — Auto Loader cannot infer the schema of ingested data — Why it is incorrect: it can infer schemas.

q067.stem: A Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline contains two Streaming Tables and three Materialized Views. The pipeline is configured for continuous execution rather than triggered execution. Previously unprocessed data exists and all definitions are valid. What should happen?
options: All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will be terminated.

All datasets will be updated continuously until the pipeline is stopped, but compute resources will terminate
automatically after the first refresh.

All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will persist without any processing. The compute resources
will
    persist but go unused.

All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will persist to allow
for
   additional testing.

The pipeline remains active, processing new source data as it arrives and keeping compute running until the
continuous execution is stopped.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: 
    The pipeline remains active, processing new source data as it arrives and keeping compute running until the
continuous execution is stopped.

Why it is correct: in continuous mode the pipeline stays active and processes new data as it arrives, with compute running until stopped.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will be terminated. — Why it is incorrect: that describes triggered mode.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: compute does not terminate after the first refresh in continuous mode.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: in continuous mode it keeps processing.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: continuous mode does not shut down.

q068.stem: Which of the following data workloads will utilize a Gold table as its source?
options: A job that enriches data by parsing its timestamps into a human-readable format
A job that aggregates uncleaned data to create standard summary statistics
A job that cleans data by removing malformed records
A job that queries aggregated data designed to feed into a dashboard
A job that ingests raw data from a streaming source into the Lakehouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: A job that queries aggregated data designed to feed into a dashboard

Why it is correct: Gold tables hold aggregated, consumption-ready data (dashboards, reports). Querying them for a dashboard uses Gold as source.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A job that enriches data by parsing its timestamps into a human-readable format — Why it is incorrect: that is Silver-style enrichment.
  • Option B — A job that aggregates uncleaned data to create standard summary statistics — Why it is incorrect: it starts from uncleaned (Bronze) data and produces Gold.
  • Option C — A job that cleans data by removing malformed records — Why it is incorrect: that is Silver-style cleaning.
  • Option E — A job that ingests raw data from a streaming source into the Lakehouse — Why it is incorrect: that is ingestion into Bronze.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q069.stem: Which two components function in the DB platform architecture's control plane? (Choose two.)
options: Virtual Machines
Compute Orchestration
Serverless Compute
Compute
Unity Catalog

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option B: Compute Orchestration
  • Option E: Unity Catalog

Why it is correct: compute orchestration and Unity Catalog (governance and metadata) are managed control-plane services.

  • Official documentation: Databricks architecture (control and data planes) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Virtual Machines — Why it is incorrect: classic cluster VMs are in the customer account (data plane).
  • Option C — Serverless Compute — Why it is incorrect: serverless compute runs in the Databricks serverless compute plane, not the control plane.
  • Option D — Compute — Why it is incorrect: data-processing compute is in the data plane.

q070.stem:
Identify how the count_if function and the count where x is null can be used.

Consider a table random_values with the data below:

col1
0
1
2
NULL
2
3

What would be the output of the below query?

select count_if(col > 1) as count_a, count(*) as count_b, count(col1) as count_c from random_values

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 3 6 5

Why it is correct: count_if counts values > 1 (2, 2, 3 → 3); count(*) counts all 6 rows; count(col1) ignores the NULL → 5. Result: 3, 6, 5.

⚠️ Heads-up: the table in the original PDF is garbled; it has been reconstructed as 0, 1, 2, NULL, 2, 3, and the query uses col where col1 is meant. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — 4 6 5 — Why it is incorrect: count_if gives 3, not 4.
  • Option C — 3 6 6 — Why it is incorrect: count(col1) excludes the NULL: 5, not 6.
  • Option D — 4 6 6 — Why it is incorrect: neither 4 nor 6 is right for the first and third counts.

q071.stem: Which of the following describes the type of workloads that are always compatible with Auto Loader?
options: Streaming workloads
Machine learning workloads
Serverless workloads
Batch workloads
Dashboard workloads

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Streaming workloads

Why it is correct: Auto Loader is a Structured Streaming source (cloudFiles with readStream), so it always works in streaming workloads.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Machine learning workloads — Why it is incorrect: the use case does not determine compatibility.
  • Option C — Serverless workloads — Why it is incorrect: it is not a workload-type condition.
  • Option D — Batch workloads — Why it is incorrect: it can run batch-style with availableNow, but "always" compatible means streaming.
  • Option E — Dashboard workloads — Why it is incorrect: unrelated.

q072.stem:
Differentiate between all-purpose clusters and jobs clusters.

A data engineering team has created a python notebook to load data from cloud storage, this job has been tested and now needs to be scheduled in production.

Which would be the best cluster to be used in this case?
options: All purpose cluster
Any Unity Catalog-enabled cluster
Jobs Cluster
Serverless SQL warehouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Jobs Cluster

Why it is correct: a Jobs Cluster is created for the run and terminates when done: cheaper and isolated for production.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — All purpose cluster — Why it is incorrect: all-purpose clusters are interactive and more expensive.
  • Option B — Any Unity Catalog-enabled cluster — Why it is incorrect: "Unity Catalog-enabled" is not a cluster type suited to scheduling.
  • Option D — Serverless SQL warehouse — Why it is incorrect: a SQL warehouse runs SQL, not Python notebooks.

q073.stem:
A data engineer is using the following code block as part of a batch ingestion pipeline to read from a table:

transactions_df = (spark.read
    .schema(schema)
    .format("delta")
    .table("transactions")
)

Which of the following changes needs to be made so this code block will work when the transactions table is a stream source?
options: Replace predict with a stream-friendly prediction function
Replace schema(schema) with option ("maxFilesPerTrigger", 1)
Replace "transactions" with the path to the location of the Delta table
Replace format("delta") with format("stream")
Replace spark.read with spark.readStream

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Replace spark.read with spark.readStream

Why it is correct: a streaming source is read with spark.readStream.

  • Official documentation: Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Replace predict with a stream-friendly prediction function — Why it is incorrect: there is no predict function in the code.
  • Option B — Replace schema(schema) with option ("maxFilesPerTrigger", 1) — Why it is incorrect: it is a rate option; it does not turn the read into a stream.
  • Option C — Replace "transactions" with the path to the location of the Delta table — Why it is incorrect: not needed; readStream.table accepts a name.
  • Option D — Replace format("delta") with format("stream") — Why it is incorrect: "stream" is not a valid format.

q074.stem: Which of the following queries is performing a streaming hop from raw data to a Bronze table?
options:
(spark.table("sales")
   .groupBy("store")
   .agg(sum("sales"))
   .writeStream
   .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
   .outputMode("complete")
   .table("newSales")
)

(spark.table("sales")
    .filter(col("units") > 0)
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("append")
    .table("newSales")
)

(spark.table("sales")
    .withColumn("avgPrice", col("sales") / col("units"))
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("append")
    .table("newSales")
)

(spark.read.load(rawSalesLocation)
   .write
   .mode("append")
   .table("newSales")
)

(spark.readStream.load(rawSalesLocation)
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("append")
    .table("newSales")
)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: 
    (spark.readStream.load(rawSalesLocation)
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)
    .outputMode("append")
    .table("newSales")
)

Why it is correct: it reads raw data with readStream and writes it as-is with writeStream in append mode: Raw → Bronze ingestion.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it aggregates (groupBy): a Gold step, with a batch read.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it filters with a batch read: Silver refinement.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it derives a column with a batch read: Silver.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: batch write (write), not streaming.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q075.stem:
A dataset has been defined using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) and includes an expectations clause:

CONSTRAINT valid_timestamp EXPECT (timestamp > '2020-01-01') ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE

What is the expected behavior when a batch of data containing data that violates these constraints is processed?
options:
Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event
log.
The affected pipeline update fails and the invalid data is not committed to the target table.
Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and loaded into a quarantine table.
Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event log.

Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and flagged as invalid in a field added to
the
      target dataset.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: The affected pipeline update fails and the invalid data is not committed to the target table.

Why it is correct: ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE fails the update and commits no invalid data.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: that is DROP ROW.
  • Option C — Records that violate the expectation are dropped from the target dataset and loaded into a quarantine table. — Why it is incorrect: no quarantine is created automatically.
  • Option D — Records that violate the expectation are added to the target dataset and recorded as invalid in the event log. — Why it is incorrect: that is the default without action (plain EXPECT).
  • Option E — … — Why it is incorrect: no flag field is added.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q076.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the relationship between Silver tables and Bronze tables is always true?
options: Silver tables contain a less refined, less clean view of data than Bronze data.
Silver tables contain aggregates while Bronze data is unaggregated.
Silver tables contain more data than Bronze tables.
Silver tables contain a more refined and cleaner view of data than Bronze tables.
Silver tables contain less data than Bronze tables.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Silver tables contain a more refined and cleaner view of data than Bronze tables.

Why it is correct: Silver applies cleaning, deduplication and validation over Bronze, so it is more refined; volume is not guaranteed.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Silver tables contain a less refined, less clean view of data than Bronze data. — Why it is incorrect: it is the other way round.
  • Option B — Silver tables contain aggregates while Bronze data is unaggregated. — Why it is incorrect: aggregates usually live in Gold.
  • Option C — Silver tables contain more data than Bronze tables. — Why it is incorrect: not always more.
  • Option E — Silver tables contain less data than Bronze tables. — Why it is incorrect: not always fewer (joins/enrichment may add rows).

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q077.stem:
A data engineering team has noticed that their Databricks SQL queries are running too slowly when they are submitted to a non-running SQL warehouse. The data engineering team wants this issue to be resolved.

Which of the following approaches can the team use to reduce the time it takes to return results in this scenario?
options:
They can turn on the Serverless feature for the SQL endpoint and change the Spot Instance Policy to
"Reliability
   Optimized."
They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL endpoint.
They can increase the cluster size of the SQL endpoint.
They can turn on the Serverless feature for the SQL warehouse.
They can increase the maximum bound of the SQL endpoint's scaling range.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: They can turn on the Serverless feature for the SQL warehouse.

Why it is correct: serverless SQL warehouses start in seconds, removing the wait for a stopped warehouse.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks | SQL warehouses - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: the spot instance policy does not speed up start-up.
  • Option B — They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: Auto Stop shuts down more, aggravating start-ups.
  • Option C — They can increase the cluster size of the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: it improves execution performance, not start-up.
  • Option E — They can increase the maximum bound of the SQL endpoint's scaling range. — Why it is incorrect: raising the scaling max does not speed up a cold start.

q078.stem: A team needs applicable ALL PRIVILEGES on Unity Catalog table main.sales_data.sales (not ownership). Which GRANT statement is correct?
options: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team;
GRANT SELECT CREATE MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE team TO main.sales_data.sales;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team;

Why it is correct: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE … TO team grants all applicable privileges without transferring ownership.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — GRANT SELECT CREATE MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team; — Why it is incorrect: a privilege list without commas is invalid syntax and does not cover all.
  • Option C — GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.sales_data.sales TO team; — Why it is incorrect: it only grants SELECT.
  • Option D — GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE team TO main.sales_data.sales; — Why it is incorrect: it swaps object and recipient.

q079.stem: Which of the following approaches should be used to send the Databricks Job owner an email in the case that the Job fails?
options: Manually programming in an alert system in each cell of the Notebook
Setting up an Alert in the Job page
Setting up an Alert in the Notebook
There is no way to notify the Job owner in the case of Job failure
MLflow Model Registry Webhooks

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Setting up an Alert in the Job page

Why it is correct: failure notifications are configured on the Job page (email, webhook, etc.).

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Manually programming in an alert system in each cell of the Notebook — Why it is incorrect: unnecessary and fragile.
  • Option C — Setting up an Alert in the Notebook — Why it is incorrect: notebooks do not manage Job notifications.
  • Option D — There is no way to notify the Job owner in the case of Job failure — Why it is incorrect: there is a way.
  • Option E — MLflow Model Registry Webhooks — Why it is incorrect: they are for Model Registry events.

q080.stem:
A data engineer has been using a Databricks SQL dashboard to monitor the cleanliness of the input data to a data analytics dashboard for a retail use case. The job has a Databricks SQL query that returns the number of store- level records where sales is equal to zero. The data engineer wants their entire team to be notified via a messaging webhook whenever this value is greater than 0.

Which of the following approaches can the data engineer use to notify their entire team via a messaging webhook whenever the number of stores with $0 in sales is greater than zero?
options: They can set up an Alert with a custom template.
They can set up an Alert with a new email alert destination.
They can set up an Alert with one-time notifications.
They can set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.
They can set up an Alert without notifications.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: They can set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.

Why it is correct: a Databricks SQL alert with a webhook destination sends the notification to the messaging tool when the condition is met.

  • Official documentation: Databricks SQL - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can set up an Alert with a custom template. — Why it is incorrect: a template changes the text, not the channel.
  • Option B — They can set up an Alert with a new email alert destination. — Why it is incorrect: an email destination does not use a webhook.
  • Option C — They can set up an Alert with one-time notifications. — Why it is incorrect: one-time does not cover continuous monitoring nor use a webhook.
  • Option E — They can set up an Alert without notifications. — Why it is incorrect: without notifications nobody is told.

q081.stem:
A data engineer wants to schedule their Databricks SQL dashboard to refresh every hour, but they only want the associated SQL warehouse to be running when it is necessary. The dashboard has multiple queries on multiple datasets associated with it. The data that feeds the dashboard is automatically processed using a Databricks Job.

Which of the following approaches can the data engineer use to minimize the total running time of the SQL warehouse used in the refresh schedule of their dashboard?
options: They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL warehouse.
They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint is not one of the included query's SQL endpoints.
They can reduce the cluster size of the SQL endpoint.
They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint matches each of the queries' SQL endpoints.
They can set up the dashboard's SQL endpoint to be serverless.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL warehouse.

Why it is correct: Auto Stop shuts the warehouse down after a period of inactivity between refreshes, so it only runs while the dashboard refreshes.

  • Official documentation: SQL warehouses - Databricks | AI/BI dashboards - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint is not one of the included query's SQL endpoints. — Why it is incorrect: it does not affect how long it stays on.
  • Option C — They can reduce the cluster size of the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: it changes performance/cost, not on-time.
  • Option D — They can ensure the dashboard's SQL endpoint matches each of the queries' SQL endpoints. — Why it is incorrect: matching does not reduce running time.
  • Option E — They can set up the dashboard's SQL endpoint to be serverless. — Why it is incorrect: serverless starts fast, but what shuts the warehouse down between refreshes is Auto Stop.

q082.stem: Which two conditions are applicable for governance in Databricks Unity Catalog? (Choose two.)
options: You can have more than 1 metastore within a databricks account console but only 1 per region.

Both catalog and schema must have a managed location in Unity Catalog provided metastore is not
associated with a
    location
You can have multiple catalogs within metastore and 1 catalog can be associated with multiple metastore
If catalog is not associated with location, it's mandatory to associate schema with managed locations
If metastore is not associated with location, it's mandatory to associate catalog with managed locations

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: You can have more than 1 metastore within a databricks account console but only 1 per region.
  • Option E: If metastore is not associated with location, it's mandatory to associate catalog with managed locations

Why it is correct: an account can have several metastores but only one per region; and if the metastore has no storage location of its own, each catalog must have a managed location.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: a catalog location is enough; the schema does not also need one.
  • Option C — You can have multiple catalogs within metastore and 1 catalog can be associated with multiple metastore — Why it is incorrect: a catalog belongs to a single metastore.
  • Option D — If catalog is not associated with location, it's mandatory to associate schema with managed locations — Why it is incorrect: without a catalog location it can inherit the metastore's; the schema one is not mandatory.

q083.stem: Which data lakehouse feature results in improved data quality over a traditional data lake?
options: A data lakehouse stores data in open formats.
A data lakehouse allows the use of SQL queries to examine data.
A data lakehouse provides storage solutions for structured and unstructured data.
A data lakehouse supports ACID-compliant transactions.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: A data lakehouse supports ACID-compliant transactions.

Why it is correct: ACID transactions prevent partial writes and guarantee consistent reads.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks | What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A data lakehouse stores data in open formats. — Why it is incorrect: open formats avoid lock-in; they do not improve quality.
  • Option B — A data lakehouse allows the use of SQL queries to examine data. — Why it is incorrect: using SQL does not improve quality.
  • Option C — A data lakehouse provides storage solutions for structured and unstructured data. — Why it is incorrect: that is flexibility, not quality.

q084.stem: In which scenario will a data team want to utilize cluster pools?
options: An automated report needs to be version-controlled across multiple collaborators.
An automated report needs to be runnable by all stakeholders.
An automated report needs to be refreshed as quickly as possible.
An automated report needs to be made reproducible.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: An automated report needs to be refreshed as quickly as possible.

Why it is correct: a pool keeps instances ready and cuts cluster start-up time, speeding up the refresh.

  • Official documentation: Pool configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — An automated report needs to be version-controlled across multiple collaborators. — Why it is incorrect: version control is done with Git folders.
  • Option B — An automated report needs to be runnable by all stakeholders. — Why it is incorrect: permissions are handled with ACLs.
  • Option D — An automated report needs to be made reproducible. — Why it is incorrect: reproducibility depends on code and versions, not pools.

q085.stem:
A data engineer needs to determine whether to use the built-in Databricks Notebooks versioning or version their project using Git folders (antes Databricks Repos).

What is an advantage of using Git folders (antes Databricks Repos) over the Databricks Notebooks versioning?
options: Databricks Repos allows users to revert to previous versions of a notebook
Databricks Repos is wholly housed within the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform
Databricks Repos provides the ability to comment on specific changes
Git folders supports the use of multiple branches

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Git folders supports the use of multiple branches

Why it is correct: Git folders integrate with Git and support working with multiple branches.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks Repos allows users to revert to previous versions of a notebook — Why it is incorrect: notebook history also lets you revert versions.
  • Option B — Databricks Repos is wholly housed within the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform — Why it is incorrect: it is not an advantage; it actually integrates with external Git providers.
  • Option C — Databricks Repos provides the ability to comment on specific changes — Why it is incorrect: commenting on changes belongs to pull requests in the Git provider; notebooks also support comments.

q086.stem: What is a benefit of the Databricks Lakehouse Architecture embracing open source technologies?
options: Avoiding vendor lock-in
Simplified governance
Ability to scale workloads
Cloud-specific integrations

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Avoiding vendor lock-in

Why it is correct: open formats and projects let you avoid dependence on a single vendor.

  • Official documentation: What is a data lakehouse? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Simplified governance — Why it is incorrect: governance comes from Unity Catalog.
  • Option C — Ability to scale workloads — Why it is incorrect: scaling comes from distributed compute.
  • Option D — Cloud-specific integrations — Why it is incorrect: openness does not imply cloud-specific integrations.

q087.stem: A data engineer needs to use a Delta table as part of a data pipeline, but they do not know if they have the appropriate permissions. In which location can the data engineer review their permissions on the table?
options: Jobs
Dashboards
Catalog Explorer
Repos

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Catalog Explorer

Why it is correct: Catalog Explorer shows Unity Catalog objects and their permissions.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Jobs — Why it is incorrect: Jobs manages runs, not table permissions.
  • Option B — Dashboards — Why it is incorrect: Dashboards is visualization.
  • Option D — Repos — Why it is incorrect: Repos is version control.

q088.stem: Which file format is used for storing Delta Lake Table?
options: CSV
Parquet
JSON
Delta

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Parquet

Why it is correct: Delta table data is stored in Parquet files; the _delta_log adds transactions.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — CSV — Why it is incorrect: CSV is not Delta's storage format.
  • Option C — JSON — Why it is incorrect: the log uses JSON for commits, but the data does not.
  • Option D — Delta — Why it is incorrect: "Delta" is the protocol/table, not a data file format.

q089.stem:
A data architect has determined that a table of the following format is necessary:

employeeId    startDate    avgRating
a1         2009-01-06   5.5
a2         2018-11-21   7.1
...      ...       ...

Which code block is used by SQL DDL command to create an empty Delta table in the above format regardless of whether a table already exists with this name?
options: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE table_name ( employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT )

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE table_name WITH COLUMNS ( employeeId STRING, startDate DATE,
avgRating FLOAT
  ) USING DELTA
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS table_name ( employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT )
CREATE TABLE table_name AS SELECT employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE table_name ( employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT )

Why it is correct: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE creates the table or replaces it if it exists; tables are Delta by default in Databricks.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: WITH COLUMNS is not valid syntax.
  • Option C — CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS table_name ( employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT ) — Why it is incorrect: IF NOT EXISTS does not replace an existing table.
  • Option D — CREATE TABLE table_name AS SELECT employeeId STRING, startDate DATE, avgRating FLOAT — Why it is incorrect: AS SELECT with types is not valid.

q090.stem:
A data engineer has been given a new record of data:

id STRING = 'a1'
rank INTEGER = 6
rating FLOAT = 9.4

Which SQL commands can be used to append the new record to an existing Delta table my_table?
options: INSERT INTO my_table VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4)
INSERT VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4) INTO my_table
UPDATE my_table VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4)
UPDATE VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4) my_table

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: INSERT INTO my_table VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4)

Why it is correct: INSERT INTO table VALUES (…) appends rows.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — INSERT VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4) INTO my_table — Why it is incorrect: the word order is invalid.
  • Option C — UPDATE my_table VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4) — Why it is incorrect: UPDATE modifies existing rows.
  • Option D — UPDATE VALUES ('a1', 6, 9.4) my_table — Why it is incorrect: invalid syntax.

q091.stem: Which command can be used to write data into a Delta table while avoiding the writing of duplicate records?
options: DROP
INSERT
MERGE
APPEND

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: MERGE

Why it is correct: MERGE inserts only rows that do not exist (upsert).

  • Official documentation: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DROP — Why it is incorrect: DROP deletes objects.
  • Option B — INSERT — Why it is incorrect: INSERT does not check duplicates.
  • Option D — APPEND — Why it is incorrect: APPEND adds without checking.

links.t: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE

q092.stem:
A data engineer is attempting to drop a Spark SQL table my_table and runs the following command:

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS my_table;

After running this command, the engineer notices that the data files and metadata files have been deleted from the file system.

What is the reason behind the deletion of all these files?
options: The table was managed
The table's data was smaller than 10 GB
The table did not have a location
The table was external

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: The table was managed

Why it is correct: dropping a managed table also deletes its data.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — The table's data was smaller than 10 GB — Why it is incorrect: size is irrelevant.
  • Option C — The table did not have a location — Why it is incorrect: every table has a location.
  • Option D — The table was external — Why it is incorrect: an external table keeps its data.

q093.stem:
A data engineer needs to create a table in Databricks using data from a CSV file at location /path/to/csv.

They run the following command:

CREATE TABLE new_table
______
OPTIONS (
  header = "true",
  delimiter = "|"
)
LOCATION "path/to/csv"

Which of the following lines of code fills in the above blank to successfully complete the task?
options: FROM "path/to/csv"
USING CSV
FROM CSV
USING DELTA

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: USING CSV

Why it is correct: USING CSV declares the source format; OPTIONS and LOCATION complete the external table over the CSV.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — FROM "path/to/csv" — Why it is incorrect: FROM is not valid in CREATE TABLE with LOCATION.
  • Option C — FROM CSV — Why it is incorrect: FROM CSV is not valid syntax.
  • Option D — USING DELTA — Why it is incorrect: USING DELTA would treat the files as Delta, not CSV.

q094.stem: Which SQL keyword can be used to convert a table from a long format to a wide format?
options: TRANSFORM
PIVOT
SUM
CONVERT

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: PIVOT

Why it is correct: PIVOT turns row values into columns.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — TRANSFORM — Why it is incorrect: TRANSFORM does not pivot.
  • Option C — SUM — Why it is incorrect: SUM is an aggregate.
  • Option D — CONVERT — Why it is incorrect: CONVERT does not pivot.

q095.stem:
A data engineer has a Python variable table_name that they would like to use in a SQL query. They want to construct a Python code block that will run the query using table_name. They have the following incomplete code block:

___(f"SELECT customer_id, spend FROM {table_name}")

What can be used to fill in the blank to successfully complete the task?
options: spark.delta.sql
spark.sql
spark.table
dbutils.sql

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: spark.sql

Why it is correct: spark.sql(f"…") runs a SQL query built with an f-string and returns a DataFrame.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — spark.delta.sql — Why it is incorrect: spark.delta.sql does not exist.
  • Option C — spark.table — Why it is incorrect: spark.table loads a table by name; it does not run a query.
  • Option D — dbutils.sql — Why it is incorrect: dbutils.sql does not exist.

q096.stem: What is used by Spark to record the offset range of the data being processed in each trigger in order for Structured Streaming to reliably track the exact progress of the processing so that it can handle any kind of failure by restarting and/or reprocessing?
options: Checkpointing and Write-ahead Logs
Replayable Sources and Idempotent Sinks
Write-ahead Logs and Idempotent Sinks
Checkpointing and Idempotent Sinks

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Checkpointing and Idempotent Sinks

Why it is correct: checkpointing stores offsets and state; idempotent sinks allow rewrites without duplication, giving exactly-once after failures.

⚠️ Heads-up: Spark docs attribute tracking to "replayable sources + idempotent sinks" and offset logging to write-ahead logs/checkpoint; the options are ambiguous. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Checkpointing and Write-ahead Logs — Why it is incorrect: it lacks the idempotent-write element on the sink side.
  • Option B — Replayable Sources and Idempotent Sinks — Why it is incorrect: replayable sources are needed, but the official option pairs checkpointing with idempotent sinks.
  • Option C — Write-ahead Logs and Idempotent Sinks — Why it is incorrect: write-ahead logs are the internal mechanism; the asked pair is checkpointing + idempotent sinks.

q097.stem: What describes the relationship between Gold tables and Silver tables?
options: Gold tables are more likely to contain aggregations than Silver tables.
Gold tables are more likely to contain valuable data than Silver tables.
Gold tables are more likely to contain a less refined view of data than Silver tables.
Gold tables are more likely to contain truthful data than Silver tables.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Gold tables are more likely to contain aggregations than Silver tables.

Why it is correct: Gold usually holds aggregates and business metrics built on Silver's cleaned data.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Gold tables are more likely to contain valuable data than Silver tables. — Why it is incorrect: "valuable" is not a technical criterion.
  • Option C — Gold tables are more likely to contain a less refined view of data than Silver tables. — Why it is incorrect: it is the other way round: Gold is more refined.
  • Option D — Gold tables are more likely to contain truthful data than Silver tables. — Why it is incorrect: truthfulness is not what sets Gold apart.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q098.stem:
A Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline includes two datasets defined using STREAMING LIVE TABLE. Three datasets are defined against Delta Lake table sources using LIVE TABLE.

The table is configured to run in Production mode using the Continuous Pipeline Mode.

What is the expected outcome after clicking Start to update the pipeline assuming previously unprocessed data exists and all definitions are valid?
options:
All datasets will be updated at set intervals until the pipeline is shut down. The compute resources will persist
to
    allow for additional testing.

All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will persist to allow
for
   additional testing.

All datasets will be updated at set intervals until the pipeline is shut down. The compute resources will be
deployed
   for the update and terminated when the pipeline is stopped.
All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will be terminated.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    All datasets will be updated at set intervals until the pipeline is shut down. The compute resources will be
deployed
   for the update and terminated when the pipeline is stopped.

Why it is correct: in continuous mode the pipeline stays active updating data; in Production mode compute is deployed for the run and released when stopped.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: in Production mode compute does not persist for testing (that is Development).
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: that describes triggered and Development.
  • Option D — All datasets will be updated once and the pipeline will shut down. The compute resources will be terminated. — Why it is incorrect: that describes triggered mode.

q099.stem: Which type of workloads are compatible with Auto Loader?
options: Streaming workloads
Machine learning workloads
Serverless workloads
Batch workloads

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Streaming workloads

Why it is correct: Auto Loader is a Structured Streaming source.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Machine learning workloads — Why it is incorrect: it does not depend on the use case.
  • Option C — Serverless workloads — Why it is incorrect: not a workload-type restriction.
  • Option D — Batch workloads — Why it is incorrect: it can run batch-style with availableNow, but the API is still streaming.

q100.stem: Which query is performing a streaming hop from raw data to a Bronze table?
options:
(spark.table("sales")
   .groupBy("store")

)

(spark.read.load(rawSalesLocation)

)

(spark.table("sales")
    .withColumn("avgPrice", col("sales") / col("units"))
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)

)

(spark.readStream.load(rawSalesLocation)
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpointPath)

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it aggregates with a batch read: a Gold step.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: batch read and write, not streaming.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q101.stem: A single Job runs two notebooks as two separate tasks. A data engineer has noticed that one of the notebooks is running slowly in the Job’s current run. The data engineer asks a tech lead for help in identifying why this might be the case. Which approach can the tech lead use to identify why the notebook is running slowly as part of the Job?
options: They can navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI to immediately review the processing notebook.

They can navigate to the Tasks tab in the Jobs UI and click on the active run to review the processing
notebook.

They can navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI and click on the active run to review the processing
notebook.
They can navigate to the Tasks tab in the Jobs UI to immediately review the processing notebook.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    They can navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI and click on the active run to review the processing
notebook.

Why it is correct: executions are found in the Runs tab; opening the active run shows the notebook and its progress.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI to immediately review the processing notebook. — Why it is incorrect: you must open the active run; it is not shown "immediately".
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: the Tasks tab defines tasks, not runs.
  • Option D — They can navigate to the Tasks tab in the Jobs UI to immediately review the processing notebook. — Why it is incorrect: the Tasks tab shows the definition, not the ongoing run.

q102.stem:
A data analysis team has noticed that their Databricks SQL queries are running too slowly when connected to their always- on SQL warehouse. They claim that this issue is present when many members of the team are running small queries

simultaneously. They ask the data engineering team for help. The data engineering team notices that each of the team’s queries uses the same SQL warehouse.

Which approach can the data engineering team use to improve the latency of the team’s queries?
options: They can increase the cluster size of the SQL endpoint.
They can increase the maximum bound of the SQL warehouse’s scaling range.
They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL endpoint.
They can turn on the Serverless feature for the SQL endpoint.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: They can increase the maximum bound of the SQL warehouse’s scaling range.

Why it is correct: the problem is concurrency: raising the maximum clusters in the scaling range lets more queries run at once.

  • Official documentation: SQL warehouses - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can increase the cluster size of the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: it helps large queries, not concurrency.
  • Option C — They can turn on the Auto Stop feature for the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: Auto Stop does not improve latency.
  • Option D — They can turn on the Serverless feature for the SQL endpoint. — Why it is incorrect: serverless helps start-up, not concurrency with an already running warehouse.

q103.stem:
A data engineer has been using a Databricks SQL dashboard to monitor the cleanliness of the input data to an ELT job. The ELT job has its Databricks SQL query that returns the number of input records containing unexpected NULL values. The data engineer wants their entire team to be notified via a messaging webhook whenever this value reaches 100.

Which approach can the data engineer use to notify their entire team via a messaging webhook whenever the number of NULL values reaches 100?
options: They can set up an Alert with a custom template.
They can set up an Alert with a new email alert destination.
They can set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.
They can set up an Alert with one-time notifications.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: They can set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.

Why it is correct: an alert with a webhook destination notifies the team in the messaging tool when the threshold is met.

  • Official documentation: Databricks SQL - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — They can set up an Alert with a custom template. — Why it is incorrect: a template changes the text, not the channel.
  • Option B — They can set up an Alert with a new email alert destination. — Why it is incorrect: email is not a webhook.
  • Option D — They can set up an Alert with one-time notifications. — Why it is incorrect: one-time does not cover recurring monitoring.

q104.stem:
A company uses OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) to collaborate with partners across different cloud providers and geographic regions.

What will result in additional costs due to cross-region or egress fees?
options: Sharing data within the same cloud provider and region

Transferring data via OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) across clouds and across different geographic
regions
Accessing Delta Sharing data using a VPN within the same data center
Utilizing Delta Sharing for internal data analytics within a single cloud environment

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Transferring data via OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) across clouds and across different geographic
regions

Why it is correct: cross-cloud or cross-region transfer incurs cloud-provider egress charges.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Sharing data within the same cloud provider and region — Why it is incorrect: within the same region there is normally no egress.
  • Option C — Accessing Delta Sharing data using a VPN within the same data center — Why it is incorrect: inside the same data center there is no cross-region egress.
  • Option D — Utilizing Delta Sharing for internal data analytics within a single cloud environment — Why it is incorrect: within one environment there is no cross-cloud egress.

q105.stem:
A data engineer is writing a script that is meant to ingest new data from cloud storage. In the event of the Schema change, the ingestion should fail. It should fail until the changes downstream source can be found and verified as intended changes.

Which command will meet the requirements?
options: failOnNewColumns
none
rescue
addNewColumns

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: failOnNewColumns

Why it is correct: failOnNewColumns (an Auto Loader schema evolution mode) fails the stream when new columns appear, until the schema is updated.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — none — Why it is incorrect: none ignores new columns without failing.
  • Option C — rescue — Why it is incorrect: rescue stores new data in _rescued_data without failing.
  • Option D — addNewColumns — Why it is incorrect: addNewColumns fails once and then adds the columns automatically.

q106.stem: Which SQL code snippet will correctly demonstrate a Data Definition Language (DDL) operation used to create a table?
options: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name STRING);
DROP TABLE employees;
ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN salary DECIMAL(10,2);
INSERT INTO employees (id, name) VALUES (1 'Alice');

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name STRING);

Why it is correct: CREATE TABLE is creation DDL.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — DROP TABLE employees; — Why it is incorrect: DROP TABLE deletes.
  • Option C — ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN salary DECIMAL(10,2); — Why it is incorrect: ALTER TABLE modifies.
  • Option D — INSERT INTO employees (id, name) VALUES (1 'Alice'); — Why it is incorrect: INSERT is DML, and is mistyped.

q107.stem:
A data engineer is working in a Databricks notebook to design and manage a batch ETL pipeline. The engineer is writing SQL and Python code to clean data, transform it, and join large datasets from different sources. The engineer wants to organize these steps into a structured process that can be run regularly and scheduled as part of a data pipeline.

Which Databricks notebook feature is applicable in the use case?
options: Real-time streaming support
Collaborative editing
Task workflows and job scheduling
Notebook version control

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Task workflows and job scheduling

Why it is correct: task workflows and job scheduling organize and run the steps on a regular basis.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Real-time streaming support — Why it is incorrect: not what is asked.
  • Option B — Collaborative editing — Why it is incorrect: collaboration does not schedule runs.
  • Option D — Notebook version control — Why it is incorrect: versioning does not run the process.

q108.stem:
A data engineer needs to develop integration tests for an ETL process and deploy a version-controlled, packaged workflow into production using an external job scheduler.

Which tool should the data engineer use for this job?
options: Databricks Connect
Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles)
Databricks Command Line Interface
Databricks Software Development Kit

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles)

Why it is correct: bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) package jobs, pipelines and configuration as version-controlled YAML and deploy via the CLI.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks Connect — Why it is incorrect: it runs Spark code from an IDE; it does not package or deploy workflows.
  • Option C — Databricks Command Line Interface — Why it is incorrect: the CLI runs commands but does not define the versioned package by itself.
  • Option D — Databricks Software Development Kit — Why it is incorrect: the SDK is a programming API; it does not package workflows.

q109.stem: Which Databricks asset bundle format is valid?
options:
resources:
  jobs:
    hello-job:
      name: hello-job
      tasks:
        - task_key: hello-task
          existing_cluster_id: 1234-567890-abcde123
          notebook_task:

{"resources":{"jobs":{"name":"hello-job","tasks":{"task_key":"hello-task","existing_cluster_id":"1234-567890-abcde123","notebook_task":{"notebook_path":".hello.py"}}}}}
configuration = {"resources":{"jobs":{"name":"hello-job","tasks":{"task_key":"hello-task","existing_cluster_id":"1234-567890-abcde123","notebook_task":{"notebook_path":".hello.py"}}}}}
resources { jobs { name = "hello-job" tasks { task_key = "hello-task" existing_cluster_id = "1234-567890-abcde123" notebook_task { notebook_path = ".hello.py" } } } }

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A:

  jobs:
    hello-job:

      tasks:

          existing_cluster_id: 1234-567890-abcde123

Why it is correct: bundles are defined in YAML files: resources → jobs → job name → tasks.

⚠️ Heads-up: the original PDF loses the YAML indentation; the correct format of option A has been reconstructed. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — {"resources":{"jobs":{"name":"hello-job","tasks":{"task_key":"hello-task","existing_cluster_id":"1234-567890-abcde123","notebook_task":{"notebook_path":".hello.py"}}}}} — Why it is incorrect: JSON with an invalid structure: the job key and tasks must be YAML maps/lists.
  • Option C — configuration = {"resources":{"jobs":{"name":"hello-job","tasks":{"task_key":"hello-task","existing_cluster_id":"1234-567890-abcde123","notebook_task":{"notebook_path":".hello.py"}}}}} — Why it is incorrect: a Python assignment is not a bundle.
  • Option D — resources { jobs { name = "hello-job" tasks { task_key = "hello-task" existing_cluster_id = "1234-567890-abcde123" notebook_task { notebook_path = ".hello.py" } } } } — Why it is incorrect: HCL/Terraform-like syntax, not YAML.

q110.stem:
A data engineer needs to ingest from both streaming and batch sources for a firm that relies on highly accurate data. Occasionally, some of the data picked up by the sensors that provide a streaming input are outside the expected parameters. If this occurs, the data must be dropped, but the stream should not fail.

Which feature of Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) meets this requirement?
options: Change Data Capture
Error Handling
Monitoring
Expectations

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Expectations

Why it is correct: expectations with ON VIOLATION DROP ROW drop invalid records without failing the pipeline.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Change Data Capture — Why it is incorrect: CDC applies source changes; it does not validate quality.
  • Option B — Error Handling — Why it is incorrect: it is not a declarative quality feature.
  • Option C — Monitoring — Why it is incorrect: it monitors; it does not drop data.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q111.stem:
A data engineer has inherited a Databricks pipeline from a previous team. The pipeline is missing SLAs and costs more than the allotted budget. On analysis, it is noted that the cluster is not being fully utilized, and the dataset is getting skewed.

How should the data engineer resolve this issue?
options: Use coalesce() on the dataset to merge partitions and reduce skew.
Increase the number of executors for the job.
Repartition the dataset to have it be more optimally spread across all nodes.
Increase the executor memory for the job.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Repartition the dataset to have it be more optimally spread across all nodes.

Why it is correct: repartition() redistributes data evenly across partitions/nodes, fixing the skew and using the cluster fully.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use coalesce() on the dataset to merge partitions and reduce skew. — Why it is incorrect: coalesce() reduces partitions without a shuffle and can worsen imbalance.
  • Option B — Increase the number of executors for the job. — Why it is incorrect: more executors do not fix a few partitions concentrating the work (and raise cost).
  • Option D — Increase the executor memory for the job. — Why it is incorrect: more memory does not fix the imbalance and raises cost.

q112.stem:
An organization is looking for an optimized storage layer that supports ACID transactions and schema enforcement.

Which technology should the organization use?
options: Delta Lake
Unity Catalog
Cloud File Storage
Data lake

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Delta Lake

Why it is correct: Delta Lake provides ACID transactions and schema enforcement on top of cloud storage.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Unity Catalog — Why it is incorrect: governance and permissions, not transactional storage.
  • Option C — Cloud File Storage — Why it is incorrect: it stores files without ACID or schema.
  • Option D — Data lake — Why it is incorrect: a data lake without a transactional layer offers no ACID.

q113.stem: What are the transformations typically included in building the Bronze layer?
options: Include columns Load date/time, process ID
Business rules and transformations
Perform extensive data cleansing
Aggregate data from multiple sources

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Include columns Load date/time, process ID

Why it is correct: Bronze keeps raw data and only adds technical metadata (load date, process ID, source).

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Business rules and transformations — Why it is incorrect: business rules are applied in Silver/Gold.
  • Option C — Perform extensive data cleansing — Why it is incorrect: extensive cleansing belongs to Silver.
  • Option D — Aggregate data from multiple sources — Why it is incorrect: aggregation belongs to Gold.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q114.stem:
An organization has data stored across multiple external systems, including MySQL, Amazon Redshift, and Google BigQuery. The data engineer wants to perform analytics without ingesting directly into Databricks, ensuring unified governance and minimizing data duplication.

Which feature of Databricks enables querying these external data sources while maintaining centralized governance?
options: Delta Lake
Lakehouse Federation
MLflow
Databricks Connect

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Lakehouse Federation

Why it is correct: Lakehouse Federation queries external systems from Unity Catalog without migrating data.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Delta Lake — Why it is incorrect: it is a table format; it does not federate external sources.
  • Option C — MLflow — Why it is incorrect: MLflow manages the ML lifecycle.
  • Option D — Databricks Connect — Why it is incorrect: it connects local IDEs to clusters.

q115.stem:
An organization needs to share a dataset stored in its Databricks Unity Catalog with an external partner who uses a different data platform that is not Databricks. The goal is to maintain data security and ensure the partner can access the data efficiently.

Which method should the data engineer use to securely share the dataset with the external partner?
options: Using OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) with the open sharing protocol
Exporting data as CSV files and emailing them
Using a third-party API to access the Delta table
Databricks-to-Databricks Sharing

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Using OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) with the open sharing protocol

Why it is correct: Delta Sharing/OpenSharing is an open protocol for sharing with recipients that do not use Databricks, with governed permissions.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Exporting data as CSV files and emailing them — Why it is incorrect: insecure and inefficient.
  • Option C — Using a third-party API to access the Delta table — Why it is incorrect: not a governed sharing method.
  • Option D — Databricks-to-Databricks Sharing — Why it is incorrect: it requires the recipient to use Databricks.

q116.stem: A data engineer streams customer orders into a Kafka topic (orders_topic) and is currently writing the ingestion script of a Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline. The data engineer needs to ingest the data from Kafka brokers to Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines using Databricks. What is the correct code for ingesting the data?
options:
from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.table(
  name = "orders_raw",
)
def orders_raw():
  return (
     spark.readStream
        .format("kafka")
        .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "broker:9092")
        .option("subscribe", "orders_topic")
        .option("startingOffsets", "earliest")
        .load()
  )

@dlt.table(
  name = "orders_raw",
)
def orders_raw():
  return (
     spark.readStream
        .format("cloud_files")
        .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
        .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", "/schema/location")
        .load("kafka://broker:9092/orders_topic")
  )

CREATE LIVE TABLE orders_raw
AS SELECT
  CAST(value AS STRING) AS json_data
FROM STREAM kafka.broker:9092/orders_topic;

CREATE STREAMING LIVE TABLE orders_raw
AS SELECT
  value:order_id AS order_id,
  value:customer_id AS customer_id,
  value:amount AS amount,
  value:order_status AS order_status,
  value:order_timestamp AS order_timestamp
FROM cloud_files("kafka://broker:9092/orders_topic", "json");

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A:
