  name = "orders_raw",
)
def orders_raw():
  return (
     spark.readStream
        .format("kafka")
        .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "broker:9092")
        .option("subscribe", "orders_topic")
        .option("startingOffsets", "earliest")
        .load()
  )

Why it is correct: a streaming table is defined with @dp.table reading Kafka via spark.readStream.format("kafka"), kafka.bootstrap.servers, subscribe and startingOffsets.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it uses cloud_files/cloudFiles (for files) with a non-existent kafka:// URL.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: FROM STREAM kafka.broker… is not valid Kafka syntax.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: cloud_files reads files, not Kafka.

q117.stem:
A global retail company sells products across multiple categories (e.g., Electronics, Clothing) and regions (e.g., North, South, East, West). The sales team has provided the data engineer with a PySpark dataframe named sales_df as below and the team wants the data engineer to analyze the sales data to help them make strategic decisions.

sales_df

product_id  category     sales_amount  region
1           Electronics  100           North
2           Clothing     200           South
3           Electronics  150           North
4           Clothing     300           South
5           Electronics  250           East
6           Clothing     400           West

Calculate the total sales amount for each product category and store the results in a new dataframe called category_sales.

What will generate the expected result of category_sales?

category     total_sales_amount
Electronics  500
Clothing     900
options: category_sales = sales_df.groupBy("category").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount"))
category_sales = sales_df.sum("sales_amount").groupBy("category").alias("total_sales_amount")
category_sales = sales_df.agg(sum("sales_amount").groupBy("category").alias("total_sales_amount"))
category_sales = sales_df.groupBy("region").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount"))

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: category_sales = sales_df.groupBy("category").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount"))

Why it is correct: groupBy("category").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias(…)) aggregates by category: Electronics 500, Clothing 900.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — category_sales = sales_df.sum("sales_amount").groupBy("category").alias("total_sales_amount") — Why it is incorrect: sum first and then groupBy: invalid order.
  • Option C — category_sales = sales_df.agg(sum("sales_amount").groupBy("category").alias("total_sales_amount")) — Why it is incorrect: sum(...).groupBy(...) inside agg is invalid.
  • Option D — category_sales = sales_df.groupBy("region").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount")) — Why it is incorrect: it groups by region, not category.

q118.stem:
A data engineer is designing an ETL pipeline to process both streaming and batch data from multiple sources. The pipeline must ensure data quality, handle schema evolution, and provide easy maintenance. The team is considering using Delta Live Tables (DLT) in Databricks to achieve these goals. They want to understand the key features and benefits of DLT that make it suitable for this use case.

Why is Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) an appropriate choice?
options: Automatic data quality checks, built-in support for schema evolution, and declarative pipeline development
Manual schema enforcement, high operational overhead, and limited scalability

Requires custom code for data quality checks, no support for streaming data, and complex pipeline
maintenance
Supports only batch processing, no data versioning, and high infrastructure costs

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Automatic data quality checks, built-in support for schema evolution, and declarative pipeline development

Why it is correct: it offers quality expectations, schema evolution and a declarative model, and handles both streaming and batch.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Manual schema enforcement, high operational overhead, and limited scalability — Why it is incorrect: it inverts the benefits.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it does support streaming and quality is declarative.
  • Option D — Supports only batch processing, no data versioning, and high infrastructure costs — Why it is incorrect: it supports batch and streaming and versions through Delta.

q119.stem: A data engineer is attempting to write Python and SQL in the same command cell and is running into an error. The engineer thought that it was possible to use a Python variable in a select statement. Why does the command fail?
options: Databricks supports language interoperability in the same cell but only between Scala and SQL.
Databricks supports multiple languages but only one per notebook.
Databricks supports one language per cell.
Databricks supports language interoperability but only if a special character is used.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Databricks supports one language per cell.

Why it is correct: each cell uses a single language (the default or that of the magic command).

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks supports language interoperability in the same cell but only between Scala and SQL. — Why it is incorrect: there is no such Scala/SQL limitation.
  • Option B — Databricks supports multiple languages but only one per notebook. — Why it is incorrect: multiple languages can be used in a notebook, one per cell.
  • Option D — Databricks supports language interoperability but only if a special character is used. — Why it is incorrect: no special character mixes languages in one cell.

q120.stem: Which compute option should be chosen in a scenario where small-scale ad-hoc Python scripts need to be run at high frequency and should wind down quickly after these queries have finished running?
options: All-purpose Cluster
Job Cluster
Serverless Compute
SQL Warehouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Serverless Compute

Why it is correct: serverless compute provisions almost instantly and releases when finished, ideal for small, frequent workloads.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — All-purpose Cluster — Why it is incorrect: it stays on and is costlier for this.
  • Option B — Job Cluster — Why it is incorrect: it has a start-up delay on every run.
  • Option D — SQL Warehouse — Why it is incorrect: it runs SQL, not Python scripts.

q121.stem:
A data engineer is working on a personal laptop and needs to perform complex transformations on data stored in a Delta Lake on cloud storage. The engineer decides to use Databricks Connect to interact with Databricks clusters and work in their local IDE.

How does Databricks Connect enable the engineer to develop, test, and debug code seamlessly on their local machine while interacting with Databricks clusters?
options:
By providing a local environment that mimics the Databricks runtime, enabling the engineer to develop, test,
and
   debug code using a specific IDE that is required by Databricks

By providing a local environment that mimics the Databricks runtime, enabling the engineer to develop, test,
and
   debug code only through Databricks’ own web interface
By allowing direct execution of Spark jobs from the local machine without needing a network connection

By providing a local environment that mimics the Databricks runtime, enabling the engineer to develop, test,
and
   debug code using their preferred IDE

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    By providing a local environment that mimics the Databricks runtime, enabling the engineer to develop, test,
and
   debug code using their preferred IDE

Why it is correct: Databricks Connect lets you use any local IDE while the Spark code runs on remote Databricks compute.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it does not require a specific IDE.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: the point is to work outside the web UI.
  • Option C — By allowing direct execution of Spark jobs from the local machine without needing a network connection — Why it is incorrect: it needs a network connection to the remote compute.

q122.stem:
A company sells products across multiple categories (e.g., Electronics, Clothing) and regions. The sales team has provided you with a PySpark dataframe named sales_df as below, and the team wants the data engineer to analyze the sales data to help make strategic decisions.

sales_df

product_id  category     sales_amount  region
1           Electronics  100           North
2           Clothing     200           South
3           Electronics  150           North
4           Clothing     300           South
5           Electronics  250           East
6           Clothing     400           West

Calculate the total sales amount for each region and store the results in a new dataframe called region_sales.

Given the expected result:

region  total_sales_amount
North   250
South   500
East    250
West    400

Which code will generate the expected result?
options: region_sales = sales_df.groupBy("category").sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount")
region_sales = sales_df.groupBy("region").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount"))
region_sales = sales_df.sum("sales_amount").groupBy("region").alias("total_sales_amount")
region_sales = sales_df.agg(sum("sales_amount").groupBy("region").alias("total_sales_amount"))

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: region_sales = sales_df.groupBy("region").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount"))

Why it is correct: groupBy("region").agg(sum("sales_amount").alias(…)) sums by region.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — region_sales = sales_df.groupBy("category").sum("sales_amount").alias("total_sales_amount") — Why it is incorrect: it groups by category, not region.
  • Option C — region_sales = sales_df.sum("sales_amount").groupBy("region").alias("total_sales_amount") — Why it is incorrect: the sum → groupBy order is invalid.
  • Option D — region_sales = sales_df.agg(sum("sales_amount").groupBy("region").alias("total_sales_amount")) — Why it is incorrect: sum(...).groupBy(...) inside agg is invalid.

q123.stem:
A Data Engineer is building a simple data pipeline using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (antes Delta Live Tables) in Databricks to ingest customer data. The raw customer data is stored in a cloud storage location in JSON format. The task is to create a Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline that reads the raw JSON data and writes it into a Delta table for further processing.

Which code snippet will correctly ingest the raw JSON data and create a Delta table using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines?
options:
from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.materialized_view
def raw_customers():
   return spark.read.format('csv').load('s3://my-bucket/raw-customers/')

from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.materialized_view
def raw_customers():
   return spark.format.json('s3://my-bucket/raw-customers/')

from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.materialized_view
def raw_customers():
  return spark.read.json('s3://my-bucket/raw-customers/')

from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.materialized_view
def raw_customers():
  return spark.read.format('parquet').load('s3://my-bucket/raw-customers/')

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    from pyspark import pipelines as dp
@dp.materialized_view
def raw_customers():
  return spark.read.json('s3://my-bucket/raw-customers/')

Why it is correct: @dp.materialized_view with spark.read.json(…) reads the JSON and creates the Delta dataset.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it reads CSV, not JSON.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: spark.format.json does not exist.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it reads Parquet, not JSON.

q124.stem:
A data engineering team is using Kafka to capture event data and then ingest it into Databricks. The team wants to be able to see these historical events. Medallion architecture is already in place. The team wants to be mindful of costs.

Where should this historical event data be stored?
options: Gold
Silver
Bronze
Raw layer

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Bronze

Why it is correct: Bronze stores events as they arrive, with the full history at low cost and without transformations.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Gold — Why it is incorrect: Gold is for aggregated consumption data.
  • Option B — Silver — Why it is incorrect: Silver holds cleansed, transformed data.
  • Option D — Raw layer — Why it is incorrect: in medallion the landing layer is Bronze; "raw" is not a table layer.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q125.stem: What is the maximum output supported by a job cluster to ensure a notebook does not fail?
options: 25MBs
10MBs
30MBs
15MBs

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 30MBs

Why it is correct: per the bank key, 30 MB.

⚠️ Heads-up: current Jobs documentation mentions a 20 MB limit for notebook cell output in a job (and 1 MB for the exit value), so this 30 MB key may be outdated or incorrect. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — 25MBs — Why it is incorrect: the limit is not 25 MB.
  • Option B — 10MBs — Why it is incorrect: the limit is not 10 MB.
  • Option D — 15MBs — Why it is incorrect: the limit is not 15 MB.

q126.stem: Which two items are characteristics of the Gold Layer? (Choose two.)
options: Historical lineage
Raw Data
Normalised
De-normalised
Read-optimized

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option D: De-normalised
  • Option E: Read-optimized

Why it is correct: Gold is modeled denormalized and read-optimized (for reports and dashboards).

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Historical lineage — Why it is incorrect: historical lineage belongs to earlier layers (Bronze).
  • Option B — Raw Data — Why it is incorrect: raw data is in Bronze.
  • Option C — Normalised — Why it is incorrect: normalization is more typical of Silver.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q127.stem:
A data engineer has developed an ETL that produce a Delta managed table with liquid clustering feature activated as output. Several consumers are having issues regarding time delay when reading this table.

How could the Data Engineer be sure about the OPTIMIZE command has been executed explicitly?
options: Check the system table system.storage.predictive_optimization_operations_history
Use SHOW TABLES EXTENDED to check the partitions columns used
Use DESCRIBE DETAIL table to see the file size and number of files for the table
Use DESCRIBE HISTORY table to check if exists any OPTIMIZE operation

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Use DESCRIBE HISTORY table to check if exists any OPTIMIZE operation

Why it is correct: DESCRIBE HISTORY lists the table's operations, including executed OPTIMIZE runs.

  • Official documentation: Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks | Optimize data file layout (OPTIMIZE) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Check the system table system.storage.predictive_optimization_operations_history — Why it is incorrect: it shows automatic predictive optimizations, not explicit runs.
  • Option B — Use SHOW TABLES EXTENDED to check the partitions columns used — Why it is incorrect: it does not show executed operations.
  • Option C — Use DESCRIBE DETAIL table to see the file size and number of files for the table — Why it is incorrect: it shows state, not operation history.

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q128.stem: A data engineer is reviewing the documentation on audit logs in Databricks for compliance purposes and needs to understand the format in which audit logs output events. How are events formatted in Databricks audit logs?
options: In Databricks, audit logs output events in a JSON format.
In Databricks, audit logs output events in a CSV format.
In Databricks, audit logs output events in an XML format.
In Databricks, audit logs output events in a plain text format.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: In Databricks, audit logs output events in a JSON format.

Why it is correct: audit logs emit events in JSON.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — In Databricks, audit logs output events in a CSV format. — Why it is incorrect: not CSV.
  • Option C — In Databricks, audit logs output events in an XML format. — Why it is incorrect: not XML.
  • Option D — In Databricks, audit logs output events in a plain text format. — Why it is incorrect: not plain text.

q129.stem:
A Python file is ready to go into production and the client wants to use the cheapest but most efficient type of cluster possible. The workload is quite small, only processing 10GBs of data with only simple joins and no complex aggregations or wide transformations.

Which cluster meets the requirement?
options: Interactive cluster
Job cluster with spot instances enabled
Job cluster with spot instances disabled
Job cluster with Photon enabled

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Job cluster with spot instances enabled

Why it is correct: a job cluster is created and destroyed per run, and spot instances cut cost on small, retry-tolerant workloads.

⚠️ Heads-up: spot can be preempted; it is valid only if the job tolerates retries. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Interactive cluster — Why it is incorrect: an interactive cluster is costlier for production.
  • Option C — Job cluster with spot instances disabled — Why it is incorrect: without spot it costs more.
  • Option D — Job cluster with Photon enabled — Why it is incorrect: Photon speeds up heavy workloads but does not cut cost for a small one.

q130.stem:
A data engineer is working on a Databricks project that utilizes cloud storage. The data engineer wants to load several JSON files from containers on a storage account as soon as the file arrives within the storage account.

Which syntax should the data engineer follow to first load the files into a dataframe and check that it is working as expected using Python?
options: df = spark.read.json("input/path")
df = spark.readStream.format("cloud").option("json").load("/input/path")
df = spark.readStream.format("json").load("input/path")
df = spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "json").load("/input/path")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: df = spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "json").load("/input/path")

Why it is correct: readStream.format("cloudFiles") with cloudFiles.format = json uses Auto Loader to ingest files as they arrive.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — df = spark.read.json("input/path") — Why it is incorrect: spark.read is batch and does not detect new files.
  • Option B — df = spark.readStream.format("cloud").option("json").load("/input/path") — Why it is incorrect: format("cloud") and option("json") are not valid.
  • Option C — df = spark.readStream.format("json").load("input/path") — Why it is incorrect: format("json") streaming requires a schema and lacks Auto Loader discovery.

q131.stem:
A data engineer team has decided to implement a new data platform on Databricks and is currently deciding how to store each kind of data on each data layer.

What is the appropriate layer and data pairing for medallion architecture?
options: Silver Layer - Raw data from deposit account application
Bronze Layer - Summary of cash deposit amount for each country and city
Silver Layer - Cleansed master customer data
Gold Layer - Deduplicated money transfer transaction

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Silver Layer - Cleansed master customer data

Why it is correct: cleansed master data belongs in Silver (cleaned, conformed data).

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Silver Layer - Raw data from deposit account application — Why it is incorrect: raw data goes to Bronze.
  • Option B — Bronze Layer - Summary of cash deposit amount for each country and city — Why it is incorrect: an aggregated summary is Gold.
  • Option D — Gold Layer - Deduplicated money transfer transaction — Why it is incorrect: deduplication is a Silver task.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q132.stem: A data engineer is processing ingested streaming tables and needs to filter out NULL values in the order_datetime column from the raw streaming table orders_raw and store the results in a new table orders_valid using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines. Which code snippet should the data engineer use?
options:
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE orders_valid(
   CONSTRAINT valid_date
   EXPECT (order_datetime IS NOT NULL)
   ON VIOLATION DROP ROW
)
AS SELECT * FROM STREAM orders_raw;

CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE orders_valid
(
    CONSTRAINT valid_date EXPECT (order_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    ON VIOLATION DROP ROW
)
AS SELECT * FROM orders_raw;

CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE orders_valid
AS
SELECT *
FROM STREAM(orders_raw)
WHERE order_datetime IS NOT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE STREAMING TABLE orders_valid
(
    FILTER (order_datetime IS NOT NULL)
)
AS SELECT * FROM STREAM(orders_raw);

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE orders_valid
AS
SELECT *
FROM STREAM(orders_raw)
WHERE order_datetime IS NOT NULL;

Why it is correct: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE … AS SELECT … FROM STREAM(orders_raw) WHERE order_datetime IS NOT NULL filters nulls reading as a stream.

⚠️ Heads-up: option B (with a DROP ROW expectation) would also filter nulls if it read with STREAM(); the official key is C. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Streaming tables - Databricks | Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: the CONSTRAINT goes after the name; it is misplaced here and STREAM orders_raw without parentheses is invalid.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it reads orders_raw without STREAM(), i.e. as batch.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: FILTER is not a valid clause there.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q133.stem:
A data engineer is managing a data pipeline in Databricks, where multiple Delta tables are used for various transformations. The team wants to track how data flows through the pipeline, including identifying dependencies between Delta tables, notebooks, jobs, and dashboards. The data engineer is utilizing the Unity Catalog lineage feature to monitor this process.

How does Unity Catalog’s data lineage feature support the visualization of relationships between Delta tables, notebooks, jobs, and dashboards?
options:
Unity Catalog lineage visualizes dependencies between Delta tables, notebooks, and jobs, but does not
provide
    column-level tracing or relationships with dashboards.

Unity Catalog lineage only supports visualizing relationships at the table level and does not extend to
notebooks,
    jobs, or dashboards.

Unity Catalog lineage provides an interactive graph that tracks dependencies between tables and notebook
but
   excludes any job-related dependencies or dashboard visualizations.

Unity Catalog provides an interactive graph that visualizes the dependencies between Delta tables,
notebooks, jobs,
   and dashboards, while also supporting column-level tracking of data transformations.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    Unity Catalog provides an interactive graph that visualizes the dependencies between Delta tables,
notebooks, jobs,
   and dashboards, while also supporting column-level tracking of data transformations.

Why it is correct: Unity Catalog captures table- and column-level lineage across tables, notebooks, jobs and dashboards, shown in an interactive graph.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: it does support columns and dashboards.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it also covers notebooks, jobs and dashboards.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it also includes jobs and dashboards.

q134.stem:
A data engineer is configuring Unity Catalog in Databricks and needs to assign a role to a user who should have the ability to grant and revoke privileges on various data objects within a specific schema, but should not have read/write access over the schema or its objects.

Which role should the data engineer assign to this user?
options: Table Owner
Catalog Owner
Schema Owner
USE catalog/schema privilege on the schema

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Schema Owner

Why it is correct: the schema owner can grant and revoke privileges on the schema's objects.

⚠️ Heads-up: a schema owner also implicitly controls its objects; the key is accepted as the best available option (current documentation also has the MANAGE privilege). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Table Owner — Why it is incorrect: it only manages that table.
  • Option B — Catalog Owner — Why it is incorrect: it covers the whole catalog, more than asked.
  • Option D — USE catalog/schema privilege on the schema — Why it is incorrect: USE does not allow granting privileges.

q135.stem:
A data engineer is debugging a Python notebook in Databricks that processes a dataset using PySpark. The notebook fails with an error during a DataFrame transformation. The engineer wants to inspect the state of variables, such as the input DataFrame and intermediate results, to identify where the error occurs.

Which tool should the engineer use to debug the notebook and inspect the values of variables like DataFrames?
options: Use the Databricks CLI to download and analyze driver logs for detailed error messages
Use the Python Notebook Interactive Debugger to set breakpoints and inspect variable values in real-time
Use the Ganglia UI to monitor cluster resource usage and identify hardware issues
Use the Spark UI to analyze the execution plan and identify stages where the job failed

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Use the Python Notebook Interactive Debugger to set breakpoints and inspect variable values in real-time

Why it is correct: the interactive debugger supports breakpoints and step-by-step inspection of variables and DataFrames.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use the Databricks CLI to download and analyze driver logs for detailed error messages — Why it is incorrect: logs give error messages but do not inspect variables.
  • Option C — Use the Ganglia UI to monitor cluster resource usage and identify hardware issues — Why it is incorrect: Ganglia monitors resources, not variables.
  • Option D — Use the Spark UI to analyze the execution plan and identify stages where the job failed — Why it is incorrect: the Spark UI shows plans and stages, not variable values.

q136.stem:
A data engineer wants to create an external table in Databricks that references data stored in an Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) location. The goal is to enable Databricks to access and query this external data without moving it into the Databricks-managed storage.

Which step should the data engineer take to successfully create the external table?
options:
Use the CREATE MANAGED TABLE statement and specify the LOCATION clause with the path to the
external data.
CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE statement without specifying a LOCATION clause.
Use the CREATE TABLE statement and specify the LOCATION clause with the path to the external data.
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement without specifying a LOCATION clause.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Use the CREATE TABLE statement and specify the LOCATION clause with the path to the external data.

Why it is correct: CREATE TABLE … LOCATION 'path' creates an external table pointing at the data without moving it.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: a managed table takes no own LOCATION and CREATE MANAGED TABLE does not exist.
  • Option B — CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE statement without specifying a LOCATION clause. — Why it is incorrect: CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE does not exist and without LOCATION there is no path.
  • Option D — CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement without specifying a LOCATION clause. — Why it is incorrect: without LOCATION it does not know where the data is.

q137.stem:
A data engineer is developing a small proof of concept in a notebook. When running the entire notebook, the Cluster usage spikes. The data engineer wants to keep the development requirements and get real-time results.

Which Cluster meets these requirements?
options: All Purpose Cluster with autoscaling
Job Cluster with Photon enabled and autoscaling
Job Cluster with autoscaling enabled
All-Purpose Cluster with a large fixed memory size

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: All Purpose Cluster with autoscaling

Why it is correct: an all-purpose cluster supports interactive development and immediate results; autoscaling absorbs spikes.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Job Cluster with Photon enabled and autoscaling — Why it is incorrect: a job cluster is not interactive.
  • Option C — Job Cluster with autoscaling enabled — Why it is incorrect: a job cluster is not interactive.
  • Option D — All-Purpose Cluster with a large fixed memory size — Why it is incorrect: large fixed memory is costlier and does not scale.

q138.stem:
A data engineer needs to process SQL queries on a large dataset with fluctuating workloads. The workload requires automatic scaling based on the volume of queries, without the need to manage or provision infrastructure. The solution should be cost-efficient and charge only for the compute resources used during query execution.

Which compute option should the data engineer use?
options: Databricks SQL Analytics
Databricks Runtime for ML
Databricks Jobs
Serverless SQL Warehouse

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Serverless SQL Warehouse

Why it is correct: a serverless SQL warehouse scales automatically, needs no infrastructure management and bills by usage.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks | SQL warehouses - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Databricks SQL Analytics — Why it is incorrect: it is the general product name; it does not guarantee serverless pay-per-use compute.
  • Option B — Databricks Runtime for ML — Why it is incorrect: it is an ML runtime.
  • Option C — Databricks Jobs — Why it is incorrect: it orchestrates tasks; it does not serve BI SQL queries.

q139.stem: What is the functionality of AutoLoader in Databricks?
options:
Auto Loader automatically ingests and processes new files from cloud storage, handling both batch and
streaming
   data with support for schema evolution.

Auto Loader automatically ingests and processes new files from cloud storage, handling batch and streaming
data
   with no support for schema evolution.

Auto Loader automatically ingests and processes new files from cloud storage, handling only streaming data
with no
   support for schema evolution.

Auto Loader automatically ingests and processes new files from cloud storage, handling batch data with
support for
   schema evolution.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Auto Loader automatically ingests and processes new files from cloud storage, handling both batch and
streaming
   data with support for schema evolution.

Why it is correct: Auto Loader detects new files, works in streaming and batch-style (availableNow) modes and supports schema evolution.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it does support schema evolution.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it is not streaming-only and does support evolution.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it is not limited to batch.

q140.stem:
A company is collaborating with a partner that does not use Databricks but needs access to a large historical dataset stored in Delta format. The data engineer needs to ensure that the partner can access the data securely, without the need for them to set up an account, and with read-only access.

How should the data be shared?
options: Share the dataset by exporting it to a CSV file and manually transferring the file to the partner’s system.

Grant your partner access to your Databricks workspace and assign them full write permissions to the Delta
table,
   enabling them to modify the dataset.

Share the dataset using Unity Catalog, ensuring that both teams have full write access to the data within the
same
   organization.

Share the dataset using OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing), which allows your partner to access the data
using a secure, read-only URL
   without requiring a Databricks account, ensuring that they cannot modify the data.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    Share the dataset using OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing), which allows your partner to access the data
using a secure, read-only URL
   without requiring a Databricks account, ensuring that they cannot modify the data.

Why it is correct: Delta Sharing/OpenSharing gives read-only access to recipients without Databricks, no account and no data copy.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Share the dataset by exporting it to a CSV file and manually transferring the file to the partner’s system. — Why it is incorrect: manual, insecure and not scalable.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it grants write and requires an account.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it requires internal users and grants write.

q141.stem:
A data engineer is using the Databricks OPTIMIZE command on a Delta table.

What happens when OPTIMIZE is run twice on the same table with the same data?
options: It has no effect because it is idempotent.
It changes the number of tuples per file significantly.
It further reduces file sizes by re-clustering the data.
It triggers a full liquid clustering process.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: It has no effect because it is idempotent.

Why it is correct: OPTIMIZE is idempotent: if files are already compacted, a second run changes nothing.

  • Official documentation: Optimize data file layout (OPTIMIZE) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — It changes the number of tuples per file significantly. — Why it is incorrect: without new data the distribution does not change.
  • Option C — It further reduces file sizes by re-clustering the data. — Why it is incorrect: it does not recompact already compacted files.
  • Option D — It triggers a full liquid clustering process. — Why it is incorrect: liquid clustering is a table setting, not an effect of repeating OPTIMIZE.

q142.stem:
A data engineer at a company that uses Databricks with Unity Catalog needs to share a collection of tables with an external partner who also uses a Databricks workspace enabled for Unity Catalog. The data engineer decides to use Delta Sharing to accomplish this.

What is the first piece of information the data engineer should request from the external partner to set up OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing)?
options: The IP address of their Databricks workspace
The name of their Databricks cluster
The sharing identifier of their Unity Catalog metastore
Their Databricks account password

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The sharing identifier of their Unity Catalog metastore

Why it is correct: in Databricks-to-Databricks sharing the provider creates the recipient using the recipient's metastore sharing identifier.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The IP address of their Databricks workspace — Why it is incorrect: the IP is not used to set up the recipient.
  • Option B — The name of their Databricks cluster — Why it is incorrect: the cluster is not involved.
  • Option D — Their Databricks account password — Why it is incorrect: passwords are never shared.

q143.stem:
A Databricks workflow fails at the last stage due to an error in a notebook. This workflow runs daily. The data engineer fixes the mistake and wants to rerun the pipeline. This workflow is very costly and time-intensive to run.

Which action should the data engineer do in order to minimise downtime and cost?
options: Re-run the entire workflow
Repair run
Restart the cluster
Switch to another cluster

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Repair run

Why it is correct: Repair run reruns only the failed tasks and their dependents, reusing those that already succeeded.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Re-run the entire workflow — Why it is incorrect: it repeats everything and costs more.
  • Option C — Restart the cluster — Why it is incorrect: it does not rerun the failed task.
  • Option D — Switch to another cluster — Why it is incorrect: it reruns nothing.

q144.stem:
An organization has implemented a data pipeline in Databricks and needs to ensure it can scale automatically based on varying workloads without manual cluster management. The goal is to meet the company’s Service Level Agreements (SLAs), which require high availability and minimal downtime, while Databricks automatically handles resource allocation and optimization.

Which approach fulfills these requirements?
options: Deploy Job Clusters with fixed configurations, dedicated to specific tasks, without automatic scaling.
Use Spot Instances to allocate resources dynamically while minimizing costs, with potential interruptions.
Use Interactive Clusters in Databricks, adjusting cluster sizes manually based on workload demands.

Use Serverless compute in Databricks to automatically scale and provision resources with minimal manual
intervention.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    Use Serverless compute in Databricks to automatically scale and provision resources with minimal manual
intervention.

Why it is correct: serverless scales and provisions automatically and reduces manual management.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Deploy Job Clusters with fixed configurations, dedicated to specific tasks, without automatic scaling. — Why it is incorrect: fixed configuration, no autoscaling.
  • Option B — Use Spot Instances to allocate resources dynamically while minimizing costs, with potential interruptions. — Why it is incorrect: spot can be interrupted; it does not guarantee high availability.
  • Option C — Use Interactive Clusters in Databricks, adjusting cluster sizes manually based on workload demands. — Why it is incorrect: manual sizing contradicts the requirement.

q145.stem:
A data engineer has been provided a PySpark DataFrame named df with columns product and revenue. The data engineer needs to compute complex aggregations to determine each product’s total revenue, average revenue, and transaction count.

Which code snippet should the data engineer use?
options:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
aggregated_df = df.groupBy("product").agg(F.sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
F.avg("revenue").alias("avg_revenue"), F.count("*").alias("transaction_count") )

aggregated_df = df.groupby("product").agg(
   "sum(revenue)",
   "avg(revenue)",
   "count(revenue)"
)

from pyspark.sql import functions as F aggregated_df = df.select("product",
"revenue").groupBy("product").agg( F.sum("revenue"), F.mean("revenue") )

aggregated_df =
df.groupBy("product").agg( {"revenue": "sum", "revenue": "avg", "revenue": "count"} )

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    from pyspark.sql import functions as F
aggregated_df = df.groupBy("product").agg(F.sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
F.avg("revenue").alias("avg_revenue"), F.count("*").alias("transaction_count") )

Why it is correct: groupBy("product").agg(F.sum(…), F.avg(…), F.count("*")) computes the three metrics with aliases.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: passing strings like "sum(revenue)" to agg is not valid.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it only computes sum and mean; the count is missing.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: a dict with a repeated key keeps only the last aggregation.

q146.stem:
A data engineer needs to provide access to a group named manufacturing-team. The team needs privileges to create tables in the quality schema.

Which set of SQL commands will grant a group named manufacturing-team to create tables in a schema named production with the parent catalog named manufacturing with the least privileges?
options:
GRANT CREATE TABLE ON SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE
SCHEMA ON SCHEMA
   manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG manufacturing TO
manufacturing-
   team;

GRANT USE TABLE ON SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE SCHEMA
ON SCHEMA
   manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG manufacturing TO
manufacturing-
   team;

GRANT CREATE TABLE ON SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT CREATE
SCHEMA ON
   SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT CREATE CATALOG ON CATALOG
manufacturing TO
   manufacturing-team;

GRANT CREATE TABLE ON SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT CREATE
SCHEMA ON
  SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG
manufacturing TO

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    GRANT CREATE TABLE ON SCHEMA manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE
SCHEMA ON SCHEMA
   manufacturing.quality TO manufacturing-team; GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG manufacturing TO
manufacturing-
   team;

Why it is correct: creating tables needs CREATE TABLE on the schema, USE SCHEMA on the schema and USE CATALOG on the catalog: the minimum.

⚠️ Heads-up: the statement mentions both "quality" and "production" as the schema; quality is used, as in the options. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: USE TABLE does not exist and does not allow creating tables.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it grants CREATE SCHEMA/CREATE CATALOG, more than minimal and lacking USE.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it adds an unnecessary CREATE SCHEMA and omits USE SCHEMA.

q147.stem:
A data engineer has written a function in a Databricks Notebook to calculate the population of bacteria in a given medium.

def calculate_population_of_bacteria (intital_population, exponential_factor)
  return future_population = intitial_population ** exponential_factor

Analysts use this function in the notebook and sometimes provide input arguments of the wrong data type, which can cause errors during execution.

Which Databricks feature will help the data engineer quickly identify if an incorrect data type has been provided as input?
options: The Spark User interface has a debug tab that contains the variables that are used in this session.
The Databricks debugger enables breakpoints that will raise an error if the wrong data type is submitted.
The Databricks debugger enables the use of a variable explorer to see at a glance the value of the variables.
The Data Engineer should add print statements to find out what the variable is.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The Databricks debugger enables the use of a variable explorer to see at a glance the value of the variables.

Why it is correct: the interactive debugger includes a variable explorer showing values and types at a glance.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The Spark User interface has a debug tab that contains the variables that are used in this session. — Why it is incorrect: the Spark UI has no tab with session variables.
  • Option B — The Databricks debugger enables breakpoints that will raise an error if the wrong data type is submitted. — Why it is incorrect: breakpoints pause execution; they do not raise type errors.
  • Option D — The Data Engineer should add print statements to find out what the variable is. — Why it is incorrect: it is slower and not a Databricks feature.

q148.stem:
A data engineer is inspecting an ETL pipeline based on a Pyspark job that consistently encounters performance bottlenecks. Based on developer feedback, the data engineer assumes the job is low on compute resources. To pinpoint the issue, the data engineer observes the Spark UI and finds out the job has a high CPU time vs Task time.

Which course of action should the data engineer take?
options:
High CPU time vs Task time means an under-utilized cluster. The data engineer may need to repartition data
to
   spread the jobs more evenly throughout the cluster.
High CPU time vs Task time means efficient use of cluster and no change needed

High CPU time vs Task time means a CPU over-utilized job. The data engineer may need to consider
executor and
   core tuning or resizing the cluster
High CPU time vs Task time means over-utilized memory and the need to increase parallelism

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    High CPU time vs Task time means a CPU over-utilized job. The data engineer may need to consider
executor and
   core tuning or resizing the cluster

Why it is correct: a high CPU time versus Task time means the job is CPU-bound: tune executors/cores or enlarge the cluster.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: under-utilization shows as low CPU time.
  • Option B — High CPU time vs Task time means efficient use of cluster and no change needed — Why it is incorrect: it is a bottleneck, not efficiency.
  • Option D — High CPU time vs Task time means over-utilized memory and the need to increase parallelism — Why it is incorrect: it does not indicate memory problems.

q149.stem:
A data engineer needs to parse only png files in a directory that contains files with different suffixes.

Which code should the data engineer use to achieve this task?
options: df = spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").append("/*.png")

df = spark.readstream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").option("pathGlobFilter",
"*.png").load()

df = spark.readstream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").option("pathGlobFilter",
"*.png").append()
df = spark.readstream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").load("/*.png")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    df = spark.readstream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").option("pathGlobFilter",
"*.png").load()

Why it is correct: cloudFiles.format = "binaryFile" with pathGlobFilter = "*.png" and .load() filters only .png files.

⚠️ Heads-up: the option code writes readstream in lowercase (the real method is readStream); that is a flaw in the original. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — df = spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").append("/*.png") — Why it is incorrect: .append() is not a loading method.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: .append() is not valid.
  • Option D — df = spark.readstream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "binaryFile").load("/*.png") — Why it is incorrect: load("/*.png") is not how to filter with Auto Loader.

q150.stem: Which languages are supported by Serverless compute clusters? (Choose two.)
options: SQL
Python
R
Scala
Java

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: SQL
  • Option B: Python

Why it is correct: serverless compute supports SQL and Python.

⚠️ Heads-up: language support depends on the mode (serverless SQL warehouse vs. serverless for notebooks/jobs) and evolves with releases. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option C — R — Why it is incorrect: R is not supported.
  • Option D — Scala — Why it is incorrect: Scala is not supported.
  • Option E — Java — Why it is incorrect: Java is not supported.

q151.stem:
A data engineer is working in a Python notebook on Databricks to process data, but notices that the output is not as expected. The data engineer wants to investigate the issue by stepping through the code and checking the values of certain variables during execution.

Which tool should the data engineer use to inspect the code execution and variables in real-time?
options: Cluster Logs
Job Execution Dashboard
Python Notebook Interactive Debugger
SQL Analytics

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Python Notebook Interactive Debugger

Why it is correct: the interactive debugger lets you step through code and inspect variables.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Cluster Logs — Why it is incorrect: logs are after the fact and not interactive.
  • Option B — Job Execution Dashboard — Why it is incorrect: it shows job runs, not variables.
  • Option D — SQL Analytics — Why it is incorrect: it is the SQL experience, not Python debugging.

q152.stem:
A data engineer has inherited a Databricks pipeline from a previous team. The pipeline is missing its SLAs, and an initial investigation has identified memory spills in Spark. These increased runtimes are also driving up costs. The data engineer needs to reduce the runtime without significantly increasing costs.

What should the data engineer do first to address this issue?
options: Tweak the "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions" configuration.
Enable autoscaling in the cluster to match the requirements
Use a photon enabled execution engine.
Ensure the cluster uses memory optimized node types.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Tweak the "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions" configuration.

Why it is correct: spills usually come from partitions that are too large after a shuffle; tuning spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is the cheap first step with no extra cost.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Enable autoscaling in the cluster to match the requirements — Why it is incorrect: autoscaling does not fix per-partition spill.
  • Option C — Use a photon enabled execution engine. — Why it is incorrect: Photon speeds up but costs more and does not target the cause.
  • Option D — Ensure the cluster uses memory optimized node types. — Why it is incorrect: memory-optimized nodes raise cost; tune partitioning first.

q153.stem:
A data engineer needs to combine sales data from an on-premises PostgreSQL database with customer data in Azure Synapse for a comprehensive report. The goal is to avoid data duplication and ensure up-to-date information.

How should the data engineer achieve this using Databricks?
options: Export data from both sources to CSV files and upload them to Databricks
Use Lakehouse Federation to query both data sources directly
Manually synchronize data from both sources into a single database
Develop custom ETL pipelines to ingest data into Databricks

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Use Lakehouse Federation to query both data sources directly

Why it is correct: Lakehouse Federation queries external sources live without copying them.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Export data from both sources to CSV files and upload them to Databricks — Why it is incorrect: it duplicates data and goes stale.
  • Option C — Manually synchronize data from both sources into a single database — Why it is incorrect: manual, error-prone and duplicating.
  • Option D — Develop custom ETL pipelines to ingest data into Databricks — Why it is incorrect: ingesting duplicates data and requires upkeep.

q154.stem:
A data engineer is facing performance bottlenecks in an e-commerce transactions Delta table. The table is a managed Unity Catalog table, and it uses partitioning and Z-ordering in its data layout scheme. The predictive optimization for Unity Catalog tables is also enabled. The table has a frequently changing query filter, and the data engineer does not observe a benefit of the Data Layout or the Predictive Optimization.

How should the data engineer fix the data layout bottlenecks?
options: Re-write the Data Layout with Liquid Clustering and cluster by the Z-Ordered columns.
Enable Delta Caching so that query results can be read through caches.
Tweak the Z-Order columns and run OPTIMIZE manually.
Switch the Data layout from Partition+Z-Ordering to Automatic Liquid Clustering.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Switch the Data layout from Partition+Z-Ordering to Automatic Liquid Clustering.

Why it is correct: with changing filters, Automatic Liquid Clustering picks and adapts clustering keys automatically on UC managed tables.

⚠️ Heads-up: the PDF notes this question nearly duplicates #183 with a different key; D (Automatic Liquid Clustering) is the one consistent with current documentation. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks | Optimize data file layout (OPTIMIZE) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Re-write the Data Layout with Liquid Clustering and cluster by the Z-Ordered columns. — Why it is incorrect: it fixes the Z-Order columns, which do not adapt to changing filters.
  • Option B — Enable Delta Caching so that query results can be read through caches. — Why it is incorrect: caching does not change the data layout.
  • Option C — Tweak the Z-Order columns and run OPTIMIZE manually. — Why it is incorrect: it would remain a manual tweak of a rigid layout.

q155.stem:
A data engineer needs to optimize the data layout and query performance for an e-commerce transactions Delta table. The table is partitioned by "purchase_date" a date column which helps with time-based queries but does not optimize searches on user statistics "customer_id", a high-cardinality column.

The table is usually queried with filters on "customer_id" within specific date ranges, but since this data is spread across multiple files in each partition, it results in full partition scans and increased runtime and costs. How should the data engineer optimize the Data Layout for efficient reads?
options: Alter table implementing liquid clustering on "customer_id" while keeping the existing partitioning.
Alter the table implementing liquid clustering by "customer_id" and "purchase_date".
Alter the table to partition by "customer_id".
Enable delta caching on the cluster so that frequent reads are cached for performance.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Alter the table implementing liquid clustering by "customer_id" and "purchase_date".

Why it is correct: liquid clustering replaces partitioning and supports several keys, here customer_id and purchase_date.

  • Official documentation: Optimize data file layout (OPTIMIZE) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Alter table implementing liquid clustering on "customer_id" while keeping the existing partitioning. — Why it is incorrect: liquid clustering cannot be combined with existing partitioning.
  • Option C — Alter the table to partition by "customer_id". — Why it is incorrect: partitioning by a high-cardinality column creates too many small partitions.
  • Option D — Enable delta caching on the cluster so that frequent reads are cached for performance. — Why it is incorrect: caching does not fix the data layout.

q156.stem: What is the structure of an Asset Bundle?
options: A Docker image containing runtime environments and the source code of the assets
A compressed archive (ZIP) that solely contains workspace assets without any accompanying metadata
A single plain text file enumerating the names of assets to be migrated to a new workspace
A YAML configuration file that specifies the artifacts, resources, and configurations for the project

answer.correct:
