  • Option D: A YAML configuration file that specifies the artifacts, resources, and configurations for the project

Why it is correct: a bundle is a declarative project described in YAML files (artifacts, resources and configuration).

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A Docker image containing runtime environments and the source code of the assets — Why it is incorrect: it is not a Docker image.
  • Option B — A compressed archive (ZIP) that solely contains workspace assets without any accompanying metadata — Why it is incorrect: it is not a ZIP of assets.
  • Option C — A single plain text file enumerating the names of assets to be migrated to a new workspace — Why it is incorrect: it is not a list of names.

q157.stem:
A data engineer is maintaining an ETL pipeline code with a GitHub repository linked to their Databricks account. The data engineer wants to deploy the ETL pipeline to production as a databricks workflow.

Which approach should the data engineer use?
options: Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles) (DAB) + GitHub Integration
Maintain workflow_config.json and deploy it using Databricks CLI
Maintain workflow_config.json and deploy it using Terraform
Manually create and manage the workflow in UI

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles) (DAB) + GitHub Integration

Why it is correct: bundles define the workflow as YAML versioned in Git and deploy it repeatably via CI/CD.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Maintain workflow_config.json and deploy it using Databricks CLI — Why it is incorrect: a custom JSON is not the supported deployment format.
  • Option C — Maintain workflow_config.json and deploy it using Terraform — Why it is incorrect: it needs extra provider setup; not the standard approach.
  • Option D — Manually create and manage the workflow in UI — Why it is incorrect: manual, with no version control or repeatability.

q158.stem:
A data engineer works for an organization that must meet a stringent Service Level Agreement (SLA) that demands minimal runtime errors and high availability for its data processing pipelines. The data engineer wants to avoid the operational overhead of managing and tuning clusters.

Which architectural solution will meet the requirements?
options: Use an auto-scaling cluster configured and monitored by the user.
Implement a hybrid approach with scheduled batch jobs on custom cloud VMs.
Deploy a dedicated, manually managed cluster optimized by in-house IT staff.

Utilize Databricks serverless compute that automatically optimizes resources and abstracts cluster
management.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    Utilize Databricks serverless compute that automatically optimizes resources and abstracts cluster
management.

Why it is correct: serverless abstracts cluster management and optimizes resources automatically.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use an auto-scaling cluster configured and monitored by the user. — Why it is incorrect: the user still manages and monitors it.
  • Option B — Implement a hybrid approach with scheduled batch jobs on custom cloud VMs. — Why it is incorrect: it adds more management.
  • Option C — Deploy a dedicated, manually managed cluster optimized by in-house IT staff. — Why it is incorrect: that is exactly the manual management to avoid.

q159.stem:
A data engineer wants to reduce costs and optimize cloud spending. The data engineer has decided to use Databricks Serverless for lowering cloud costs while maintaining existing SLAs.

What is the first step in migrating to Databricks Serverless?
options: Legacy Ingestion pipelines that include ingestion from sources API’s, files, JDBC/ODBC connections

A frequently running and efficient Python-based data transformation pipeline compatible with the latest
Databricks
   runtime and Unity Catalog

A frequently running and efficient Scala-based data transformation pipeline compatible with the latest
Databricks
   runtime and Unity Catalog
Low frequency BI Dashboarding and Adhoc SQL Analytics

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    A frequently running and efficient Python-based data transformation pipeline compatible with the latest
Databricks
   runtime and Unity Catalog

Why it is correct: start with a frequent, efficient Python workload compatible with Unity Catalog and the latest runtime, as it is the easiest to migrate and saves the most.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Legacy Ingestion pipelines that include ingestion from sources API’s, files, JDBC/ODBC connections — Why it is incorrect: legacy pipelines often have incompatible dependencies.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: Scala is not supported on serverless.
  • Option D — Low frequency BI Dashboarding and Adhoc SQL Analytics — Why it is incorrect: low-frequency workloads give little savings.

q160.stem:
A data engineering project involves processing large batches of data on a daily schedule using ETL. The jobs are resource- intensive and vary in size, requiring a scalable, cost-efficient compute solution that can automatically scale based on the workload.

Which compute approach will satisfy the needs described? Assume this workload requires configurable classic compute rather than serverless jobs.
options: Job Cluster
Dedicated Cluster
All-Purpose Cluster
Databricks SQL Serverless

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Job Cluster

Why it is correct: a Job Cluster is created for the job, autoscales and terminates when done, the cheapest option for scheduled batch ETL.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Dedicated Cluster — Why it is incorrect: a dedicated cluster is for assigned/interactive use, costlier.
  • Option C — All-Purpose Cluster — Why it is incorrect: an all-purpose cluster is costlier and stays on.
  • Option D — Databricks SQL Serverless — Why it is incorrect: the statement requires classic compute.

q161.stem:
A data engineer is configuring OpenSharing (antes Delta Sharing) for a multi-team project where teams from different departments will need to access shared data. The data engineer has successfully created a Unity Catalog metastore and is now setting up the Delta Share. The goal is to ensure that internal teams can access the shared data with full permissions, while external partners can only read the data.

Which action should the Data Engineer take to configure the sharing correctly?
options:
Create a Delta Share, set up a secure access URL for internal teams and external partners, and distribute the
URL to
   provide them access to the shared data.

Create a Delta Share, add the internal team's tables and views, and assign READ/WRITE permissions to both
external
    partners and internal teams.

Assign READ permissions to external partners through the Delta Share and READ/WRITE permissions to
internal
   teams, and ensure the correct tables and views are shared.

Grant READ permissions to external partners and READ/WRITE permissions to internal teams through the
Delta
   Share.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    Assign READ permissions to external partners through the Delta Share and READ/WRITE permissions to
internal
   teams, and ensure the correct tables and views are shared.

Why it is correct: external partners get read-only through the share, and internal teams get write through Unity Catalog permissions, making sure the right tables and views are shared.

⚠️ Heads-up: options C and D are very similar; C adds checking which tables are shared. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks | Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: a shared URL does not enforce differentiated permissions.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it would give write to external users.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: internal write is not granted through the share and what is shared is not ensured.

q162.stem:
A data engineer manages multiple external tables linked to various data sources. The data engineer wants to manage these external tables efficiently and ensure that only the necessary permissions are granted to users for accessing specific external tables.

How should the data engineer manage access to these external tables?
options: Set up Azure Blob Storage permissions at the container level, allowing access to all external tables.
Create a single user role with full access to all external tables and assign it to all users.
Grant permissions on the Databricks workspace level, which will automatically apply to all external tables.
Use Unity Catalog to manage access controls and permissions for each external table individually.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Use Unity Catalog to manage access controls and permissions for each external table individually.

Why it is correct: Unity Catalog governs each external table with granular permissions, granting only what is needed.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Set up Azure Blob Storage permissions at the container level, allowing access to all external tables. — Why it is incorrect: container-wide access is too broad.
  • Option B — Create a single user role with full access to all external tables and assign it to all users. — Why it is incorrect: full access for everyone violates least privilege.
  • Option C — Grant permissions on the Databricks workspace level, which will automatically apply to all external tables. — Why it is incorrect: workspace permissions do not govern individual tables.

q163.stem:
A data engineer is setting up access control in Unity Catalog and needs to ensure that a group of data analysts can query tables but not modify data.

Which permission should the data engineer grant to the data analysts?
options: ALL PRIVILEGES
MODIFY
SELECT
INSERT

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: SELECT

Why it is correct: SELECT allows reading without modifying.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — ALL PRIVILEGES — Why it is incorrect: it grants everything, including write.
  • Option B — MODIFY — Why it is incorrect: it allows modifying data.
  • Option D — INSERT — Why it is incorrect: it allows inserting data.

q164.stem: What Databricks feature can be used to check the data sources and tables used in a workspace?
options: Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that highlights where the table is used only in reports.
Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that highlights where the table is used only in notebooks.

Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that shows all dependencies, including where the table is used in
notebooks, other tables, and reports.

Do not use the lineage feature as it only tracks activity from the last 3 months and will not provide full details
on
   dependencies.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that shows all dependencies, including where the table is used in
notebooks, other tables, and reports.

Why it is correct: Unity Catalog lineage shows all dependencies in a graph: tables, notebooks, jobs and reports.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that highlights where the table is used only in reports. — Why it is incorrect: it is not limited to reports.
  • Option B — Use the lineage feature to visualize a graph that highlights where the table is used only in notebooks. — Why it is incorrect: it is not limited to notebooks.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it does provide full dependency details.

q165.stem: A partner organization also uses a Unity Catalog-enabled Databricks workspace. You must securely share Unity Catalog-managed Delta tables and the notebook files containing the SQL/Python source code that produces those tables. The partner does not need your Lakeflow Job definitions, schedules, compute settings, or run permissions. Which approach supports this?
options: Email a ZIP of the data and notebooks and grant direct access to your cloud data lake.

Share the tables and notebook files using OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing) and manage the shares and
recipients with Unity Catalog.

Grant Unity Catalog SELECT on your own tables and assume that this automatically publishes the notebooks
and data to an external organization.
Share a GitHub repository and expect Git access to share the governed table data automatically.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Share the tables and notebook files using OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing) and manage the shares and
recipients with Unity Catalog.

Why it is correct: OpenSharing lets you share governed tables and notebooks via Unity Catalog without exposing jobs or compute.

  • Official documentation: Delta Sharing - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Email a ZIP of the data and notebooks and grant direct access to your cloud data lake. — Why it is incorrect: insecure and outside governance.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: SELECT publishes nothing to an external organization.
  • Option D — Share a GitHub repository and expect Git access to share the governed table data automatically. — Why it is incorrect: Git does not share table data.

q166.stem:
A data engineering team wants to validate a new ingestion pipeline locally while ensuring large aggregations run in serverless compute in their Databricks workspace. They plan to use Databricks Connect and have the option to attach to either a shared cluster or serverless.

Which workspace requirement should be confirmed first to avoid connection failures?
options:
Verify that the workspace has Unity Catalog disabled and the Databricks Connect version is less than the
serverless
   Runtime version.

Verify that the workspace has Unity Catalog enabled and that the Databricks Connect version supports
serverless for
   the target Runtime release.

Verify that only assigned access mode clusters are used because serverless is not supported by Databricks
Connect.
Verify that the local Spark version equals the serverless Spark version to satisfy Spark Connect parity.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Verify that the workspace has Unity Catalog enabled and that the Databricks Connect version supports
serverless for
   the target Runtime release.

Why it is correct: serverless requires Unity Catalog and a Databricks Connect version compatible with the runtime.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks | Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: serverless needs Unity Catalog enabled.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: Databricks Connect does support serverless.
  • Option D — Verify that the local Spark version equals the serverless Spark version to satisfy Spark Connect parity. — Why it is incorrect: exact local/remote Spark equality is not required.

q167.stem: A data engineer needs SQL exploratory analysis over a database reachable only inside the company's customer-managed cloud network. Custom networking is required and private connectivity from Databricks Serverless to that database has not been configured. Which SQL Warehouse type is most appropriate?
options: Classic SQL Warehouse
Serverless SQL Warehouse
Pro SQL Warehouse
All-purpose compute cluster

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Pro SQL Warehouse

Why it is correct: a Pro SQL warehouse runs in the customer network and can reach its private database, unlike serverless without private connectivity configured.

⚠️ Heads-up: option A (classic) also runs in the customer network; the bank key prefers Pro. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: SQL warehouses - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Classic SQL Warehouse — Why it is incorrect: classic has fewer features than Pro for exploratory analytics.
  • Option B — Serverless SQL Warehouse — Why it is incorrect: it has no private connectivity configured.
  • Option D — All-purpose compute cluster — Why it is incorrect: an all-purpose cluster is not a SQL warehouse.

q168.stem:
A data engineer must deliver a trustworthy customer 360 dataset in Databricks for data scientists and BI teams. The engineer plans to join deduplicated customer records with cleaned transaction data, enforce schema and data quality checks, and create a conformed "customer_transactions" view. Later, highly aggregated, domain-specific tables (for weekly spend and executive summaries) will be produced for dashboards.

Where should the engineer build the conformed "customer_transactions" dataset, and where should the aggregated, report-ready tables reside?
options: Build both “customer_transactions” and aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver to keep the model simpler.
Build “customer_transactions” in Bronze and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver.
Build “customer_transactions” in Gold and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver.
Build “customer_transactions” in Silver and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Gold.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Build “customer_transactions” in Silver and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Gold.

Why it is correct: the conformed dataset (cleaned, joined data) is Silver; highly aggregated dashboard tables are Gold.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Build both “customer_transactions” and aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver to keep the model simpler. — Why it is incorrect: consumption aggregates go in Gold.
  • Option B — Build “customer_transactions” in Bronze and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver. — Why it is incorrect: Bronze is raw landing, not conformed.
  • Option C — Build “customer_transactions” in Gold and put the aggregated, report-ready tables in Silver. — Why it is incorrect: it inverts the layers.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q169.stem:
A data engineer requires rapid iteration on pipelines while maintaining reliable rollbacks after bad ingests, ensuring audit trails for regulatory compliance, and providing consistent access to a single source of truth for both AI and BI workloads.

Which strategy should the data engineer apply to meet the needs?
options: Delta Lake ACID transactions and time travel, governed by Unity Catalog for consistent access and lineage.
DBFS CSV storage with manual file versioning and nightly copies for rollback.
Ephemeral in-memory DataFrames for audit trails and BI distribution.
Cloud objects storage only, with ad hoc SQL queries for recovery and governance.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Delta Lake ACID transactions and time travel, governed by Unity Catalog for consistent access and lineage.

Why it is correct: Delta Lake gives ACID and time travel (rollback, audit) and Unity Catalog adds governance and lineage over a single source of truth.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks | Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — DBFS CSV storage with manual file versioning and nightly copies for rollback. — Why it is incorrect: manual, fragile and ungoverned.
  • Option C — Ephemeral in-memory DataFrames for audit trails and BI distribution. — Why it is incorrect: in-memory DataFrames are lost; they do not serve for audit.
  • Option D — Cloud objects storage only, with ad hoc SQL queries for recovery and governance. — Why it is incorrect: no transactional layer or governance.

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q170.stem:
A data engineer is setting up a new Databricks pipeline that ingests clickstream events from Kafka and daily product catalogs from cloud object storage. To ensure auditability and easy reprocessing, the engineer wants to land all source data. Later stages will handle cleaning, deduplication, and business modeling before the data is used in dashboards.

Which approach aligns to Medallion Architecture principles?
options: Land both sources in Gold with denormalized star schemas to optimize BI while retaining full source fidelity.

Land streaming events from Kafka in silver, and the product catalog directly in Gold to minimize layers for
batch data.

Land both sources in the Bronze layer append-only with minimal validation, then build Silver/Gold
downstream for
   quality and analytics.

Land both sources directly into the Silver layer with schema enforcement and deduplication to reduce
downstream
   complexity.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    Land both sources in the Bronze layer append-only with minimal validation, then build Silver/Gold
downstream for
   quality and analytics.

Why it is correct: medallion lands everything in Bronze (append-only, minimal validation) and refines in Silver and Gold.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Land both sources in Gold with denormalized star schemas to optimize BI while retaining full source fidelity. — Why it is incorrect: Gold is not a landing layer.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it mixes layers and loses fidelity.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: cleaning before landing loses the original data.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q171.stem:
A data engineer is building a PySpark ingestion pipeline in a local IDE and must execute heavy DataFrame transformations on a remote Databricks cluster for scale while stepping through business logic locally. The workspace uses Unity Catalog and a cluster running Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS. The engineer also plans to register UDFs.

What should the data engineer do to avoid runtime issues during development with Databricks Connect?
options:
Match the local Python minor version to the cluster’s Python minor version when using UDFs, and use a
Databricks Connect package compatible with the cluster’s Runtime version

Use any local Python version as long as the PySpark minor version matches, because the cluster’s Python
version
   is isolated from the client.
Use serverless, because Databricks Connect does not support assigned or shared clusters.

Disable Unity Catalog on the workspace because it conflicts with remote execution through Databricks
Connect.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Match the local Python minor version to the cluster’s Python minor version when using UDFs, and use a
Databricks Connect package compatible with the cluster’s Runtime version

Why it is correct: with UDFs the local Python minor version must match the cluster's, and the Databricks Connect package must match the runtime.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: the client Python version does matter with UDFs.
  • Option C — Use serverless, because Databricks Connect does not support assigned or shared clusters. — Why it is incorrect: Databricks Connect does support assigned and shared clusters.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: Unity Catalog does not conflict.

q172.stem:
A data engineer is migrating pipeline tasks to reduce operational toil. The workspace used Unity Catalog and is in a region that supports serverless. The engineer wants Databricks to auto select instance types, manage scaling, apply Photon, and handle runtime upgrades automatically for job runs.

How should the data engineer meet this requirement while adhering to Databricks constraints?
options:
Run the job on a serverless compute for workflows configuration, ensuring Unity Catalog is enabled and
regional
   support is available.
Use a Pro SQL warehouse and schedule Python notebook tasks to execute as pipeline steps.
Create a job with a single-task job cluster and manually set instance families and min/max workers.
Use an all-purpose cluster with cluster policies to enforce standard sizes and enable autoscaling.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Run the job on a serverless compute for workflows configuration, ensuring Unity Catalog is enabled and
regional
   support is available.

Why it is correct: serverless compute for workflows picks instances, scales, applies Photon and upgrades the runtime automatically; it requires Unity Catalog and regional support.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Use a Pro SQL warehouse and schedule Python notebook tasks to execute as pipeline steps. — Why it is incorrect: a SQL warehouse does not run Python notebook tasks.
  • Option C — Create a job with a single-task job cluster and manually set instance families and min/max workers. — Why it is incorrect: manual configuration contradicts the requirement.
  • Option D — Use an all-purpose cluster with cluster policies to enforce standard sizes and enable autoscaling. — Why it is incorrect: policies are still manual configuration.

q173.stem:
A data engineer is standardizing repository layouts for multiple teams adopting Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles). The engineer wants to ensure every project has a single authoritative configuration file at the repository root that defines the bundle name, targets, workspace settings, permissions, and resource mappings (for jobs and pipelines).

What strategy should the data engineer use to meet the goal?
options:
Place multiple databricks.yml files under each subfolder (for example, jobs/pipelines/, workspace/) and merge
them
   at deploy time using the include mapping.

Place exactly one databricks.yml at the repository root; it is the main configuration file and may reference
additional
   configuration files via the include mapping.

Place a databricks.yml in a databricks/.hidden folder at the repository root; only hidden locations are valid for
bundle
   configs.

Place a databricks.yaml at the repository root and optional databricks.yml in subfolders; the CLI prefers .yaml
over
   .yml when both exist.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Place exactly one databricks.yml at the repository root; it is the main configuration file and may reference
additional
   configuration files via the include mapping.

Why it is correct: a bundle's entry point is a single databricks.yml at the root, which can include other YAML files via include.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: the main file must be single and at the root.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: there are no mandatory "hidden locations".
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: the file name is databricks.yml, not .yaml.

q174.stem:
A data engineer wants to delegate day-to-day permission management for the schema main_marketing to the mkt- admins group, without making them workspace admins. They should be able to grant and revoke privileges for other users on objects within that schema.

Which approach aligns with UC’s ownership and privilege model?
options:
Grant MANAGE permissions on the metastore to mkt-admins, which allows managing privileges for all
schemas and
   tables globally.

Make mkt-admins a workspace-level admins group, then SELECT on main.marketing to allow privilege
delegation.

Transfer ownership of the schema main_marketing to mkt-admins; owners can manage privileges on the
schema and
   its contained objects.

Grant USE SCHEMA on main.marketing and MODIFY on all tables to mkt-admins, which enables managing
grants
   within the schema.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    Transfer ownership of the schema main_marketing to mkt-admins; owners can manage privileges on the
schema and
   its contained objects.

Why it is correct: a schema owner can manage privileges on it and its objects without being a workspace admin.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: too broad (global).
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it makes them admins, which was not wanted.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: USE SCHEMA and MODIFY do not allow granting privileges.

q175.stem:
A data engineer is decommissioning a sandbox schema in Unity Catalog. Some tables are ephemeral staging outputs that can be safety removed entirely, but a few tables point at shared cloud storage used by downstream jobs outside Databricks. The engineer must avoid deleting any shared files when cleaning up catalog objects.

How does Unity Catalog behave when dropping Managed vs External tables?
options: DROP all tables; Databricks will only remove metadata for both managed and external tables.
DROP managed tables that are ephemeral and DROP external tables; files for both remain for 7 days.

DROP managed staging tables to remove data and metadata, and DROP external tables to remove only
metadata
DROP external tables first to delete their files, then DROP managed tables to keep their files for recovery.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: 
    DROP managed staging tables to remove data and metadata, and DROP external tables to remove only
metadata

Why it is correct: dropping a managed table deletes data and metadata; dropping an external one removes only the definition and leaves the files.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DROP all tables; Databricks will only remove metadata for both managed and external tables. — Why it is incorrect: managed tables also lose their data.
  • Option B — DROP managed tables that are ephemeral and DROP external tables; files for both remain for 7 days. — Why it is incorrect: 7-day retention applies to managed tables (UNDROP), not external ones.
  • Option D — DROP external tables first to delete their files, then DROP managed tables to keep their files for recovery. — Why it is incorrect: it inverts the behavior.

q176.stem:
A data engineer is onboarding a new bronze ingestion pipeline in Databricks with Unity Catalog. The team wants Databricks to handle storage layout, apply platform optimizations over time, and simplify lifecycle management so that when a table is dropped, its underlying data is also cleaned up according to Databricks-managed retention policies.

Which table type should the data engineer create for these ingestion tables?
options: Managed tables so that Unity Catalog manages both metadata and underlying data lifecycle.
External tables with a LOCATION pointing to an external volume for full control of file layout.
Foreign tables federated from an external catalog to delegate optimization to the source system.
Temporary views over files to avoid table-level governance and lifecycle coupling.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Managed tables so that Unity Catalog manages both metadata and underlying data lifecycle.

Why it is correct: managed tables leave storage, optimizations and data cleanup on drop to Unity Catalog.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — External tables with a LOCATION pointing to an external volume for full control of file layout. — Why it is incorrect: with an external table you control the files and they are not deleted on drop.
  • Option C — Foreign tables federated from an external catalog to delegate optimization to the source system. — Why it is incorrect: a foreign table delegates to the source system.
  • Option D — Temporary views over files to avoid table-level governance and lifecycle coupling. — Why it is incorrect: a temporary view neither persists data nor governs.

q177.stem:
A data engineer working in Databricks needs to control BI query latency and cost for a sales analytics domain. Silver tables already contain validated, normalized sales and product data. The team wants dashboard-friendly query performance and to align datasets with business concepts (e.g., weekly_sales and account_performance) without overloading analysts with complex joins.

Which design approach should a data engineer choose for the Gold layer in a medallion architecture?
options: Move raw, append-only source data directly into Gold to avoid transformation costs and enable time travel.

Create denormalized, domain-aligned tables and materialized aggregates (e.g., weekly_sales) optimized for
reporting
   and dashboards.
Build only lightly cleansed views in Gold and preserve most business logic in Silver to reduce duplication.
Keep all data heavily normalized in Gold to minimize storage and rely on BI tools to join data at query time.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Create denormalized, domain-aligned tables and materialized aggregates (e.g., weekly_sales) optimized for
reporting
   and dashboards.

Why it is correct: Gold should be denormalized, business-aligned and include materialized aggregates for fast queries.

  • Official documentation: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Move raw, append-only source data directly into Gold to avoid transformation costs and enable time travel. — Why it is incorrect: raw data belongs to Bronze.
  • Option C — Build only lightly cleansed views in Gold and preserve most business logic in Silver to reduce duplication. — Why it is incorrect: Gold needs materialized business logic, not just light views.
  • Option D — Keep all data heavily normalized in Gold to minimize storage and rely on BI tools to join data at query time. — Why it is incorrect: heavy normalization forces costly joins in BI.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q178.stem:
A team is designing their Data bricks Asset Bundle for deployment. They want to ensure their bundle includes all necessary resources, targeted environment configurations, and deployment settings in a single version- controlled file.

What is required as the main configuration file at the root of their project?
options: A Python script called configure_bundle.py that dynamically creates resources at runtime
A databricks.yml YAML file that contains the bundle's name, targets, includes resources, and variables
A directory with multiple TXT files, each describing a single resource for the bundle
A JSON file named bundle_config.json that stores all resource details and environment variables

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A databricks.yml YAML file that contains the bundle's name, targets, includes resources, and variables

Why it is correct: a bundle's root file is databricks.yml, with name, targets, includes and variables.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A Python script called configure_bundle.py that dynamically creates resources at runtime — Why it is incorrect: a dynamic script is not declarative configuration.
  • Option C — A directory with multiple TXT files, each describing a single resource for the bundle — Why it is incorrect: TXT files are not a supported format.
  • Option D — A JSON file named bundle_config.json that stores all resource details and environment variables — Why it is incorrect: the format is YAML, not JSON.

q179.stem:
A developer has configured Databricks Connect and starts running PySpark code locally. They notice that DataFrame operations are executed on the remote cluster, but actions like .show() return results directly in their local console.

What does this behaviour illustrate about how Databricks Connect is used?
options: It requires manual synchronization of results from the cluster
It runs all Spark compute locally and only reads remote files
It proxies Spark commands from the local client to the remote cluster
It mirrors the entire cluster environment on the developer's machine

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: It proxies Spark commands from the local client to the remote cluster

Why it is correct: Databricks Connect proxies Spark commands from the local client to the remote cluster and returns results.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — It requires manual synchronization of results from the cluster — Why it is incorrect: there is no manual synchronization.
  • Option B — It runs all Spark compute locally and only reads remote files — Why it is incorrect: compute runs remotely.
  • Option D — It mirrors the entire cluster environment on the developer's machine — Why it is incorrect: it does not mirror the cluster.

q180.stem:
A data engineer needs to configure an external location and a storage credential so that a new bronze ingestion pipeline can land data in cloud storage governed by Unity Catalog. The engineer has CREATE TABLE permission on schemas but receives a permission error when attempting to create the external location.

Which role is required to unblock this setup, the principle of least privilege?
options:
Grant CREATE EXTERNAL LOCATION on both the metastore and the referenced storage credential so the
engineer can
   define the external location.
Grant ALL PRIVILEGES on the catalog so the engineer can create external locations under its schemas.
Promote the engineer to Workspace Admin so they can manage objects and jobs.
Assign the engineer as Metastore Admin because only Metastore Admins can create external locations.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Grant CREATE EXTERNAL LOCATION on both the metastore and the referenced storage credential so the
engineer can
   define the external location.

Why it is correct: CREATE EXTERNAL LOCATION on the metastore and on the storage credential is enough: the least privilege.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Grant ALL PRIVILEGES on the catalog so the engineer can create external locations under its schemas. — Why it is incorrect: external locations do not hang off a catalog and ALL PRIVILEGES is excessive.
  • Option C — Promote the engineer to Workspace Admin so they can manage objects and jobs. — Why it is incorrect: it gives no Unity Catalog object rights and is excessive.
  • Option D — Assign the engineer as Metastore Admin because only Metastore Admins can create external locations. — Why it is incorrect: being Metastore Admin is not required.

q181.stem:
A data engineer needs to compute metrics such as: • rolling 7-day sales • percent of total revenue • top-N most profitable categories

Which two approaches are appropriate for implementing these metrics with PySpark DataFrames? (Choose two.)
options: Using RDD aggregations for better performance.
Using mapPartitions to manually implement rolling windows.
Using window functions for rolling and ranking calculations.
Collecting the DataFrame to the driver for faster iterative processing.
Using joins and groupBy to compute percent-of-total metrics.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option C: Using window functions for rolling and ranking calculations.
  • Option E: Using joins and groupBy to compute percent-of-total metrics.

Why it is correct: window functions handle rolling and ranking calculations, and groupBy + join computes percent-of-total, all distributed.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Using RDD aggregations for better performance. — Why it is incorrect: RDDs lose DataFrame optimizations.
  • Option B — Using mapPartitions to manually implement rolling windows. — Why it is incorrect: manual, complex and error-prone implementation.
  • Option D — Collecting the DataFrame to the driver for faster iterative processing. — Why it is incorrect: collect() can exhaust driver memory.

q182.stem:
After a failed multi-task job run, a data engineer changes the cluster size and updates a notebook path for one task. The data engineer wants to re-run just the failed/skipped tasks with the updated settings and keep the run lineage intact.

Which strategy should the data engineer use to preserve the run history?
options:
Use Jobs REST API repairRun to re-run failed tasks; the repair uses the current job and task settings and
appears in
    the run history.

Increase the task retry count and click 'Retry' on the failed task to automatically apply new cluster settings
within the
   same run.
Export the job as a Databricks Asset Bundle, redeploy it, and re-run only the modified tasks from the bundle.

Use 'Run now' to start a new run, so that the updated settings apply; the new run replaces the prior run
history.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Use Jobs REST API repairRun to re-run failed tasks; the repair uses the current job and task settings and
appears in
    the run history.

Why it is correct: repairRun reruns only failed/skipped tasks with current settings and stays in the same run's history.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: retries do not apply new cluster settings.
  • Option C — Export the job as a Databricks Asset Bundle, redeploy it, and re-run only the modified tasks from the bundle. — Why it is incorrect: it is not a run-repair function.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: Run now creates another run and does not replace history.

q183.stem: When using MERGE INTO in Delta Lake on Databricks, which clause allows you to automatically delete target rows that no longer match any source rows?
options: WHEN MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET NULL
WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN DELETE

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE

Why it is correct: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE deletes target rows that have no match in the source.

  • Official documentation: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — WHEN MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET NULL — Why it is incorrect: MATCHED BY SOURCE is not a valid clause.
  • Option B — WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE — Why it is incorrect: WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE deletes rows that do match.
  • Option D — WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN DELETE — Why it is incorrect: NOT MATCHED refers to source rows without a target and does not allow DELETE.

links.t: Upsert into a Delta Lake table using MERGE

q184.stem:

SQL Warehouse (Serverless) with Photon enabled.

q185.stem:

q186.stem:
A data engineering team is analyzing customer transactions using a PySpark DataFrame named transactions with columns customer_id, amount, and category.

The team needs to compute, for each customer, the total transaction amount, the average transaction amount, and the maximum amount - all in a single operation for efficiency.

Which code fragment should be used to achieve this in PySpark?
options:
transactions.groupBy("customer_id")
.agg(sum("amount"), avg("amount"), max("amount"))

transactions.groupBy("customer_id")
.select(sum("amount"), avg("amount"), max("amount"))

transactions.agg(groupBy("customer_id"),
sum("amount"),
avg("amount"),
max("amount"))

transactions.groupBy("customer_id")
.sum("amount")
   .avg("amount").max("amount")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    transactions.groupBy("customer_id")
.agg(sum("amount"), avg("amount"), max("amount"))

Why it is correct: groupBy("customer_id").agg(sum, avg, max) computes the three metrics in a single pass.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks

q187.stem:
A Lakeflow Jobs workflow fails at the last task because of an error in a notebook task. This workflow is scheduled to run daily. The data engineer fixes the notebook and wants to rerun the pipeline. This workflow is very compute- intensive and expensive to run.

Which action should the data engineer take in order to minimize downtime and compute cost?

Re-run the entire workflow
Switch to another cluster
Repair run

Correct answer:

  • Option B — Re-run the entire workflow — Why it is incorrect: it repeats what already worked, costlier.

q188.stem:
A data engineer is investigating a Lakehouse ETL job on Databricks that has suddenly become four times slower.

Cluster Metrics (Metrics tab on the compute) to view historical Spark and hardware metrics, without using the
Spark

   Spark metrics.

Ganglia metrics for the cluster, which provide full visibility into Spark stages, tasks, and shuffle metrics for the

q189.stem:

q190.stem:
A data engineer uses the Databricks workspace UI with Unity Catalog enabled. In Data Explorer, they select catalog corp_marketing, then schema campaigns, and see table email_stats. 1. On schema campaigns, open Permissions and grant USE SCHEMA to growth-analysts. 2. On the table
email_stats,

1. On catalog corp_marketing, open Permissions and grant USE CATALOG to growth-analysts. 2. On schema
   campaigns, open Permissions and grant USE SCHEMA to growth-analysts. 3. On the table email_stats, open
Permissions
   and grant SELECT to growth-analysts

1. On catalog corp_marketing, open Permissions and grant USE CATALOG and CREATE SCHEMA to
growth-analysts. 2.
   On schema campaigns, open Permissions and grant USE SCHEMA to growth-analysts. 3. On the table
email_stats, open
   Permissions and grant SELECT to growth-analysts

1. On schema campaigns, open Permissions and grant USE SCHEMA and SELECT to growth-analysts. 2.
On the table
   email_stats, open Permissions and grant SELECT to growth-analysts

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    1. On catalog corp_marketing, open Permissions and grant USE CATALOG to growth-analysts. 2. On schema
   campaigns, open Permissions and grant USE SCHEMA to growth-analysts. 3. On the table email_stats, open
Permissions
   and grant SELECT to growth-analysts

Why it is correct: reading requires USE CATALOG + USE SCHEMA + SELECT, nothing more.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: USE CATALOG is missing and MODIFY allows modification.

q191.stem:
An organization is building a data lakehouse and needs to ingest data from multiple sources into Unity Catalog- managed tables:

• Source 1: Salesforce (50+ objects, frequent schema changes, OAuth authentication required) • Source 2: On-premises SQL server database (100+ tables, CDC enabled, requires network connectivity) • Source 3: Daily JSON files landing in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2

Which ingestion strategy meets these requirements?
options:
Use partner connectors (Fivetran) for all three sources via Partner Connect, as they provide the most
comprehensive

Use Lakeflow Connect managed connectors for all three sources, as they provide consistent serverless
execution and
    Unity Catalog integration across all data source types.

Use Lakeflow Connect managed connectors for Salesforce and SQL Server, and Auto Loader for ADLS files,
all within

Use Auto Loader for all three sources with custom Python code to handle Salesforce API calls and SQL

answer.correct:

all within

Why it is correct: Lakeflow Connect managed connectors cover SaaS (Salesforce) and databases (SQL Server with CDC), while Auto Loader suits JSON files.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks | What is Auto Loader? - Databricks

q192.stem:
A data engineer has manually created several Databricks jobs and dashboards using the workspace UI. The team now wants to manage these resources as code using Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles)), store the configuration in a Git repository, and deploy changes through CI/CD.

Run databricks bundle init to create a new bundle project, then use databricks bundle deploy pointed at the

Use the Databricks REST API to export each job's JSON definition, save the JSON files into a Git repository,

Run databricks bundle generate for each existing resource, use --bind to link the generated configuration to

Clone an empty Git repository into a Git Folder, recreate each job and dashboard configuration in YAML by

Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it keeps JSON and REST, not a bundle project.

q193.stem:
A developer is building a data pipeline that processes records from a bronze table into a silver table. The bronze table, bronze_events, contains duplicate records due to at-least-once delivery guarantees from the upstream ingestion system. The developer writes the following PySpark code to prepare the data:

deduped_df = df.dropDuplicates()
deduped_df.summary("count", "mean", "stddev").show()
from pyspark.sql.functions import approx_count_distinct
deduped_df.select(approx_count_distinct("user_id")).show()

The developer notices that after running dropDuplicates() without arguments, some rows that differ only in the event_timestamp column remain. The developer wants to de-duplicate based only on user_id and event_type, keeping one row per unique combination of these two columns.

Which code change achieves this deduplication requirement?
options: Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.groupBy("user_id", "event_type").count()
Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.distinct().select("user_id", "event_type")
Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.dropDuplicates(["user_id", "event_type"])
Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.drop("event_timestamp").dropDuplicates()

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.dropDuplicates(["user_id", "event_type"])

Why it is correct: dropDuplicates(["user_id","event_type"]) keeps one row per combination of those columns.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.groupBy("user_id", "event_type").count() — Why it is incorrect: groupBy().count() returns counts, not deduplicated rows.
  • Option B — Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.distinct().select("user_id", "event_type") — Why it is incorrect: distinct().select() dedups before projecting and drops columns.
  • Option D — Replace df.dropDuplicates() with df.drop("event_timestamp").dropDuplicates() — Why it is incorrect: dropping the column dedups on all remaining columns, not just those two.

q194.stem:
A governance team is evaluating whether to use Unity Catalog attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies or manually applied row filters and column masks to protect sensitive data across their catalog.

Why should the team use ABAC policies instead of manually applied row filters and column masks?
options:
ABAC policies use governed tags to dynamically match tables and columns, so a single policy defined on a
catalog
    automatically applies to all current and future tables within that catalog without per-table configuration.

ABAC policies allow row filters and column masks to be written in Python and Scala directly, whereas
manually
    applied filters and masks can only use SQL user-defined functions.

ABAC policies can be applied to views and materialized views in addition to tables, whereas manually applied
row
    filters and column masks can only be applied to tables.

ABAC policies support applying multiple distinct row filters to the same table for a single user at query time,
whereas
    manually applied row filters are limited to one filter per table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    ABAC policies use governed tags to dynamically match tables and columns, so a single policy defined on a
catalog
    automatically applies to all current and future tables within that catalog without per-table configuration.

Why it is correct: ABAC is defined once on a catalog and applied via tags to all current and future tables and columns, with no table-by-table setup.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: filters and masks use SQL UDFs in both cases.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: not the main difference.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: not ABAC's main advantage.

q195.stem: A data engineering team needs to ingest historical CSV files from a cloud storage location that already contains 50,000 existing files. They also expect new files to arrive continuously going forward. The team wants to use Auto Loader to incrementally process both existing files and new arrivals efficiently. Which Auto Loader mode should the team configure for this use case?

Use directory listing mode because it provides better performance for the initial processing of 50,000 existing

Use directory listing mode initially to process the 50,000 existing files, then reconfigure the stream to use file
notification mode for ongoing ingestion of new arrivals.

Use file notification mode only after all existing files have been processed, as it cannot efficiently handle large
volumes of pre-existing files.

new
      arrivals by using cloud storage events rather than repeatedly listing directories.

⚠️ Heads-up: Auto Loader's incremental directory listing also scales well and is the default; key A follows the "many files" guidance. Check it against the linked documentation.

q196.stem:

Enable Liquid Clustering with CLUSTER BY on each table to automatically compact and remove stale data

Set the delta.autoOptimize.autoCompact and delta.autoOptimize.optimizeWrite table properties to trigger

Enable predictive optimization at the account, catalog, or schema level so the platform automatically identifies

q197.stem: A data engineering team needs to incrementally ingest customer transactions from a SaaS app into Data Intelligence Platform with: • Built-in change data capture (including updates and deletes) • Automatic schema evolution • Serverless execution with retries and minimal maintenance • OAuth support and basic monitoring Which solution meets all of these requirements?

q198.stem:
A data engineer is designing a cost-optimized, event-driven pipeline. They configure a Lakeflow Job with a File Arrival trigger to watch an S3 bucket. The job runs a notebook that uses Auto Loader with trigger(availableNow=True) to ingest data into a Bronze table.

What is the technical relationship between the File Arrival trigger and Auto Loader in this integration pattern?

The File Arrival trigger starts the job run, while Auto Loader uses its internal checkpoint to independently

    and process only the new files that have arrived since the last successful commit.

The File Arrival trigger automatically passes the specific file path of the new arrival to Auto Loader, allowing
the
    engineer to skip the source path configuration in the code.

Using a File Arrival trigger requires the engineer to disable Auto Loader's checkpointing to prevent the job
from
    processing the same file multiple times.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    The File Arrival trigger starts the job run, while Auto Loader uses its internal checkpoint to independently
identify
    and process only the new files that have arrived since the last successful commit.

Why it is correct: the trigger only starts the job; Auto Loader decides which files are new using its checkpoint.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks

q199.stem:
A data engineer is transforming a bronze table containing API response data into a silver table. The bronze table has a user_profile column of type STRING that contains JSON data. An example value is:

'{"user_id": "12345", "name": "John Smith", "age": 32, "email": "john@example.com"}'

The silver table needs to make this data easily queryable for analytics without requiring JSON parsing in every downstream query. Which approach standardizes this column for the silver table?
options:
SELECT
  get_json_object(user_profile, 'user_id') AS user_id,
  get_json_object(user_profile, 'name') AS name,
  get_json_object(user_profile, 'age') AS age,
  get_json_object(user_profile, 'email') AS email
FROM bronze_table;

SELECT
   user_profile.user_id  AS user_id,
   user_profile.name      AS name,
   CAST(user_profile.age AS INT) AS age,
  user_profile.email                AS email
FROM bronze_table;

SELECT
  from_json(
     user_profile,
     'user_id STRING, name STRING, age STRING, email STRING'
  ) AS parsed_profile
FROM bronze_table;

SELECT
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.user_id') AS user_id,
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.name') AS name,
  CAST(get_json_object(user_profile, '$.age') AS INT) AS age,
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.email') AS email
FROM bronze_table;

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: 
    SELECT
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.user_id') AS user_id,
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.name') AS name,
  CAST(get_json_object(user_profile, '$.age') AS INT) AS age,
  get_json_object(user_profile, '$.email') AS email
FROM bronze_table;

Why it is correct: get_json_object(col, '$.field') extracts each field with the right JSON path and CAST sets the type (age → INT).

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: the paths do not start with $., so they return NULL.
  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: a STRING does not support dot access like a struct.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it returns a single struct column, not separate standard columns, and keeps age as string.

q200.stem:
A data engineer is troubleshooting two different pipeline failures: • Pipeline A fails with a java.lang.OutOfMemoryError is immediately thrown after the command display(df.collect()) is called on a 100GB dataset. • Pipeline B fails during a wide transformation (a join of two large tables) with an ExecutorLostFailure error message, indicating executor memory exhaustion during shuffle.

Which action should the data engineer take to fix these two issues?
options: For Pipeline A, switch to a Storage Optimized cluster; for Pipeline B, use a Compute Optimized cluster.

For Pipeline A, increase the spark.driver.memory; for Pipeline B, increase the spark.sql.shuffle.partitions or
executor
     memory.
For Pipeline A, increase the number of executors; for Pipeline B, increase the driver memory.

For both pipelines, enable Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) as it automatically manages memory allocation
for both
    the driver and executors.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    For Pipeline A, increase the spark.driver.memory; for Pipeline B, increase the spark.sql.shuffle.partitions or
executor
     memory.

Why it is correct: collect() pulls everything to the driver, so A needs more driver memory; B is shuffle memory pressure, relieved with more partitions or executor memory.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — For Pipeline A, switch to a Storage Optimized cluster; for Pipeline B, use a Compute Optimized cluster. — Why it is incorrect: the cluster type does not fix these specific causes.
  • Option C — For Pipeline A, increase the number of executors; for Pipeline B, increase the driver memory. — Why it is incorrect: it swaps the causes: more executors do not help A.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: AQE does not manage driver memory nor guarantee avoiding these failures.

q201.stem:
A data engineering team needs to integrate two data sources into Databricks: • Clickstream Events: Ingesting 5,000 events per second from an Apache Kafka topic. • Customer Master Data: Syncing only changed records every 4 hours from a Snowflake database.

The solution must meet two key requirements: • Process the streaming clickstream data with a latency of under 30 seconds. • Prevent the reprocessing of customer master data that has not changed.

Which data ingestion approach meets these requirements?
options:
Use Structured Streaming for Kafka and a Lakeflow Connect standard connector with full refresh for
Snowflake.

Use Structured Streaming for Kafka and Lakeflow Connect managed connector with incremental mode for
Snowflake.
Use spark.readStream() with Kafka and query Snowflake hourly with a time-based filter.

Use a non-incremental Snowflake connector with polling and fetch all data every 4 hours with MERGE
operations.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Use Structured Streaming for Kafka and Lakeflow Connect managed connector with incremental mode for
Snowflake.

Why it is correct: Structured Streaming meets Kafka latency and the managed connector in incremental mode syncs only changes.

  • Official documentation: Structured Streaming - Databricks | Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: full refresh reprocesses everything.
  • Option C — Use spark.readStream() with Kafka and query Snowflake hourly with a time-based filter. — Why it is incorrect: a time filter is brittle and queries hourly.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: it fetches everything each time, with no incrementality.

q202.stem:
A data engineer configures a Databricks Lakeflow Job for daily customer data processing: • Entry task: Single notebook loads raw data • Parallel tasks: o SQL query task for cleansing o Notebook task for feature engineering o Pipeline task for model updates • Exit task: Dashboard refresh (must run after all parallel tasks complete) • Requirement: Implement this dependency pattern using a DAG-based task graph

Which task configuration ensures all parallel tasks complete before the dashboard refresh task runs?
options:
Create separate Lakeflow Jobs for each parallel task and trigger them sequentially using external
orchestration.
Add the dashboard task as dependent on all three parallel tasks using fan-in control flow.
Configure the parallel tasks with sequential dependencies so each task waits for the previous one to finish.
Set the dashboard task to depend only on the SQL query task; other tasks run independently.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Add the dashboard task as dependent on all three parallel tasks using fan-in control flow.

Why it is correct: a task with Depends on on all three parallel tasks waits for all of them: the fan-in pattern.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: unnecessary external orchestration and not a single DAG.
  • Option C — Configure the parallel tasks with sequential dependencies so each task waits for the previous one to finish. — Why it is incorrect: it makes them sequential, losing parallelism.
  • Option D — Set the dashboard task to depend only on the SQL query task; other tasks run independently. — Why it is incorrect: the dashboard would not wait for the other two.

q203.stem:
A data engineer has a PySpark DataFrame events_df which contains a nested device struct, which itself includes a nested location struct, as shown:

event_id STRING,
device STRUCT<id: STRING, model: STRING, location: STRUCT<latitude: DOUBLE, longitude: DOUBLE>>,
event_ts TIMESTAMP

The goal is to flatten the nested fields into root-level columns while keeping the event identifiers and timestamp.

Which PySpark expression achieves this?
options:
events_df.select("event_id", "event_ts", "device.id", "device.model", "device.location.latitude",
"device.location.longitude")

events_df.withColumn("device_id", events_df["device.id"]).withColumn("device_model",
events_df["device.model"]).withColumn("location", events_df["device.location"])

events_df.select("event_id", "device[id]", "device[model]", "device.location[latitude]",
"device.location[longitude]", "event_ts")
events_df.select("event_id", "event_ts", "device.*")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    events_df.select("event_id", "event_ts", "device.id", "device.model", "device.location.latitude",
"device.location.longitude")

Why it is correct: selecting each field by dot path (device.id, device.location.latitude…) flattens all levels.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: withColumn keeps location as an unflattened struct and retains the other columns.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: the device[id] notation is not valid for structs like this.
  • Option D — events_df.select("event_id", "event_ts", "device.*") — Why it is incorrect: device.* flattens one level but leaves location as a struct.

q204.stem: A data engineer has developed a Python notebook in a Databricks workspace and has configured it to run as a scheduled Job to process daily sales data. How are the storage and execution of this notebook managed within the Databricks architecture?
options:
The notebook is stored securely and encrypted in the control plane, and the code executes in the compute
plane
    when the job runs.

The notebook is stored securely and encrypted in the compute plane, and the code executes in the control
plane
     when the job runs.

The notebook is stored securely and encrypted in Unity Catalog, and the code executes in Delta Lake when
the job
     runs.

The notebook is stored unencrypted in the workspace storage bucket, and the code executes on the cluster
driver
    node in the compute plane when the job runs.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    The notebook is stored securely and encrypted in the control plane, and the code executes in the compute
plane
    when the job runs.

Why it is correct: notebooks are stored encrypted in the control plane and the code runs in the compute plane.

  • Official documentation: Databricks architecture (control and data planes) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it swaps the planes.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: Unity Catalog does not store notebooks and Delta Lake does not run code.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: the notebook is stored encrypted, not unencrypted.

q205.stem:
A data engineering team uses Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Declarative Automation Bundles (antes Databricks Asset Bundles)) to deploy the same codebase across dev, test, and prod environments. The team wants environment-specific behavior to be applied only through bundle configuration, without modifying notebooks, job definitions, or deployment logic during promotion.

Which approach applies environment-specific configuration while meeting this requirement?
options:
Use separate Git branches per environment so each branch can contain environment-specific configuration
values.

Define bundle variables and reference them from bundle resources, then override variable values per
environment
    using bundle targets.

Parameterize environment-specific values inside notebooks and set those parameters when each job run is
triggered.

Deploy the same bundle once and edit job settings in the workspace UI for each environment after
deployment.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Define bundle variables and reference them from bundle resources, then override variable values per
environment
    using bundle targets.

Why it is correct: bundle variables overridden per targets apply per-environment configuration without touching code or resources.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: per-environment branches complicate promotion and diverge.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: it modifies notebooks, which is to be avoided.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: manual post-deploy edits, not reproducible.

q206.stem:
A data engineer observes that an ETL job in Databricks has increased its execution time from 5 minutes (baseline) to 12 minutes over the past week. Using the Lakeflow Jobs run history view, the engineer needs to identify whether the slowdown is consistent or intermittent and determine the root cause.

Which action should the engineer take to analyze execution time trends against the baseline?
options: Compare cluster metrics in Lakeflow Jobs run history to spot resource spikes causing delays.
Archive old job runs and resets the baseline counter to ensure accurate comparison of current performance.

Rerun the job immediately to establish a new baseline since historical data becomes irrelevant after seven
days.
Increase cluster size automatically whenever execution time exceeds the previous run's duration.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Compare cluster metrics in Lakeflow Jobs run history to spot resource spikes causing delays.

Why it is correct: run history lets you compare durations and cluster metrics across runs to spot resource spikes.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks | Compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Archive old job runs and resets the baseline counter to ensure accurate comparison of current performance. — Why it is incorrect: archiving removes the needed baseline.
  • Option C — … — Why it is incorrect: history remains relevant.
  • Option D — Increase cluster size automatically whenever execution time exceeds the previous run's duration. — Why it is incorrect: enlarging the cluster without a root cause raises cost.

q207.stem:
A data engineer maintains a Declarative Automation Bundle (formerly Databricks Asset Bundle), which deploys a dashboard.

The databricks.yml includes:

bundle:
  name: workspace_assets
variables:
  dataset_catalog:
    default: catalog_dev
targets:
  dev:
    variables:
      dataset_catalog: catalog_dev
  prod:
    variables:
      dataset_catalog: catalog_prod

Which set of actions will enable the dashboard to be deployed in prod using catalog_prod without changing the resource definition?
options: Run databricks bundle deploy --profile prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically.
Run databricks bundle deploy --target prod so the deployment uses targets.prod and overrides dataset_catalog to catalog_prod.
Run databricks bundle execute --profile prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically.
Run databricks bundle deploy --var dataset_catalog=catalog_prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Run databricks bundle deploy --target prod so the deployment uses targets.prod and overrides dataset_catalog to catalog_prod.

Why it is correct: --target prod selects the prod target and its overridden variables.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Run databricks bundle deploy --profile prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically. — Why it is incorrect: --profile picks the authentication profile, not the target.
  • Option C — Run databricks bundle execute --profile prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically. — Why it is incorrect: bundle execute does not exist (it is bundle run) and --profile does not select a target.
  • Option D — Run databricks bundle deploy --var dataset_catalog=catalog_prod so the CLI selects targets.prod and applies dataset_catalog: catalog_prod automatically. — Why it is incorrect: --var only changes one variable; it does not select the target.

q208.stem:
A data engineering team is designing the Gold layer in their Unity Catalog-governed lakehouse for downstream BI and analytics users. The team wants to expose business-ready metrics with fast query performance and consistent definitions, while keeping the transformation logic in Spark notebooks.

Which type of Gold layer object meets this requirement?
options:
A materialized view that precomputes aggregations from Silver tables on a schedule and is queried by BI tools
for
   faster, consistent analytics.

A streaming table that continuously ingests raw events from source systems and exposes them directly to BI
users.
A view that directly references raw Bronze tables so BI tools can define their own joins and aggregations.

A collection of CSV files stored in a cloud storage object. BI users will parse the files to query the gold layer
data.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    A materialized view that precomputes aggregations from Silver tables on a schedule and is queried by BI tools
for
   faster, consistent analytics.

Why it is correct: a materialized view precomputes aggregations from Silver and offers fast queries with consistent definitions.

  • Official documentation: Materialized views - Databricks | What is the medallion lakehouse architecture? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: a streaming table of raw events is not a Gold layer.
  • Option C — A view that directly references raw Bronze tables so BI tools can define their own joins and aggregations. — Why it is incorrect: referencing Bronze skips layers and repeats logic in BI.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: ungoverned CSVs with no performance.

links.t: What is the medallion lakehouse architecture?

q209.stem:
A company has a strict 15-minute Service Level Agreement (SLA) for updating its currency exchange dashboard. The source data arrives in small increments every few minutes. The data engineering team needs a triggering strategy for their Lakeflow Job that keeps end-to-end latency within the SLA while minimizing compute costs and DBU consumption.

Which triggering strategy for the Lakeflow Job is the recommended way to meet this 15-minute SLA?
options:
Use a Scheduled trigger set to run every 12 minutes, with the streaming task configured to use
Trigger.AvailableNow.
Use a Scheduled trigger set to run every 1 minute to ensure the SLA is never at risk.
Use a File Arrival trigger configured to fire every time a single JSON file lands in the bucket.
Use a Continuous trigger to ensure data is processed as soon as it arrives.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Use a Scheduled trigger set to run every 12 minutes, with the streaming task configured to use
Trigger.AvailableNow.

Why it is correct: a 12-minute schedule with availableNow meets the 15-minute SLA and only consumes compute during each run.

  • Official documentation: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers - Databricks | Structured Streaming trigger intervals - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Use a Scheduled trigger set to run every 1 minute to ensure the SLA is never at risk. — Why it is incorrect: every minute raises cost unnecessarily.
  • Option C — Use a File Arrival trigger configured to fire every time a single JSON file lands in the bucket. — Why it is incorrect: it would launch a job per file, inefficient.
  • Option D — Use a Continuous trigger to ensure data is processed as soon as it arrives. — Why it is incorrect: continuous mode keeps compute on all the time.

links.t: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers

q210.stem:
A data engineering team ingests customer transaction data from three enterprise sources (SQL database, S3, and Kafka stream) into Unity Catalog tables. The data must maintain lineage and support compliance audits requiring historical snapshots.

Which Lakeflow Connect configuration satisfies both the governance and audit requirements?
options:
Single Lakeflow connector with all three sources, direct Delta writes, and disabled table versioning to reduce
storage
   costs.

Separate connectors per source with CDC, individual Unity Catalog schemas per source, and table versioning
enabled
   for audit compliance.
Separate connectors with full-load sync only, archival of historical data, and external tables for audit queries.

Single connector with batch scheduling, shared Unity Catalog schema, and incremental snapshots stored
externally.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: 
    Separate connectors per source with CDC, individual Unity Catalog schemas per source, and table versioning
enabled
   for audit compliance.

Why it is correct: per-source connectors with CDC, separate Unity Catalog schemas and table versioning enabled keep lineage and history for audits.

⚠️ Heads-up: the question mixes Kafka with Lakeflow Connect (which does not cover Kafka as a managed connector); key B is the most coherent option. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks | Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: disabling versioning prevents historical snapshots.
  • Option C — Separate connectors with full-load sync only, archival of historical data, and external tables for audit queries. — Why it is incorrect: full load does not track changes and history sits outside governance.
  • Option D — … — Why it is incorrect: a shared schema and external snapshots weaken governance.

q211.stem:
A data engineer needs to support a Unity Catalog Delta table catalog.schema.sales that is currently registered as an external table. New requirements state: • Automatic file cleanup after a drop is handled by the platform. • Minimal downtime during migration while keeping the same table name, permissions, and history. • Enforced name-based access through Unity Catalog (no path-based access).

Which action should the data engineer take to meet the requirements?
options: Run ALTER TABLE catalog.schema.sales SET MANAGED to convert and meet the goals
Run DROP TABLE catalog.schema.sales PURGE to delete files and meet goals
Run ALTER TABLE catalog.schema.sales SET LOCATION to switch external paths now
Create a new managed table with CTAS and migrate workloads to that table today

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Run ALTER TABLE catalog.schema.sales SET MANAGED to convert and meet the goals

Why it is correct: ALTER TABLE … SET MANAGED converts the external table to managed keeping name, permissions and history, with minimal downtime.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:
