  • Option B — Run DROP TABLE catalog.schema.sales PURGE to delete files and meet goals — Why it is incorrect: it deletes the table instead of migrating it.
  • Option C — Run ALTER TABLE catalog.schema.sales SET LOCATION to switch external paths now — Why it is incorrect: it stays external with path-based access.
  • Option D — Create a new managed table with CTAS and migrate workloads to that table today — Why it is incorrect: CTAS loses history and forces workload migration.

q212.stem:
A data engineer has finished developing a new Declarative Automation Bundle (formerly Databricks Asset Bundle) for a streaming pipeline. They need to ensure the configuration is syntactically correct, push the code to the workspace, and finally trigger the pipeline to verify it runs as expected.

Which sequence of Databricks CLI commands should the engineer use to perform these steps in the correct order?
options: databricks bundle init -> databricks bundle deploy -> databricks bundle run
databricks bundle validate -> databricks bundle deploy -> databricks bundle run
databricks bundle validate -> databricks bundle sync -> databricks bundle execute
databricks bundle check -> databricks bundle upload -> databricks bundle start

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: databricks bundle validate -> databricks bundle deploy -> databricks bundle run

Why it is correct: the order is validate → deploy → run.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks bundle init -> databricks bundle deploy -> databricks bundle run — Why it is incorrect: init creates a new project; it does not validate.
  • Option C — databricks bundle validate -> databricks bundle sync -> databricks bundle execute — Why it is incorrect: bundle sync and bundle execute do not serve these steps (execute does not exist).
  • Option D — databricks bundle check -> databricks bundle upload -> databricks bundle start — Why it is incorrect: check, upload and start are not bundle subcommands.

q213.stem:
A data engineer has configured a Lakeflow Job that runs daily to ingest customer transaction data from a legacy relational database. The extracted data must be written directly to a Unity Catalog table and be immediately queryable via SQL. The team needs to ensure full data lineage is preserved.

Which action enables this data ingestion with direct landing in Unity Catalog, preserved lineage, and immediate SQL query ability?
options: Stage data in cloud storage via REST API, then load with a separate job
Use spark.read.format("jdbc") and write with saveAsTable("catalog.schema.table")
Extract to Pandas DataFrame, convert to Spark, then save() to external path
Use ODBC pooling to extract all records in one batch and write to /dbfs/

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Use spark.read.format("jdbc") and write with saveAsTable("catalog.schema.table")

Why it is correct: spark.read.format("jdbc") + saveAsTable("catalog.schema.table") writes directly to a Unity Catalog table with lineage.

  • Official documentation: Query databases using JDBC - Databricks | What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Stage data in cloud storage via REST API, then load with a separate job — Why it is incorrect: an intermediate storage step breaks direct landing and lineage.
  • Option C — Extract to Pandas DataFrame, convert to Spark, then save() to external path — Why it is incorrect: saving to an external path bypasses the governed table and breaks lineage.
  • Option D — Use ODBC pooling to extract all records in one batch and write to /dbfs/ — Why it is incorrect: writing to /dbfs/ is not a Unity Catalog table.

q214.stem:
A data engineer is designing a bronze-to-silver pipeline on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. The source system sends daily CSV files, and over time, new optional columns are added.

The data engineer wants a storage format and table feature that together ensure the following: • The table prevents writes that do not conform to the defined schema. • The table can evolve its schema to include new optional columns without having to manually recreate the table. • Previous versions of the table can be queried later for debugging and auditing.

Which solution fulfills the requirements?
options:
Use a Parquet table with Spark's default schema inference and rely on re-running the job when the schema
changes.
Use an external table with Auto Loader schema inference for CSV files.
Use a Delta table with its native capabilities.
Use a Delta table with schema enforcement and recreate the table whenever new columns are added.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Use a Delta table with its native capabilities.

Why it is correct: Delta natively provides schema enforcement, schema evolution (mergeSchema) and time travel.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake on Databricks - Databricks | Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — … — Why it is incorrect: Parquet neither enforces schema nor versions.
  • Option B — Use an external table with Auto Loader schema inference for CSV files. — Why it is incorrect: an external table alone gives no versioning or enforcement.
  • Option D — Use a Delta table with schema enforcement and recreate the table whenever new columns are added. — Why it is incorrect: recreating the table is manual and loses history.

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q215.stem:
A data engineer is designing a Databricks Job that includes a Notebook task for data cleansing and a SQL Query task for generating a summary report. The summary report must only execute after the cleansing task completes successfully.

How should the dependency be configured in the Lakeflow Jobs task graph?
options:
Set the cleansing task as a dependency in the report task's Depends on field, and keep Run if = All
succeeded.
Set both tasks to run on the same schedule with a five-minute start delay for the report.
Configure the cleansing task to use an 'On Failure' trigger to start the summary report.
Place both tasks in the same notebook and use a standard Python function call.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: 
    Set the cleansing task as a dependency in the report task's Depends on field, and keep Run if = All
succeeded.

Why it is correct: Depends on + Run if = All succeeded ensures the report only runs when cleansing succeeds.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Set both tasks to run on the same schedule with a five-minute start delay for the report. — Why it is incorrect: a fixed delay guarantees neither order nor success.
  • Option C — Configure the cleansing task to use an 'On Failure' trigger to start the summary report. — Why it is incorrect: "On Failure" fires on failure, the opposite of what is asked.
  • Option D — Place both tasks in the same notebook and use a standard Python function call. — Why it is incorrect: a SQL Query task cannot be put in the same notebook as a task.

q216.stem:
A notebook task check_volume calculates a daily data volume and writes it to a Lakeflow Jobs taskValue named record_count. If the count is greater than 1 million, the job should run high_volume_pipeline; otherwise, it should run normal_pipeline.

Which control-flow feature should be used?
options: Add an If/else condition task that reads the record_count task value and routes to different downstream tasks.
Use a For each task over the record_count and stop when it is below the threshold.
Configure additional retries for check_volume until the count exceeds the threshold.
Configure Run if conditions based purely on task status.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Add an If/else condition task that reads the record_count task value and routes to different downstream tasks.

Why it is correct: the If/else condition task evaluates a value (taskValue) and routes to one branch or the other.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Use a For each task over the record_count and stop when it is below the threshold. — Why it is incorrect: For each iterates over a collection; it does not choose a branch.
  • Option C — Configure additional retries for check_volume until the count exceeds the threshold. — Why it is incorrect: retries do not evaluate values.
  • Option D — Configure Run if conditions based purely on task status. — Why it is incorrect: Run if uses task status, not the computed value.

q217.stem:
A data engineer is cleaning a bronze table that receives the same customer records from multiple source systems. Duplicate rows have the same customer_id and email but different ingestion_timestamp values. The silver table should contain only one record per unique combination of customer_id and email.

Which PySpark operation correctly deduplicates based on the business keys?
options: df.dropDuplicates(['customer_id', 'email'])
df.groupBy('customer_id', 'email').agg(max('ingestion_timestamp').alias('latest_ts'))
df.select('customer_id', 'email').distinct()
df.distinct()

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: df.dropDuplicates(['customer_id', 'email'])

Why it is correct: dropDuplicates(['customer_id','email']) keeps one full row per combination of those keys.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — df.groupBy('customer_id', 'email').agg(max('ingestion_timestamp').alias('latest_ts')) — Why it is incorrect: it returns only keys and the max, not complete records.
  • Option C — df.select('customer_id', 'email').distinct() — Why it is incorrect: it projects only two columns and loses the rest.
  • Option D — df.distinct() — Why it is incorrect: it dedups on all columns, and the timestamp differs.

q218.stem:
A data engineer ingests semi-structured JSON logs into a Delta table using Auto Loader with schema evolution enabled. A new string field userAgent appears in the JSON.

What happens to the new userAgent field?
options: All existing data is backfilled with a default value for userAgent and made non-nullable.
The new userAgent field is added as a new nullable column in the Delta table, populated for new data.
Ingestion fails with a schema-mismatch error until the table is altered.
The new userAgent field is silently ignored, and its data is dropped for all new files.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: The new userAgent field is added as a new nullable column in the Delta table, populated for new data.

Why it is correct: with schema evolution the new column is added as nullable and populated for new data; old rows stay NULL.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — All existing data is backfilled with a default value for userAgent and made non-nullable. — Why it is incorrect: no backfill happens and it does not become non-nullable.
  • Option C — Ingestion fails with a schema-mismatch error until the table is altered. — Why it is incorrect: with evolution enabled it does not fail permanently (in addNewColumns it restarts and adds the column).
  • Option D — The new userAgent field is silently ignored, and its data is dropped for all new files. — Why it is incorrect: it is not ignored: it is added (or rescued) depending on the mode.

q219.stem:
A data engineer is tasked with cleaning a bronze table. The requirement is to eliminate rows where either the customer_email or the customer_phone field is null. This data cleaning must be performed in a single operation using a single method call.

Which PySpark approach supports filtering multiple columns for nulls in one call?
options: df.dropna(subset=['customer_email', 'customer_phone'])
df.where('customer_email IS NOT NULL').where('customer_phone IS NOT NULL')
df.na.drop(how='all')
df.filter(col('customer_email').isNotNull() & col('customer_phone').isNotNull())

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: df.dropna(subset=['customer_email', 'customer_phone'])

Why it is correct: dropna(subset=[…]) removes rows with nulls in any of those columns in a single call.

⚠️ Heads-up: option D (a single filter with two conditions) also removes null rows in one call; the official key is A (dropna). Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — df.where('customer_email IS NOT NULL').where('customer_phone IS NOT NULL') — Why it is incorrect: it chains two where calls.
  • Option C — df.na.drop(how='all') — Why it is incorrect: how="all" only drops rows where all columns are null.
  • Option D — df.filter(col('customer_email').isNotNull() & col('customer_phone').isNotNull()) — Why it is incorrect: it is a single filter call, but a filtering expression rather than the multi-column null-cleaning method expected.

q220.stem: A Unity Catalog external Delta table is converted to a managed table using ALTER TABLE catalog.schema.table_name SET MANAGED. A Structured Streaming job reading the table was running during conversion and stops after the conversion. How should the engineer restore processing while preserving progress?
options: Grant the streaming job additional permissions on the new managed storage location
Restart the streaming job, so it picks up the new managed table location
Run REFRESH TABLE on the converted table to update the streaming checkpoint
Delete the streaming checkpoint directory and let the job reprocess from the beginning

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Restart the streaming job, so it picks up the new managed table location

Why it is correct: restarting the job is enough for it to read the new location; the checkpoint is kept and no progress is lost.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks | Structured Streaming - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Grant the streaming job additional permissions on the new managed storage location — Why it is incorrect: permissions come from Unity Catalog; that is not the cause.
  • Option C — Run REFRESH TABLE on the converted table to update the streaming checkpoint — Why it is incorrect: REFRESH TABLE does not update checkpoints.
  • Option D — Delete the streaming checkpoint directory and let the job reprocess from the beginning — Why it is incorrect: it would lose progress and reprocess everything.

q221.stem:
A data engineer needs to find all customers who have never placed an order. The customers table contains customer_id, customer_name, and other customer attributes. The orders table contains order_id, customer_id, and other order attributes. Both tables share customer_id as the join key. The result must include only customer columns with no order- related columns in the output.

Which expression exactly achieves this requirement?
options: Inner join, then filter for NULL order_id
Left anti-join from customers to orders
Left outer join from orders to customers
Full outer join, then filter where order_id is NULL

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Left anti-join from customers to orders

Why it is correct: the left anti-join returns customers rows with no match in orders, with only customers columns.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Inner join, then filter for NULL order_id — Why it is incorrect: an inner join never leaves order_id NULL.
  • Option C — Left outer join from orders to customers — Why it is incorrect: it starts from orders and brings order columns.
  • Option D — Full outer join, then filter where order_id is NULL — Why it is incorrect: it returns columns from both tables.

q222.stem:
A data engineering team runs nightly batch ETL pipelines that transform large volumes of data stored in Delta Lake. The workloads are predictable and run on a fixed schedule. The team wants automatic scaling and cost efficiency, paying only for compute used during job execution.

Which Databricks compute option is appropriate for this workload?
options: An all-purpose compute cluster configured with autoscaling.
A Databricks SQL warehouse configured for serverless execution.
A single-node compute cluster configured without autoscaling.
A job compute cluster triggered by a scheduled workflow.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: A job compute cluster triggered by a scheduled workflow.

Why it is correct: a jobs cluster is created for the scheduled run, autoscales and terminates when done: you pay only for what you use.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — An all-purpose compute cluster configured with autoscaling. — Why it is incorrect: it stays on and is costlier.
  • Option B — A Databricks SQL warehouse configured for serverless execution. — Why it is incorrect: a SQL warehouse is for SQL, not notebook ETL.
  • Option C — A single-node compute cluster configured without autoscaling. — Why it is incorrect: without autoscaling it fails the requirement.

q223.stem:
A data engineer is attempting to grant a user access to a view. They successfully run GRANT SELECT ON VIEW sales_catalog.market_data.summary TO analyst_group.

However, the analyst still receives an "Insufficient Permissions" error when trying to query the view.

In which order should the engineer verify the Hierarchy of Securable Objects to ensure the analyst has the necessary usage permissions?
options: CATALOG -> SCHEMA -> VIEW
METASTORE -> TABLE -> VIEW
STORAGE CREDENTIAL -> EXTERNAL LOCATION -> VIEW
WORKSPACE -> CLUSTER -> VIEW

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: CATALOG -> SCHEMA -> VIEW

Why it is correct: querying a view needs USE CATALOG on the catalog, USE SCHEMA on the schema and SELECT on the view.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — METASTORE -> TABLE -> VIEW — Why it is incorrect: the hierarchy goes through catalog and schema, not a table.
  • Option C — STORAGE CREDENTIAL -> EXTERNAL LOCATION -> VIEW — Why it is incorrect: credentials and external locations are not a view's path.
  • Option D — WORKSPACE -> CLUSTER -> VIEW — Why it is incorrect: workspace and cluster are not the securable hierarchy.

q224.stem:
A data engineer needs Task C to run ONLY if Task A succeeds AND Task B fails.

Which dependency configuration implements this conditional logic?
options: Task C depends on Task A (All done) and Task B (All done) with a condition widget.
Task C depends on Task A (Success) with Task B listed as a negative dependency.
Task C uses two dependency chains: Task A with All succeeded, Task B with at least one failed.
Create a Python task that checks dbutils.jobs.taskValues from Tasks A and B before running Task C.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Task C uses two dependency chains: Task A with All succeeded, Task B with at least one failed.

Why it is correct: combine Run if conditions per dependency: A with All succeeded and B with At least one failed.

⚠️ Heads-up: in Lakeflow Jobs Run if is evaluated over all of a task's dependencies; this question simplifies the real model. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Task C depends on Task A (All done) and Task B (All done) with a condition widget. — Why it is incorrect: All done runs regardless of A or B failing.
  • Option B — Task C depends on Task A (Success) with Task B listed as a negative dependency. — Why it is incorrect: "negative dependencies" do not exist.
  • Option D — Create a Python task that checks dbutils.jobs.taskValues from Tasks A and B before running Task C. — Why it is incorrect: an extra task is not the declarative way and does not replace Run if.

q225.stem:
A data engineer is preparing a Declarative Automation Bundle (formerly Databricks Asset Bundle) to deploy a Lakeflow pipeline.

To ensure the pipeline is deployed to the correct environment, where should the workspace-specific configurations, such as the host URL and root storage path, be defined within the bundle project?
options: In a global environment variable on the local development machine
Within the Python source code of the Lakeflow pipeline
In the targets section of the databricks.yml file
Inside the README.md file of the bundle root directory

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: In the targets section of the databricks.yml file

Why it is correct: the targets section of databricks.yml defines the workspace (host), paths and per-environment settings.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — In a global environment variable on the local development machine — Why it is incorrect: not reproducible or version-controlled.
  • Option B — Within the Python source code of the Lakeflow pipeline — Why it is incorrect: it mixes deployment configuration with code.
  • Option D — Inside the README.md file of the bundle root directory — Why it is incorrect: a README is not configuration.

q226.stem:
A data engineer needs to ingest JSON change data from Salesforce into Unity Catalog-governed Delta tables with a low- code, fully managed experience.

Which Databricks capability should the data engineer use?
options: A Lakeflow Connect managed Salesforce connector that writes into Unity Catalog Delta tables

Use the Salesforce REST API in a PySpark notebook to query changed records and write them to Delta
tables
Auto Loader reading JSON files from an S3 bucket exported by Salesforce
Auto Loader with a file arrival trigger on DBFS

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: A Lakeflow Connect managed Salesforce connector that writes into Unity Catalog Delta tables

Why it is correct: Lakeflow Connect offers a low-code managed Salesforce connector writing to Delta with Unity Catalog governance.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — … — Why it is incorrect: it needs custom code.
  • Option C — Auto Loader reading JSON files from an S3 bucket exported by Salesforce — Why it is incorrect: it depends on manual exports.
  • Option D — Auto Loader with a file arrival trigger on DBFS — Why it is incorrect: DBFS and file arrival do not ingest from Salesforce.

q227.stem:
A data engineer triggers a scheduled job but finds that the new run was not executed. The run history shows the run was skipped with a concurrency-related queue message.

Which configuration should the engineer investigate?
options: The SQL warehouse permissions for the task
The task-level timeout_seconds configuration
The job-level max_concurrent_runs setting and whether queueing is enabled
The cluster spot-instance availability in the cloud provider

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The job-level max_concurrent_runs setting and whether queueing is enabled

Why it is correct: max_concurrent_runs limits simultaneous runs and queueing decides whether they queue or are skipped.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The SQL warehouse permissions for the task — Why it is incorrect: permissions do not produce a concurrency message.
  • Option B — The task-level timeout_seconds configuration — Why it is incorrect: a timeout cancels long runs; it does not skip them due to queueing.
  • Option D — The cluster spot-instance availability in the cloud provider — Why it is incorrect: spot availability does not explain a concurrency skip.

q228.stem:
A pipeline uses COPY INTO to ingest CSV files from cloud object storage into a Unity Catalog Delta table. Some files are occasionally re-uploaded with corrections using the same filename.

The engineer needs the corrected data ingested as soon as it occurs. What should the engineer do?
options: Reload all files from the source path on each run
Load corrections as new files and apply updates to the target table
Recreate the target table before each run
Overwrite the target Delta table on each run

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Load corrections as new files and apply updates to the target table

Why it is correct: COPY INTO skips already loaded files with the same name; corrections must arrive as new files and be applied (e.g. with MERGE).

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Reload all files from the source path on each run — Why it is incorrect: it would duplicate already loaded data.
  • Option C — Recreate the target table before each run — Why it is incorrect: it destroys history and is costly.
  • Option D — Overwrite the target Delta table on each run — Why it is incorrect: overwriting everything is inefficient and loses history.

q229.stem:
A data engineer is running a Spark SQL job on Databricks and notices that joins between a small lookup table and a large fact table are slow. The data engineer wants Spark to automatically send the small lookup table to all executors to speed up the join.

Which configuration parameter should the data engineer adjust?
options: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
spark.executor.memory
spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold
spark.default.parallelism

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold

Why it is correct: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold sets the maximum table size Spark broadcasts automatically.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — spark.sql.shuffle.partitions — Why it is incorrect: it controls shuffle partitions, not broadcast.
  • Option B — spark.executor.memory — Why it is incorrect: executor memory, not broadcast.
  • Option D — spark.default.parallelism — Why it is incorrect: default RDD parallelism.

q230.stem:
A data engineer is joining a very large events_df (billions of rows) with a small country_lookup_df (fewer than 10,000 rows) on the country_code column. The join is slow due to data shuffling.

How should the data engineer improve performance?
options: Cache both DataFrames, then run the same join
Persist both DataFrames, then run the same join
broadcast events_df when performing the join
broadcast country_lookup_df when performing the join

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: broadcast country_lookup_df when performing the join

Why it is correct: broadcasting the small table avoids shuffling the large one.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Cache both DataFrames, then run the same join — Why it is incorrect: caching does not remove the shuffle.
  • Option B — Persist both DataFrames, then run the same join — Why it is incorrect: persisting does not remove the shuffle.
  • Option C — broadcast events_df when performing the join — Why it is incorrect: broadcasting the large table is infeasible.

q231.stem:
A data engineer runs df.toPandas() on a wide DataFrame containing 50 million rows. The notebook cell fails with a java.lang.OutOfMemoryError on the driver.

Which memory configuration is directly responsible for this failure?
options: spark.memory.fraction is too low, limiting the storage memory available for caching
spark.executor.memory is too low to process the DataFrame transformations
spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is set too high, causing excessive memory consumption during shuffles
spark.driver.memory is too low to hold the collected result set

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: spark.driver.memory is too low to hold the collected result set

Why it is correct: toPandas() pulls the whole result to the driver, so what is lacking is spark.driver.memory.

  • Official documentation: Compute configuration reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — spark.memory.fraction is too low, limiting the storage memory available for caching — Why it is incorrect: it affects executor caching.
  • Option B — spark.executor.memory is too low to process the DataFrame transformations — Why it is incorrect: the failure is on the driver, not executors.
  • Option C — spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is set too high, causing excessive memory consumption during shuffles — Why it is incorrect: it does not explain an OOM from collecting results.

q232.stem:
A data engineer investigates a slow stage in the Databricks Spark UI. The engineer scrolls down to the Summary Metrics section for task durations, and they observe for that stage: • 25th percentile duration: 40 seconds • Median duration: 45 seconds • 75th percentile duration: 50 seconds • Max duration: 80 seconds

What is the interpretation of these metrics?
options: There is a GC issue.
The stage likely suffers from data skew.
The stage is healthy.
The cluster is under-provisioned.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: The stage likely suffers from data skew.

Why it is correct: most tasks take 40–50 s but some reach 80 s: a skew signal, with a few tasks holding more data.

⚠️ Heads-up: the max (80 s) is only 1.6× the median: the skew is mild; the bank key is B. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — There is a GC issue. — Why it is incorrect: GC shows in the GC time column, not in this distribution.
  • Option C — The stage is healthy. — Why it is incorrect: there is a tail of slow tasks.
  • Option D — The cluster is under-provisioned. — Why it is incorrect: under-provisioning would affect all tasks alike.

q233.stem:
A data engineer uploads a CSV file using the "Create or modify a table using file upload" option in Databricks. To avoid incorrect schema inference, they disable Automatically detect column types before creating a Unity Catalog- managed table.

What is the outcome?
options: All columns are created with the STRING data type.
Numeric columns are inferred as numeric types; others are STRING.
Previously inferred column types are preserved.
Table creation fails because column types are not specified.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: All columns are created with the STRING data type.

Why it is correct: without automatic type detection, all columns are created as STRING.

  • Official documentation: Tables in Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Numeric columns are inferred as numeric types; others are STRING. — Why it is incorrect: that would be with detection enabled.
  • Option C — Previously inferred column types are preserved. — Why it is incorrect: there are no inferred types to keep.
  • Option D — Table creation fails because column types are not specified. — Why it is incorrect: it does not fail: it uses STRING.

q234.stem:
A data engineer has a bundle with a job resource keyed as etl_job in databricks.yml. After running 'databricks bundle deploy', the job appears in the workspace but has not executed.

Which command triggers execution of the deployed job?
options: databricks jobs submit --json
databricks bundle run etl_job
databricks bundle deploy --run
databricks bundle execute etl_job

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: databricks bundle run etl_job

Why it is correct: databricks bundle run etl_job triggers a bundle resource.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks jobs submit --json — Why it is incorrect: jobs submit sends a one-off run from JSON, not a bundle resource.
  • Option C — databricks bundle deploy --run — Why it is incorrect: deploy --run does not exist.
  • Option D — databricks bundle execute etl_job — Why it is incorrect: bundle execute does not exist.

q235.stem:
A data engineering team is building a new data transformation notebook. During development, they need fast testing, quick code changes, and easy debugging. Later, the notebook will run nightly as a scheduled job without human intervention. They want to optimize for development speed.

Which compute should they use during development?
options: Use instance pools.
Use classic job compute.
Use interactive compute.
Use SQL warehouses.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Use interactive compute.

Why it is correct: interactive (all-purpose) compute allows quick iteration and debugging.

  • Official documentation: Compute - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use instance pools. — Why it is incorrect: pools reduce start-up; they are not a development compute type by themselves.
  • Option B — Use classic job compute. — Why it is incorrect: a job cluster is created per run and is not interactive.
  • Option D — Use SQL warehouses. — Why it is incorrect: a SQL warehouse runs SQL, not a Python transformation notebook.

q236.stem:
A data engineer is designing a Gold layer table for a BI team that needs to query complex aggregations. The requirements state that the data should be precomputed to ensure low latency for dashboard users, but the underlying data changes only once every few hours.

Which object type should be implemented in Unity Catalog to meet these requirements?
options: Streaming table
External table
Materialized view
View

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Materialized view

Why it is correct: a materialized view precomputes and stores the result, refreshing when data changes.

  • Official documentation: Materialized views - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Streaming table — Why it is incorrect: a streaming table processes increments; it does not precompute complex aggregations.
  • Option B — External table — Why it is incorrect: an external table does not precompute.
  • Option D — View — Why it is incorrect: a view recomputes on every query.

q237.stem:
A data engineer is building a Silver layer pipeline that should only execute after the Bronze layer table has been successfully updated with new records.

Which trigger type in Databricks Jobs is specifically designed to orchestrate this dependency by reacting to changes in the upstream Unity Catalog table?
options: Table update trigger
File arrival trigger
Scheduled trigger
Continuous trigger

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Table update trigger

Why it is correct: the Table update trigger starts the job when a Unity Catalog table is updated.

  • Official documentation: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — File arrival trigger — Why it is incorrect: it reacts to new storage files, not tables.
  • Option C — Scheduled trigger — Why it is incorrect: it is clock-based, not table-change-based.
  • Option D — Continuous trigger — Why it is incorrect: it runs non-stop; it does not react to specific changes.

links.t: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers

q238.stem:
A data engineering team runs multiple daily batch jobs. The team needs to run the jobs on a fixed overnight schedule with consistent performance and controlled resource usage. The team wants to minimize operational overhead and reduce idle cluster costs.

Which compute option should the team use?
options: SQL warehouses
Classic all-purpose compute
Serverless jobs compute
Classic jobs compute

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Serverless jobs compute

Why it is correct: serverless jobs compute removes cluster management and leaves no idle resources.

⚠️ Heads-up: classic jobs compute also minimizes idle cost; the key prefers serverless for lower operational overhead. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Serverless compute - Databricks | Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SQL warehouses — Why it is incorrect: it is for SQL, not general batch jobs.
  • Option B — Classic all-purpose compute — Why it is incorrect: it idles and needs management.
  • Option D — Classic jobs compute — Why it is incorrect: it requires configuring and tuning clusters (more operational overhead).

q239.stem:
A Databricks Job with four sequential tasks is executed. The job failed at Task 3. After the root cause is fixed, the data engineer needs to complete the workflow without re-running the successful Tasks 1 and 2.

Which action in the Job Run details page allows the engineer to resume execution from the point of failure?
options: Repair run
Reset job
Clone task
Run now

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Repair run

Why it is correct: Repair run reruns only failed and pending tasks without repeating the successful ones.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Reset job — Why it is incorrect: it is not a resume action.
  • Option C — Clone task — Why it is incorrect: it copies a task; it does not resume.
  • Option D — Run now — Why it is incorrect: it starts a new full run.

q240.stem: Which single Databricks CLI command deploys local bundle assets to the target workspace specified in the configuration file?
options: databricks bundle init && databricks bundle deployment
databricks bundle plan && databricks bundle run
databricks bundle deploy
databricks bundle validate

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: databricks bundle deploy

Why it is correct: databricks bundle deploy deploys resources to the configured target.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks bundle init && databricks bundle deployment — Why it is incorrect: init creates a project; deployment does not deploy the bundle.
  • Option B — databricks bundle plan && databricks bundle run — Why it is incorrect: plan is not a deploy step and run executes.
  • Option D — databricks bundle validate — Why it is incorrect: validate only validates.

q241.stem:
A data engineer has two DataFrames: orders_df (all orders) and customers_df (only active customers). The data engineer needs to filter out orders placed by inactive customers.

Which operation should the data engineer use?
options: customers_df left join with orders_df
orders_df and customers_df inner join
orders_df and customers_df cross join
orders_df left join with customers_df

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: orders_df and customers_df inner join

Why it is correct: an inner join keeps only orders whose customer is in the active-customers list.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — customers_df left join with orders_df — Why it is incorrect: it keeps all customers; it does not filter orders.
  • Option C — orders_df and customers_df cross join — Why it is incorrect: a cross join yields the Cartesian product.
  • Option D — orders_df left join with customers_df — Why it is incorrect: it keeps all orders, including inactive customers' (with NULL).

q242.stem: Which Databricks SQL predicate correctly performs a null-safe equality comparison so that rows are matched when both sides are NULL or when both are equal non-NULL values?
options: WHERE customer_id <=> :cid
WHERE customer_id = :cid
WHERE COALESCE(customer_id, '') = COALESCE(:cid, '')
WHERE customer_id <> :cid OR customer_id IS NULL

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: WHERE customer_id <=> :cid

Why it is correct: the <=> operator is null-safe equality: true if both sides are NULL or equal.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — WHERE customer_id = :cid — Why it is incorrect: = returns NULL if either side is NULL.
  • Option C — WHERE COALESCE(customer_id, '') = COALESCE(:cid, '') — Why it is incorrect: COALESCE with an empty string conflates NULL with ''.
  • Option D — WHERE customer_id <> :cid OR customer_id IS NULL — Why it is incorrect: it expresses inequality, not equality.

q243.stem:
A data engineer needs to audit who made changes to a Delta table in the last 7 days.

Which SQL statement returns the record of past operations, including timestamps, users, and operation types?
options: DESCRIBE DETAIL my_table
DESCRIBE HISTORY my_table
SHOW TBLPROPERTIES my_table
SELECT * FROM 'delta.my_table/_delta_log/'

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: DESCRIBE HISTORY my_table

Why it is correct: DESCRIBE HISTORY lists versions, timestamp, user and operation.

  • Official documentation: Work with Delta table history (time travel) - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — DESCRIBE DETAIL my_table — Why it is incorrect: DESCRIBE DETAIL gives current metadata, not history.
  • Option C — SHOW TBLPROPERTIES my_table — Why it is incorrect: it shows properties, not operations.
  • Option D — SELECT * FROM 'delta.my_table/_delta_log/' — Why it is incorrect: reading the log by hand is not a supported statement like that.

links.t: Work with Delta table history (time travel)

q244.stem: A project contains targets dev and prod. Which CLI command deploys the bundle resources to the prod target?
options: databricks bundle run prod
databricks bundle validate -t prod
databricks bundle deploy -t prod
databricks workspace import prod

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: databricks bundle deploy -t prod

Why it is correct: bundle deploy -t prod deploys to the prod target.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks bundle run prod — Why it is incorrect: run runs a resource; it does not deploy.
  • Option B — databricks bundle validate -t prod — Why it is incorrect: it only validates.
  • Option D — databricks workspace import prod — Why it is incorrect: it imports notebooks, not bundles.

q245.stem: Before deploying changes, a CI pipeline must check the bundle configuration for errors without creating workspace resources. Which command is appropriate?
options: databricks bundle deploy -t prod
databricks bundle destroy -t prod
databricks bundle validate -t prod
databricks bundle run -t prod etl

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: databricks bundle validate -t prod

Why it is correct: bundle validate checks the configuration without creating resources.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks bundle deploy -t prod — Why it is incorrect: it creates resources.
  • Option B — databricks bundle destroy -t prod — Why it is incorrect: it removes resources.
  • Option D — databricks bundle run -t prod etl — Why it is incorrect: it runs a resource.

q246.stem:
A target specifies mode: development. With default behavior and no overrides, what happens to schedules/ triggers on deployed jobs?

targets:
  dev:
    mode: development
options: They are paused by default
They are forcibly deleted
They are automatically scheduled every minute
They are always enabled in all development workspaces

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: They are paused by default

Why it is correct: in mode: development schedules and triggers are paused by default.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — They are forcibly deleted — Why it is incorrect: they are not deleted.
  • Option C — They are automatically scheduled every minute — Why it is incorrect: no new schedules are created.
  • Option D — They are always enabled in all development workspaces — Why it is incorrect: they are paused.

q247.stem: The same bundle must deploy to dev and prod, with different catalog names and service endpoints but the same code. Which design is best?
options: Hardcode catalog=prod everywhere in notebooks
Use target-specific variables/overrides in the bundle configuration
Copy the project into two unrelated repositories
Rename all resources manually after deploying

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Use target-specific variables/overrides in the bundle configuration

Why it is correct: per-target variables and overrides keep a single codebase with different configuration.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Hardcode catalog=prod everywhere in notebooks — Why it is incorrect: it breaks dev.
  • Option C — Copy the project into two unrelated repositories — Why it is incorrect: it duplicates and desynchronizes.
  • Option D — Rename all resources manually after deploying — Why it is incorrect: manual and error-prone.

q248.stem:
Which top-level bundle resource mapping is appropriate for declaring a Lakeflow Job managed by a Declarative Automation Bundle?

resources:
  jobs:
    sales_etl:
      name: sales-etl
options: cloudFiles.schemaLocation
resources.jobs
resources.sql.only
workspace.git.pull_request

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: resources.jobs

Why it is correct: jobs are declared under resources.jobs.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — cloudFiles.schemaLocation — Why it is incorrect: it is an Auto Loader option.
  • Option C — resources.sql.only — Why it is incorrect: it does not exist.
  • Option D — workspace.git.pull_request — Why it is incorrect: it is not a resource mapping.

q249.stem: A target uses mode: production and specifies git.branch: main. A deployment runs from feature/change with no force override. What behavior should you expect?
options: Production mode ignores the branch constraint
The bundle automatically switches to dev mode
The CLI silently merges feature/change into main
The deployment is validated against the configured branch and can be rejected

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: The deployment is validated against the configured branch and can be rejected

Why it is correct: in production the configured branch is checked and the deployment can be rejected.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks | Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Production mode ignores the branch constraint — Why it is incorrect: the constraint applies.
  • Option B — The bundle automatically switches to dev mode — Why it is incorrect: it does not change mode.
  • Option C — The CLI silently merges feature/change into main — Why it is incorrect: the CLI does not merge branches.

q250.stem: A team uses Databricks Git folders and an external Git provider. Where is a pull request generally reviewed and merged?
options: In the external Git provider (for example GitHub)
Only inside a Databricks SQL warehouse
In a Delta table history log
In the Unity Catalog privilege editor

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: In the external Git provider (for example GitHub)

Why it is correct: pull requests are handled in the Git provider, not in Databricks.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Only inside a Databricks SQL warehouse — Why it is incorrect: a warehouse does not handle PRs.
  • Option C — In a Delta table history log — Why it is incorrect: Delta history is not Git.
  • Option D — In the Unity Catalog privilege editor — Why it is incorrect: it is for permissions.

q251.stem: An engineer modifies notebook code inside a Git folder, but wants to make the changes available to remote collaborators. Which sequence is most appropriate?
options: Run COPY INTO to create a Git commit
Change the SQL warehouse name to match the branch
Commit the local changes and push to the remote branch
Pull then delete the local branch

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Commit the local changes and push to the remote branch

Why it is correct: you commit and push to the remote branch.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Git folders - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Run COPY INTO to create a Git commit — Why it is incorrect: COPY INTO does not create commits.
  • Option B — Change the SQL warehouse name to match the branch — Why it is incorrect: irrelevant.
  • Option D — Pull then delete the local branch — Why it is incorrect: it discards the work.

q252.stem: A bundle has already been deployed to test. What CLI command executes its etl_job resource against the test target?
options: databricks bundle deploy -t prod etl_job
databricks bundle validate -t test etl_job
databricks bundle run -t test etl_job
databricks bundle destroy -t test etl_job

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: databricks bundle run -t test etl_job

Why it is correct: bundle run -t test etl_job runs the resource on test.

  • Official documentation: Databricks Asset Bundles - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — databricks bundle deploy -t prod etl_job — Why it is incorrect: it deploys to prod.
  • Option B — databricks bundle validate -t test etl_job — Why it is incorrect: it only validates.
  • Option D — databricks bundle destroy -t test etl_job — Why it is incorrect: it removes resources.

q253.stem:
A Delta target must load Parquet files with different source schemas and also add newly discovered columns to the target table. Which configuration covers both requirements?

COPY INTO main.bronze.events FROM '/Volumes/main/raw/landing/events' FILEFORMAT = PARQUET -- choose the options
options: FORMAT_OPTIONS ('inferSchema'='true') only
COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') only
FORMAT_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') and COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true')
FORMAT_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') only

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: FORMAT_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') and COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true')

Why it is correct: the reader's mergeSchema merges schemas across Parquet files and the one in COPY_OPTIONS lets the target table evolve.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — FORMAT_OPTIONS ('inferSchema'='true') only — Why it is incorrect: inferSchema does not evolve the target table.
  • Option B — COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') only — Why it is incorrect: it only evolves the target; it does not merge source schemas.
  • Option D — FORMAT_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') only — Why it is incorrect: it only merges schemas on read; it does not add columns to the target.

q254.stem: A JSON file was loaded yesterday with COPY INTO and then overwritten at the same path. The team explicitly wants to reprocess it, accepting possible duplicates. Which option disables file skipping?
options: FORMAT_OPTIONS ('force'='true')
VALIDATE ALL
COPY_OPTIONS ('force'='true')
COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true')

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: COPY_OPTIONS ('force'='true')

Why it is correct: COPY_OPTIONS ('force'='true') reloads files already registered in COPY INTO's history.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — FORMAT_OPTIONS ('force'='true') — Why it is incorrect: force is a copy option, not a format option.
  • Option B — VALIDATE ALL — Why it is incorrect: VALIDATE ALL only validates without inserting.
  • Option D — COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true') — Why it is incorrect: mergeSchema does not affect file skipping.

q255.stem: Before writing incoming files into an existing Delta table, an engineer needs to detect parse and target-constraint errors without inserting rows. Which clause is appropriate?
options: OVERWRITE
FORCE
PATTERN
VALIDATE ALL

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: VALIDATE ALL

Why it is correct: VALIDATE ALL validates the data that would be loaded without inserting it.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — OVERWRITE — Why it is incorrect: OVERWRITE overwrites data.
  • Option B — FORCE — Why it is incorrect: FORCE forces reloading.
  • Option C — PATTERN — Why it is incorrect: PATTERN filters paths.

q256.stem: A scheduled COPY INTO runs twice over the same path with identical files and default options. What happens on the second successful run?
options: The target table is replaced
The command errors because input files already exist
Files previously loaded are skipped
All rows are appended again

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Files previously loaded are skipped

Why it is correct: COPY INTO is idempotent by default and skips already loaded files.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The target table is replaced — Why it is incorrect: it does not replace the table.
  • Option B — The command errors because input files already exist — Why it is incorrect: it does not fail.
  • Option D — All rows are appended again — Why it is incorrect: it does not duplicate rows by default.

q257.stem:
An Auto Loader JSON stream must infer new columns but should treat customer_id as LONG. The team wants addNewColumns to continue working. Which technique is suitable?

.option('cloudFiles.schemaHints', 'customer_id LONG')
options: Use COPY_OPTIONS (mergeSchema=true) on the stream
Set cloudFiles.schemaHints to customer_id LONG
Specify a complete schema with .schema() and addNewColumns
Set schemaEvolutionMode to none

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Set cloudFiles.schemaHints to customer_id LONG

Why it is correct: cloudFiles.schemaHints sets a column type without disabling inference or addNewColumns.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use COPY_OPTIONS (mergeSchema=true) on the stream — Why it is incorrect: COPY_OPTIONS belongs to COPY INTO, not Auto Loader.
  • Option C — Specify a complete schema with .schema() and addNewColumns — Why it is incorrect: a full schema disables inference and evolution.
  • Option D — Set schemaEvolutionMode to none — Why it is incorrect: none disables evolution.

q258.stem: An Auto Loader JSON reader specifies a complete StructType schema and no schema evolution mode. A new JSON field appears. What is the default behavior?
options: The field is written into a new Delta table
The stream always fails and updates schemaLocation
The field is ignored unless explicit rescued-data handling is configured
The stream automatically appends the new field

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The field is ignored unless explicit rescued-data handling is configured

Why it is correct: with an explicit schema the default mode is none: the new field is ignored (unless rescued data is configured).

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The field is written into a new Delta table — Why it is incorrect: no other table is created.
  • Option B — The stream always fails and updates schemaLocation — Why it is incorrect: it does not fail by default.
  • Option D — The stream automatically appends the new field — Why it is incorrect: it is not added with an explicit schema.

q259.stem: A JSON Auto Loader stream without an explicit schema sees a new top-level field. Under default evolution, the stream raises UnknownFieldException. What is the intended recovery?
options: Configure failOnNewColumns and restart unchanged
Delete the existing target and checkpoint
Restart after the schema metadata has been updated
Switch from streaming to a SQL view

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Restart after the schema metadata has been updated

Why it is correct: with addNewColumns the stream fails once, updates the schema and restarts successfully.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Configure failOnNewColumns and restart unchanged — Why it is incorrect: failOnNewColumns would keep failing.
  • Option B — Delete the existing target and checkpoint — Why it is incorrect: destructive and unnecessary.
  • Option D — Switch from streaming to a SQL view — Why it is incorrect: it does not solve the schema change.

q260.stem: A JSON producer introduces unexpected fields frequently. The team wants to retain them for later inspection but not change the declared schema or stop on each new field. Which mode best fits?
options: failOnNewColumns
addNewColumnsWithTypeWidening
addNewColumns
rescue

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: rescue

Why it is correct: rescue stores unexpected fields in _rescued_data without changing the schema or failing.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — failOnNewColumns — Why it is incorrect: it fails on new columns.
  • Option B — addNewColumnsWithTypeWidening — Why it is incorrect: it modifies the schema.
  • Option C — addNewColumns — Why it is incorrect: it changes the schema and restarts the stream.

q261.stem: A stream uses schemaEvolutionMode=failOnNewColumns. A previously unseen column arrives. Which statement is true?
options: The stream silently stores the new field in the primary table schema
The stream automatically overwrites historical records
The stream fails and does not automatically add the new column to its schema
The stream never needs a schema update to resume

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The stream fails and does not automatically add the new column to its schema

Why it is correct: failOnNewColumns fails the stream and does not update the schema; you must update it manually.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — The stream silently stores the new field in the primary table schema — Why it is incorrect: it does not store the field.
  • Option B — The stream automatically overwrites historical records — Why it is incorrect: it does not touch historical records.
  • Option D — The stream never needs a schema update to resume — Why it is incorrect: it needs a schema update.

q262.stem: Millions of files arrive every day and scanning directories repeatedly is inefficient. What is the recommended scalable file discovery approach when available?
options: Rescan all folders from scratch on every run
Rely on alphabetical file ordering
Disable checkpoints to accelerate the stream
Use managed file events/notifications with Auto Loader

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Use managed file events/notifications with Auto Loader

Why it is correct: managed file events avoid directory listing and scale to millions of files.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Rescan all folders from scratch on every run — Why it is incorrect: that is exactly the inefficient approach.
  • Option B — Rely on alphabetical file ordering — Why it is incorrect: alphabetical order does not guarantee detecting new files.
  • Option C — Disable checkpoints to accelerate the stream — Why it is incorrect: without a checkpoint progress is lost.

q263.stem:
Which function allows an engineer to inspect the discovery/processing state of individual files tracked by an Auto Loader checkpoint?

SELECT * FROM cloud_files_state('/Volumes/ops/checkpoints/c1');
options: TABLE_CHANGES
CLOUD_FILES_STATE
READ_FILES
DESCRIBE HISTORY

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: CLOUD_FILES_STATE

Why it is correct: cloud_files_state(checkpoint_path) shows the state of each file in the checkpoint.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — TABLE_CHANGES — Why it is incorrect: TABLE_CHANGES relates to Change Data Feed.
  • Option C — READ_FILES — Why it is incorrect: READ_FILES reads files.
  • Option D — DESCRIBE HISTORY — Why it is incorrect: DESCRIBE HISTORY is for Delta tables.

q264.stem: Under default schema inference for ordinary JSON files (without inferColumnTypes=true), which data type is assigned to discovered user fields?
options: VARIANT for every JSON column automatically
STRING
INT for all numeric fields
BOOLEAN whenever values include true/false

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: STRING

Why it is correct: by default Auto Loader infers JSON columns as STRING.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — VARIANT for every JSON column automatically — Why it is incorrect: VARIANT is not assigned automatically.
  • Option C — INT for all numeric fields — Why it is incorrect: numeric types are not inferred without inferColumnTypes.
  • Option D — BOOLEAN whenever values include true/false — Why it is incorrect: BOOLEAN is not inferred either.

q265.stem: A supported SaaS platform requires credential management and incremental synchronization into Unity Catalog with minimal custom code. Which method best aligns with that requirement?
options: A hand-built REST poller in a scheduled notebook
A supported managed connector in Lakeflow Connect
A regular SELECT directly from a JSON file
A Spark UDF for API authentication

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A supported managed connector in Lakeflow Connect

Why it is correct: a Lakeflow Connect managed connector handles credentials, incremental sync and governance.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A hand-built REST poller in a scheduled notebook — Why it is incorrect: it requires custom code.
  • Option C — A regular SELECT directly from a JSON file — Why it is incorrect: it does not sync incrementally.
  • Option D — A Spark UDF for API authentication — Why it is incorrect: a UDF is not an ingestion mechanism.

q266.stem: A source is a supported SharePoint file repository. The team wants managed file ingestion with authentication, retries, and destination tables without custom Spark source code. What is the best fit?
options: JDBC read on the SharePoint URL
The Azure Event Hubs standard connector
A Kafka SQL warehouse
Lakeflow Connect managed file connector

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Lakeflow Connect managed file connector

Why it is correct: the Lakeflow Connect managed file connector covers SharePoint with authentication and retries.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — JDBC read on the SharePoint URL — Why it is incorrect: JDBC does not read SharePoint.
  • Option B — The Azure Event Hubs standard connector — Why it is incorrect: Event Hubs is for events, not files.
  • Option C — A Kafka SQL warehouse — Why it is incorrect: there is no "Kafka SQL warehouse".

q267.stem: A managed file connector is configured for a supported document repository. Which object stores source authentication details as a governed Unity Catalog securable?
options: CheckpointLocation
Connection
SQL warehouse query history
Pipeline event log

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Connection

Why it is correct: a Unity Catalog Connection stores source credentials as a governed securable.

  • Official documentation: What is Unity Catalog? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — CheckpointLocation — Why it is incorrect: it stores progress, not credentials.
  • Option C — SQL warehouse query history — Why it is incorrect: it is history.
  • Option D — Pipeline event log — Why it is incorrect: it is an event log.

q268.stem: In a standard gateway-based database CDC connector, the source must be captured continuously while target ingestion pipelines run periodically. Which statement describes the architecture?
options: Auto Loader is required to connect directly to the DB log
There can be no intermediate staging location
The gateway captures changes into staging; scheduled pipelines apply them to target tables
Every BI query must trigger an entire source snapshot

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: The gateway captures changes into staging; scheduled pipelines apply them to target tables

Why it is correct: the gateway continuously captures changes into staging and scheduled pipelines apply them to the target.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Auto Loader is required to connect directly to the DB log — Why it is incorrect: Auto Loader does not read DB logs.
  • Option B — There can be no intermediate staging location — Why it is incorrect: there is staging.
  • Option D — Every BI query must trigger an entire source snapshot — Why it is incorrect: no snapshot is taken per query.

q269.stem:
A source directory contains many file types, but only files matching sales_*.csv should be ingested by COPY INTO. Which clause filters source file paths?

COPY INTO bronze.sales FROM '/Volumes/raw/landing/' FILEFORMAT = CSV PATTERN = 'sales_*.csv';
options: TIMESTAMP AS OF
VALIDATE
PATTERN
COLUMNS

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: PATTERN

Why it is correct: PATTERN filters source files by glob pattern.

  • Official documentation: Load data using COPY INTO - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — TIMESTAMP AS OF — Why it is incorrect: TIMESTAMP AS OF is for time travel.
  • Option B — VALIDATE — Why it is incorrect: VALIDATE validates without inserting.
  • Option D — COLUMNS — Why it is incorrect: COLUMNS does not filter files.

q270.stem: A source generates JSON files every few minutes into cloud storage. The pipeline should pick up new files incrementally with checkpoints and schema evolution. What is the most natural first choice?
options: A SQL warehouse on top of a Python list
Manual full directory overwrite
Auto Loader on cloudFiles
A JDBC connector against object storage

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Auto Loader on cloudFiles

Why it is correct: Auto Loader (cloudFiles) ingests new files incrementally with checkpoints and schema evolution.

  • Official documentation: What is Auto Loader? - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A SQL warehouse on top of a Python list — Why it is incorrect: not an ingestion mechanism.
  • Option B — Manual full directory overwrite — Why it is incorrect: manual and costly.
  • Option D — A JDBC connector against object storage — Why it is incorrect: JDBC does not read object storage.

q271.stem: An internal REST API has no compatible managed connector and requires a custom OAuth flow and payload transformation. What is a reasonable ingestion pattern?
options: COPY INTO FROM an HTTP JSON response directly
Use Unity Catalog row filters to fetch records
A custom notebook/SDK REST client orchestrated by Lakeflow Jobs, writing governed tables
Force AUTO CDC to call arbitrary APIs without an adapter

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: A custom notebook/SDK REST client orchestrated by Lakeflow Jobs, writing governed tables

Why it is correct: without a connector, a custom REST client orchestrated by Jobs that writes governed tables is the reasonable choice.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — COPY INTO FROM an HTTP JSON response directly — Why it is incorrect: COPY INTO does not read HTTP responses.
  • Option B — Use Unity Catalog row filters to fetch records — Why it is incorrect: row filters protect data; they do not extract it.
  • Option D — Force AUTO CDC to call arbitrary APIs without an adapter — Why it is incorrect: AUTO CDC does not call APIs.

q272.stem:
A data engineer must extract rows from an external RDBMS not covered by managed connectors, transform them, and land them in Delta. Which API is suitable for source extraction?

df = spark.read.format('jdbc').option('url', jdbc_url).option('dbtable', 'dbo.orders').load()
options: spark.read.format("jdbc") with URL and credentials
spark.read.format("cloudFiles") for a database socket
MERGE INTO with a JDBC URL as target table
COPY INTO FROM JDBC as a native SQL source clause

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: spark.read.format("jdbc") with URL and credentials

Why it is correct: the Spark JDBC reader extracts rows from an RDBMS.

  • Official documentation: Query databases using JDBC - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — spark.read.format("cloudFiles") for a database socket — Why it is incorrect: cloudFiles reads files.
  • Option C — MERGE INTO with a JDBC URL as target table — Why it is incorrect: MERGE does not take a JDBC URL as target.
  • Option D — COPY INTO FROM JDBC as a native SQL source clause — Why it is incorrect: COPY INTO does not support JDBC.

q273.stem: In a job, tasks ingest_A and ingest_B may run in parallel. build_gold must start only when both have succeeded. How should build_gold be configured?
options: Use At least one succeeded with a dependency on ingest_A only
Depend only on ingest_A
Depend on ingest_A and ingest_B with All succeeded
Set the three tasks to execute at the same time

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Depend on ingest_A and ingest_B with All succeeded

Why it is correct: All succeeded with both dependencies requires both to finish successfully.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use At least one succeeded with a dependency on ingest_A only — Why it is incorrect: one is enough and it does not wait for ingest_B.
  • Option B — Depend only on ingest_A — Why it is incorrect: it ignores ingest_B.
  • Option D — Set the three tasks to execute at the same time — Why it is incorrect: without dependencies there is no ordering.

q274.stem: A cleanup task must run after upstream tasks finish regardless of whether they succeeded or failed (assuming their states allow the condition). Which Run if choice is intended?
options: All done
None failed
At least one succeeded
All succeeded

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: All done

Why it is correct: All done runs once all dependencies have completed, successful or not.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — None failed — Why it is incorrect: requires none to fail.
  • Option C — At least one succeeded — Why it is incorrect: requires at least one success.
  • Option D — All succeeded — Why it is incorrect: requires all to succeed.

q275.stem: An upstream task emits a row_count task value. Gold processing should run only when row_count > 0. Which Lakeflow task supports this branch?
options: Run Job task
For each task
If/else condition task
SQL warehouse refresh interval

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: If/else condition task

Why it is correct: the If/else condition task evaluates a condition on task values and branches.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Run Job task — Why it is incorrect: it launches another job.
  • Option B — For each task — Why it is incorrect: it iterates over a list.
  • Option D — SQL warehouse refresh interval — Why it is incorrect: it is not a control-flow task.

q276.stem: A parameterized notebook must execute once for each region in a dynamically computed array ["ES","PT","FR"]. Which control-flow task is designed for this?
options: For each
If/else
File arrival trigger
Run Job

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: For each

Why it is correct: For each iterates a task over the items of a list.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — If/else — Why it is incorrect: it only branches.
  • Option C — File arrival trigger — Why it is incorrect: it is a trigger, not a task.
  • Option D — Run Job — Why it is incorrect: it invokes a job; it does not iterate.

q277.stem: A downstream team has an independently managed Lakeflow Job that must be invoked as one step of a larger orchestration. Which task type should the parent job add?
options: For each with no child task
Dashboard refresh task
Run Job task
Notebook task with copied source

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Run Job task

Why it is correct: the Run Job task invokes another existing job as a step.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — For each with no child task — Why it is incorrect: it does not invoke another job.
  • Option B — Dashboard refresh task — Why it is incorrect: it refreshes dashboards.
  • Option D — Notebook task with copied source — Why it is incorrect: copying code duplicates and desynchronizes.

q278.stem: Task A succeeded, task B failed, and downstream task C was skipped. Which feature recovers the failed run while avoiding unnecessary reruns of A?
options: Delete all run history
Full re-deploy of the workspace
Drop and recreate Unity Catalog tables
Repair run

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Repair run

Why it is correct: Repair run reruns only the failed and dependent tasks.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Jobs - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Delete all run history — Why it is incorrect: it recovers nothing.
  • Option B — Full re-deploy of the workspace — Why it is incorrect: excessive.
  • Option C — Drop and recreate Unity Catalog tables — Why it is incorrect: destructive and unnecessary.

q279.stem: Gold should run when a specific supported Unity Catalog source table is updated, without polling on a fixed schedule. Which trigger matches this requirement?
options: Manual Run now
Table update trigger
Scheduled trigger
File arrival trigger

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Table update trigger

Why it is correct: the table update trigger launches the job when the source table changes.

  • Official documentation: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Manual Run now — Why it is incorrect: it is manual.
  • Option C — Scheduled trigger — Why it is incorrect: it polls on a schedule.
  • Option D — File arrival trigger — Why it is incorrect: it reacts to files, not tables.

links.t: Automating jobs with schedules and triggers

q280.stem: A pipeline should start when files arrive in a monitored Unity Catalog storage location rather than at a particular time. Which trigger type is intended?
options: File arrival
Scheduled
Continuous
Table update

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: File arrival

Why it is correct: File arrival launches the job when new files arrive.

q281.stem: A team sets a Lakeflow Job to Continuous. Which description best matches how that job is scheduled?

q282.stem: A scheduled job sometimes overlaps its previous execution. By default, what prevents simultaneous runs from exceeding the job concurrency limit?

q283.stem: A Lakeflow Job consists of a SQL query task and a Python notebook task. Which allocation is generally appropriate?

q285.stem: An API occasionally returns a transient 503 causing one notebook task to fail. Which Lakeflow Job setting is intended to retry that task automatically?

q286.stem: A downstream task may proceed if EITHER of two upstream independent validation tasks succeeds. Which Run if condition captures this?

q287.stem: A Spark stage has 150 tasks. The median task runs 5 seconds, but one runs 12 minutes and reads 45 times more shuffle data. Which cause is most likely?

q288.stem: Spark UI shows high disk spill across join and aggregation tasks. What is the most direct interpretation?

q289.stem: A complex SQL statement would benefit from a different join order. An engineer assumes AQE will reorder all joins dynamically. Which statement is accurate?
options: AQE only applies to Git workflows

q290.stem: A skewed shuffle-based LEFT OUTER JOIN is executed with AQE. Which join side can AQE split for supported skew handling?

q291.stem: A scheduled pipeline historically takes 8 minutes, but the last 10 runs take 30 minutes. Where should an engineer first compare timings and isolate slow tasks?

q292.stem: Frequent microbatch writes have created hundreds of thousands of tiny Delta files, slowing scans. Which operation most directly compacts files?

q293.stem: An engineer enables Liquid Clustering on a Delta table to improve common selective queries. What should they avoid configuring together with it?

q295.stem: A notebook fails when a developer calls df.collect() on a 100 GB DataFrame. Executor task stages had previously completed. What is the most plausible immediate cause?

q296.stem: A reporting team runs ad-hoc SQL dashboards over Delta tables. Low cold-start latency and managed scaling are more important than custom Spark JVM settings. Which compute should they choose?

q300.stem: An engineer must explain why Delta tables can support atomic updates and historical version queries over cloud object storage. What is the essential mechanism?

q302.stem:

q305.stem: An ABAC mask policy defines MATCH COLUMNS has_tag_value("pii","email") AS e. Which clause identifies the column whose value is passed automatically as the first UDF argument?

q308.stem: An older example uses hasTagValue("pii", "ssn"). What is the preferred modern spelling for new policies?

q310.stem: What does granting BROWSE on a Unity Catalog catalog provide?
