  • Option B — RESTORE TABLE TO VERSION AS OF 0 — Why it is incorrect: it restores versions.
  • Option D — DROP TABLE then CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME — Why it is incorrect: destructive and not equivalent.

q314.stem: A policy should hide sales rows outside a user region, but still show the same columns for permitted rows. Which control is appropriate?
options: Liquid Clustering by region
Column mask only
COPY INTO with VALIDATE
ROW FILTER backed by a boolean UDF

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: ROW FILTER backed by a boolean UDF

Why it is correct: a row filter with a boolean UDF hides rows per user.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Liquid Clustering by region — Why it is incorrect: it is a physical layout.
  • Option B — Column mask only — Why it is incorrect: it hides values, not rows.
  • Option C — COPY INTO with VALIDATE — Why it is incorrect: it is for ingestion.

q315.stem: An ABAC policy should apply to all account users except members of compliance_admins. Which clause pattern implements principal targeting and exclusion?
options: USING COLUMNS (compliance_admins)
MATCH COLUMNS session_user() AS principal
TO account users EXCEPT compliance_admins
WHEN NOT has_tag("compliance_admins")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: TO account users EXCEPT compliance_admins

Why it is correct: TO ... EXCEPT ... defines affected and excluded principals.

  • Official documentation: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — USING COLUMNS (compliance_admins) — Why it is incorrect: it passes columns to the UDF.
  • Option B — MATCH COLUMNS session_user() AS principal — Why it is incorrect: MATCH COLUMNS selects columns.
  • Option D — WHEN NOT has_tag("compliance_admins") — Why it is incorrect: WHEN evaluates tags, not principals.

q316.stem: An engineer wants customer records that have no matching row in an orders DataFrame. Which PySpark join type directly returns these unmatched left-side records?
options: cross
left_anti
left_semi
left_outer

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: left_anti

Why it is correct: left_anti returns left rows with no match on the right.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — cross — Why it is incorrect: cross is a Cartesian product.
  • Option C — left_semi — Why it is incorrect: left_semi returns those that do match.
  • Option D — left_outer — Why it is incorrect: left_outer returns all left rows, not only unmatched ones.

q317.stem: A team needs the distinct set of orders that have a matching payment record, but none of the payment columns should appear in the result. Which join type is most direct?
options: full_outer
left_semi
left_anti
cross

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: left_semi

Why it is correct: left_semi returns left rows with a match, without right-side columns.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — full_outer — Why it is incorrect: full_outer brings columns from both.
  • Option C — left_anti — Why it is incorrect: left_anti returns non-matching rows.
  • Option D — cross — Why it is incorrect: cross is a Cartesian product.

q318.stem:
A 200 GB events DataFrame is joined to an 8 MB lookup dimension on product_id. Which PySpark construct explicitly suggests broadcasting the dimension?

from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
result = events.join(broadcast(dim), 'product_id')
options: events.crossJoin(dim)
dim.collect() followed by Python dictionary filtering
events.repartition(1).join(dim)
events.join(broadcast(dim), "product_id")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: events.join(broadcast(dim), "product_id")

Why it is correct: broadcast(dim) sends the small dimension to all executors and avoids the shuffle.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — events.crossJoin(dim) — Why it is incorrect: crossJoin creates a Cartesian product.
  • Option B — dim.collect() followed by Python dictionary filtering — Why it is incorrect: collect() pulls everything to the driver and breaks distributed execution.
  • Option C — events.repartition(1).join(dim) — Why it is incorrect: repartition(1) concentrates everything in one partition.

q319.stem: Two DataFrames have identical column names but different column positions. They must append rows aligning fields by name. Which operation should be used?
options: df1.intersect(df2)
df1.join(df2)
df1.union(df2)
df1.unionByName(df2)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: df1.unionByName(df2)

Why it is correct: unionByName aligns columns by name.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — df1.intersect(df2) — Why it is incorrect: intersect returns common rows.
  • Option B — df1.join(df2) — Why it is incorrect: join combines columns; it does not stack rows.
  • Option C — df1.union(df2) — Why it is incorrect: union aligns by position.

q320.stem: An engineer performs df1.union(df2) in PySpark and must eliminate duplicate resulting rows. Which statement is correct?
options: unionByName also always removes duplicate rows
union appends rows by position; distinct() can remove duplicate rows afterward
union removes duplicates automatically, as SQL UNION
A join must replace union because no deduplication is possible

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: union appends rows by position; distinct() can remove duplicate rows afterward

Why it is correct: in PySpark union is like UNION ALL (no dedup) and you use distinct() afterwards.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — unionByName also always removes duplicate rows — Why it is incorrect: it does not dedup either.
  • Option C — union removes duplicates automatically, as SQL UNION — Why it is incorrect: it does not dedup automatically.
  • Option D — A join must replace union because no deduplication is possible — Why it is incorrect: deduplication is possible.

q321.stem: A column items contains ["A","B"] and another contains ["C"]. The target requires one row per array item with the other row columns retained. Which expression does this?
options: array_distinct(items)
concat(items)
collect_list(items)
explode(items)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: explode(items)

Why it is correct: explode(items) produces one row per array element.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — array_distinct(items) — Why it is incorrect: array_distinct removes duplicates within the array.
  • Option B — concat(items) — Why it is incorrect: concat joins arrays.
  • Option C — collect_list(items) — Why it is incorrect: collect_list aggregates rows into an array (the opposite).

q322.stem: A source column region_codes contains a pipe-separated STRING such as "ES|PT|FR". Which PySpark function returns an array of individual codes?
options: countDistinct(col("region_codes"))
explode(col("region_codes"))
unionByName(col("region_codes"))
split(col("region_codes"), "\|")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: split(col("region_codes"), "\|")

Why it is correct: split(col, "\|") splits the string into an array of codes.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — countDistinct(col("region_codes")) — Why it is incorrect: countDistinct counts values.
  • Option B — explode(col("region_codes")) — Why it is incorrect: explode expects an array or map, not a string.
  • Option C — unionByName(col("region_codes")) — Why it is incorrect: unionByName is for DataFrames.

q323.stem: What does SELECT try_cast("not_a_number" AS INT) return when the source and target types support TRY_CAST?
options: A parsing exception
NULL
The string unchanged

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: NULL

Why it is correct: TRY_CAST returns NULL when the conversion fails instead of raising an error.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — A parsing exception — Why it is incorrect: that is what CAST does (in ANSI mode).
  • Option B — 0 — Why it is incorrect: it does not return 0.
  • Option D — The string unchanged — Why it is incorrect: it does not return the string.

q324.stem:
Each invoice can have multiple line items. A Gold daily_revenue table needs sum(amount) and number of distinct invoice_ids per date. Which pair of aggregations is correct?

df.groupBy('invoice_date').agg(
    F.sum('amount').alias('total'),
    F.countDistinct('invoice_id').alias('invoices')
)
options: sum(amount) and countDistinct(invoice_id)
sum(invoice_id) and count(amount)
count(amount) and approx_count_distinct(customer_id)
avg(amount) and count(customer_id)

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: sum(amount) and countDistinct(invoice_id)

Why it is correct: the total is sum(amount) and distinct invoices are counted with countDistinct(invoice_id).

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — sum(invoice_id) and count(amount) — Why it is incorrect: summing identifiers makes no sense.
  • Option C — count(amount) and approx_count_distinct(customer_id) — Why it is incorrect: it uses customer_id and an approximate count, not the requested one.
  • Option D — avg(amount) and count(customer_id) — Why it is incorrect: it computes an average and counts customers, not what is asked.

q325.stem: A Silver ingestion should remove rows where order_id is NULL while preserving rows whose optional description is NULL. Which filter is most appropriate?
options: df.distinct()
df.fillna({"order_id": 0})
df.filter(F.col("order_id").isNotNull())
df.na.drop() with no subset

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: df.filter(F.col("order_id").isNotNull())

Why it is correct: filter(col("order_id").isNotNull()) removes only rows without order_id.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — df.distinct() — Why it is incorrect: distinct() does not filter nulls.
  • Option B — df.fillna({"order_id": 0}) — Why it is incorrect: fillna would invent an id 0.
  • Option D — df.na.drop() with no subset — Why it is incorrect: na.drop() with no subset would also drop rows with a NULL description.

q326.stem: A dataset is duplicated according to business keys (order_id, line_number), but different loads may contain different ingestion timestamps. Which operation directly removes duplicates based on those keys?
options: distinct(["order_id", "line_number"])
groupBy().collect()
dropDuplicates(["order_id", "line_number"])
drop("ingestion_timestamp")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: dropDuplicates(["order_id", "line_number"])

Why it is correct: dropDuplicates([keys]) deduplicates by those columns.

  • Official documentation: PySpark on Databricks - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — distinct(["order_id", "line_number"]) — Why it is incorrect: distinct() does not take a column list.
  • Option B — groupBy().collect() — Why it is incorrect: groupBy().collect() does not deduplicate.
  • Option D — drop("ingestion_timestamp") — Why it is incorrect: drop removes a column, not rows.

q327.stem: Bronze stores amounts as strings, sometimes malformed. Silver must parse valid numerics but keep malformed rows for a separate quality review. Which expression avoids aborting on invalid numeric text?
options: TRY_CAST(amount AS DOUBLE)
COUNT(DISTINCT amount)
CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) in every configuration
DELETE every row where amount is STRING

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: TRY_CAST(amount AS DOUBLE)

Why it is correct: TRY_CAST returns NULL for an invalid value without aborting, letting you review those rows.

  • Official documentation: SQL language reference - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — COUNT(DISTINCT amount) — Why it is incorrect: COUNT(DISTINCT) does not convert.
  • Option C — CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) in every configuration — Why it is incorrect: CAST can fail with invalid text.
  • Option D — DELETE every row where amount is STRING — Why it is incorrect: deleting rows loses data for review.

q328.stem: Gold joins current customer attributes with sales aggregations; corrections to historical customer rows must be reflected on refresh. Which object best fits by default?
options: An append-only streaming table ignoring old updates
A materialized view
A CSV file written once
A temporary SQL view persisted as Delta without materialization

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: A materialized view

Why it is correct: a materialized view recomputes/updates its result reflecting source changes, including historical corrections.

  • Official documentation: Materialized views - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — An append-only streaming table ignoring old updates — Why it is incorrect: a streaming table ignores changes to old rows.
  • Option C — A CSV file written once — Why it is incorrect: a static CSV does not refresh.
  • Option D — A temporary SQL view persisted as Delta without materialization — Why it is incorrect: without materialization there is no managed refresh.

q329.stem: A pipeline materialized view has a complex query that is not eligible for incremental refresh. What can Databricks do to maintain its result?
options: It can perform a full recomputation on refresh
It permanently disables the materialized view
It silently omits all modified rows
It must turn automatically into an append-only streaming table

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: It can perform a full recomputation on refresh

Why it is correct: if it cannot be incremental, Databricks fully recomputes the view on refresh.

  • Official documentation: Materialized views - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — It permanently disables the materialized view — Why it is incorrect: it is not disabled.
  • Option C — It silently omits all modified rows — Why it is incorrect: it does not omit changes.
  • Option D — It must turn automatically into an append-only streaming table — Why it is incorrect: its type does not change.

q330.stem:
In Python Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, which decorator declares a materialized view?

from pyspark import pipelines as dp

@dp.materialized_view
def sales_gold():
    return spark.read.table('sales_silver')
options: @dp.stream
@dp.managed_delta
@dp.table
@dp.materialized_view

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: @dp.materialized_view

Why it is correct: @dp.materialized_view declares a materialized view.

  • Official documentation: Materialized views - Databricks | Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — @dp.stream — Why it is incorrect: @dp.stream does not exist.
  • Option B — @dp.managed_delta — Why it is incorrect: @dp.managed_delta does not exist.
  • Option C — @dp.table — Why it is incorrect: @dp.table declares a streaming table.

q331.stem: A pipeline must stop the affected flow if amount <= 0, rather than drop rows and continue. Which expectation API expresses this?
options: dp.expect_or_drop("valid", "amount > 0")
dp.ignore_invalid("valid")
dp.expect_or_fail("valid", "amount > 0")
dp.expect("valid", "amount > 0")

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: dp.expect_or_fail("valid", "amount > 0")

Why it is correct: dp.expect_or_fail fails the update when the rule is violated.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — dp.expect_or_drop("valid", "amount > 0") — Why it is incorrect: expect_or_drop drops rows and continues.
  • Option B — dp.ignore_invalid("valid") — Why it is incorrect: ignore_invalid does not exist.
  • Option D — dp.expect("valid", "amount > 0") — Why it is incorrect: expect only records metrics and keeps the rows.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q332.stem: A streaming transformation should record how many records violate a rule but keep those records for later investigation. Which expectation behavior is appropriate?
options: VACUUM invalid records
WARN / @dp.expect
FAIL UPDATE / @dp.expect_or_fail
DROP ROW / @dp.expect_or_drop

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: WARN / @dp.expect

Why it is correct: WARN (@dp.expect) records violation metrics and keeps the rows.

  • Official documentation: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — VACUUM invalid records — Why it is incorrect: VACUUM is not an expectation.
  • Option C — FAIL UPDATE / @dp.expect_or_fail — Why it is incorrect: it stops the update.
  • Option D — DROP ROW / @dp.expect_or_drop — Why it is incorrect: it drops the rows.

links.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

q333.stem:
Out-of-order customer CDC events must produce complete history with validity intervals. Which AUTO CDC configuration is necessary?

CREATE FLOW cdc AS AUTO CDC INTO customers_hist FROM stream(bronze.customers_cdc) KEYS (customer_id) SEQUENCE BY change_seq STORED AS SCD TYPE 2;
options: APPEND all rows and use DISTINCT
SEQUENCE BY current_timestamp(), STORED AS SCD TYPE 1
GROUP BY customer_id, MAX(event_time), no CDC flow
KEYS(customer_id), SEQUENCE BY event_time, STORED AS SCD TYPE 2

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: KEYS(customer_id), SEQUENCE BY event_time, STORED AS SCD TYPE 2

Why it is correct: KEYS + SEQUENCE BY event_time + SCD TYPE 2 orders events and keeps history with validity intervals.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — APPEND all rows and use DISTINCT — Why it is incorrect: append + distinct handles neither ordering nor validity.
  • Option B — SEQUENCE BY current_timestamp(), STORED AS SCD TYPE 1 — Why it is incorrect: current_timestamp() does not reflect source order and SCD1 keeps no history.
  • Option C — GROUP BY customer_id, MAX(event_time), no CDC flow — Why it is incorrect: without a CDC flow there is no history.

q334.stem:
Several CDC events share the same timestamp. The source also has a strictly ordered event_id to break ties. How should an AUTO CDC sequence be expressed?

SEQUENCE BY STRUCT(event_time, event_id)
options: SEQUENCE BY CONCAT(event_time, event_id) interpreted arbitrarily
SEQUENCE BY STRUCT(event_time, event_id)
SEQUENCE BY user_name
SEQUENCE BY RAND()

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: SEQUENCE BY STRUCT(event_time, event_id)

Why it is correct: SEQUENCE BY STRUCT(event_time, event_id) orders by timestamp and breaks ties with event_id.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — SEQUENCE BY CONCAT(event_time, event_id) interpreted arbitrarily — Why it is incorrect: concatenation would be interpreted arbitrarily.
  • Option C — SEQUENCE BY user_name — Why it is incorrect: user_name does not order events.
  • Option D — SEQUENCE BY RAND() — Why it is incorrect: RAND() is random.

q335.stem: Incoming CDC updates contain NULL for attributes not changed. The team wants to retain the existing values rather than overwrite them with NULL. Which AUTO CDC clause addresses this?
options: APPLY AS TRUNCATE WHEN
IGNORE NULL UPDATES
DELETE FROM on every update
STORED AS SCD TYPE 2 only

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: IGNORE NULL UPDATES

Why it is correct: IGNORE NULL UPDATES ignores NULLs in updates and keeps existing values.

  • Official documentation: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines - Databricks
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — APPLY AS TRUNCATE WHEN — Why it is incorrect: APPLY AS TRUNCATE WHEN truncates the table.
  • Option C — DELETE FROM on every update — Why it is incorrect: it deletes rows on every update.
  • Option D — STORED AS SCD TYPE 2 only — Why it is incorrect: SCD2 keeps history but does not prevent NULL overwrites.
